Chapter Four: The Section on the Jewel Banner, Part Nine: The Chapter on Samādhi and the Supernormal Power of the Feet.
At that time, the four great disciples of the Tathāgata, together with the sons of Māra, wandered through the city of Rājagṛha, performing songs, dances, and verses.
At that time, the great earth shook in six ways, and immeasurable devas and humans wept with sorrowful hearts, crying out: "Alas! Alas!"
"Now that the Tathāgata still remains in the world, our four disciples have been made a mere sport for the hosts of Māras.
Thereupon, they gathered together and went to where the Buddha was, saying these words:
"World-Honored One!"
I only pray that the Tathāgata will relinquish his mind of equanimity. Why is this?
All the māras desire to destroy the Buddha-dharma.
The Buddha said:
"I shall now enter the great city of Rājagṛha to transform sentient beings, to destroy the works of Māra, and to manifest great supernormal powers in performing the buddha-work."
At that time, the Buddha wished to enter the city of Rājagṛha.
Then the assembly of devas wailed toward the Buddha and spoke these words:
“It is truly not the right time for the Buddha to enter the city now.”

Why is this? Because immeasurable evil spirits fill the void, and immeasurable hosts of Māras hold swords and great stones; if the Buddha enters the city, the Tathāgata’s lamp of Dharma will soon be extinguished.
At that time, the Tathāgata remained silent and did not grant permission.
Again, another deva said:
“World-Honored One!
"In the city of Rājagṛha, five hundred sons of Māra are brandishing swords and halberds, wishing to harm the Tathāgata.
Then another deva wept and said,
"Now this Śākya clan shall soon be destroyed."
Again, another deva said:
"The unsurpassed Dharma-ship is now about to disperse and perish; among the sentient beings of the triple world, who shall ferry them across to reach the other shore?
Still another deva said:
"All sentient beings are constantly entangled by afflictions; if the Unsurpassed Great Teacher were to pass into extinction, who would enable them to attain liberation?"
Again, another deity said:
“World-Honored One!
Do you not see the immeasurable hosts of Māras in the air, wishing to rain down swords, great stones, and fierce fires?”
"We only pray that the Tathāgata, out of compassion for sentient beings, will not yet enter the city.
Furthermore, another deva said:
"World-Honored One!..."
Within the city of Rājagṛha, there were twenty thousand Māras, each manifesting in the guise of a brāhmaṇa, wielding swords and blades with the intent to harm the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, twenty thousand held spears awaiting the Buddha; another twenty thousand wielded bows and arrows; and another twenty thousand carried great torches of fire.
“We only pray that the Tathāgata will accept our words and not enter the city again.
At that time, the Tathāgata remained silent and did not grant his permission.
Then, as the World-Honored One entered the gate of the city of Rājagṛha, the deity who guarded the city wept before the Buddha and spoke these words:
“I only pray that the Tathāgata will not enter the city again.
For what reason?
Because this city is now filled with a multitude of evil beings.”
If the Tathāgata were to pass into extinction here, how could I ever behold the hosts of devas?

Now the Māra hosts wish to rain down swords, fierce fires, and great stones; if the Tathāgata were to pass into extinction, sentient beings would walk in darkness, the great Dharma-torch would be extinguished, and the great mountain of Dharma would be destroyed, while they would rejoice in the pleasures of birth, old age, sickness, and death.
At that time, although the Buddha heard these words, he did not grant his consent.
Then the deva spoke again:
"World-Honored One!"
If you do not spare your body or life and are determined to relinquish them, why must it be at these six great cities?
If the Tathāgata were to pass into parinirvāṇa in this place, it would cause me to incur a great ill repute throughout immeasurable ages.
At that time, there were again immeasurable devas who together approached the Buddha’s dwelling and spoke these words:
“World-Honored One!

We have already seen immeasurable Buddhas preaching the Dharma and teaching and transforming immeasurable sentient beings; yet we have truly never before seen such a host of Māras. Sentient beings in the world are constantly surrounded by immeasurable evil afflictions, yet they have encountered a skilled physician who has mastered immeasurable medical arts and skillful means.”
"For what reason does the Tathāgata abandon his heart of great loving-kindness and great compassion?
Another deity further said:

"In the past, throughout immeasurable kalpas, the Tathāgata cultivated and accumulated ascetic practices for the sake of all sentient beings; why now do you wish to abandon sentient beings and cast aside your own life?"
I only pray that you will compassionately expound the True Dharma to subdue all ignorant and deluded sentient beings.

I pray that you will bestow light upon sentient beings, showing the correct path to those who wander in confusion, forever severing all suffering of the three evil realms. I only pray that you will remain for a long time and not relinquish your life.
At that time, there were also gods from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens who addressed the other gods, saying:
"Cease your wailing and abandon your grief; the Tathāgata, endowed with the ten powers and fearlessnesses, now intends to utterly destroy all the hosts of Māra."
"Even if there were immeasurable and boundless hosts of Māras, they would not be able to move even a single hair of the Buddha.
At that time, Brahmā Śakra and Śakra-devendra went to where the Buddha was and addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
All the hosts of Māras now certainly intend to harm and destroy the Tathāgata; we pray only that you do not go.
The Tathāgata shall extinguish the darkness of ignorance and unwholesome conduct of all sentient beings.
World-Honored One, in the past you invited all sentient beings and promised them the nectar of immortality; since this matter remains unfulfilled, why do you now wish to relinquish your life?
Do not rely on the fact that you defeated one Māra beneath the Bodhi tree in the past to think you can treat the rest with contempt.
"If the Tathāgata enters the city of Rājagṛha, he will immediately vanish and disappear; of this there is no doubt.
At that time, the World-Honored One emitted a great Brahma-voice that pervaded the trichiliocosm, and then spoke these words:
"Listen attentively!"
Listen attentively!
Even if all the Māras were to fill the worlds of the ten directions and exhaust all their power and might, they could not move even a single hair of mine.

In the past, I already made a vow for immeasurable sentient beings, promising them the ambrosia of immortality; now I shall expound the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*) to increase wholesome dharmas, and preach the true path in accordance with my original aspiration.

Throughout immeasurable eons in the past, for the sake of all sentient beings, I have endured much suffering and affliction. I renounced all gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, precious goods, kingdoms, cities, wives, children, clothing, food, and drink, as well as my own body and life. I made offerings to the Buddhas with exquisite incense, flowers, banners, canopies, lamps, and lights, upheld the pure precepts, and practiced patience.
Who could inflict evil upon my body?
I constantly cultivate loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings; who could cause me to perish?
Just as I have already crushed the retinues of Māra in the past, you should know that I can likewise destroy them now.
"Do not harbor fear regarding this. When the immeasurable devas heard these words, joy arose in their hearts and they each said:

"Homage to the Great Being, the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One! You who destroy the great hosts of Māra and shatter all afflictions; who forever sever habitual tendencies and crush the mountain of arrogance; who uproot the tree of birth-and-death, extinguish the sun and moon of death, and dispel the darkness of ignorance; who convert all sentient beings of false views, dry up the four torrents, and kindle the great torch of Dharma; who show the path to Bodhi and beat the great drum of Dharma."

"I shall bestow upon all sentient beings the bliss of the sublime Dharma, further cause them to awaken to the characteristics of the Four Noble Truths, and ferry them across the ocean of birth and death into the state of fearlessness.
Having spoken these words, he made offerings to the Buddha with exquisite incense, flowers, banners, canopies, and musical performances.
Furthermore, they scattered various kinds of exquisite and beautiful flowers over the city of Rājagṛha,
namely: māndārava flowers, mahāmāndārava flowers, pāruṣaka flowers, mahāpāruṣaka flowers,
karkārava flowers, mahākarkārava flowers, mañjūṣaka flowers, and mahāmañjūṣaka flowers.
Śāla flowers, campaka flowers, mahācampaka flowers, saumanasa flowers, mahāsaumanasa flowers, vārṣika flowers, mahāvārṣika flowers,
pārijātaka flowers, kovidāra flowers, utpala flowers, kuvalaya flowers, and padma flowers.
With *puṇḍarīka* flowers and other such blossoms, the Tathāgata’s path was adorned and completely covered.
On both sides of the road stood rows of seven-jeweled trees as tall as a *tāla* tree, with clear springs of eightfold flavor flowing between them.

In the space above, there were many devas holding exquisite banners and canopies made of the seven precious jewels; they rained down various flowers and treasures such as gold, silver, crystal, and lapis lazuli.
Gośīrṣa sandalwood, white sandalwood, firm and solid aloeswood, and various fragrant flowers rained down everywhere along the path where the Tathāgata traveled.

Furthermore, there were various subtle and exquisite musical performances; all the people together adorned and prepared the route outside the city of Rājagṛha for the Tathāgata’s journey, while the retinues of the Māras adorned the interior of the city.
At that time, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, entered the city of Rājagṛha.
Then, his mind dwelt in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, manifesting the subtle and wondrous eighty minor marks of excellence.

If one worships an elephant, an elephant appears; if one worships a lion, a lion appears; if one worships an ox, an ox appears; if one worships a *jīvañjīvaka* bird, a *jīvañjīvaka* appears; if one worships a rabbit, a rabbit appears. If one worships a fish, dragon, tortoise, or turtle; Brahmā, Maheśvara, Skanda, or the eight-armed [Viṣṇu]; Śakra, asuras, garuḍas, tigers, wolves, pigs, deer, the deities of water, fire, wind, the sun, moon, and stars; kings, ministers, men, women, the great, or the small; śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, the Four Kings, yakṣas, bodhisattvas, or Tathāgatas—each shall see them according to what they worship. Having seen them, they all cry out, "Namo, namo to the Unsurpassed World-Honored One," joining their palms with reverence, prostrating, and making offerings.
At that time, the seer Himavatprabhārasa was standing to one side with his disciples beneath the western gate, waiting for the Buddha.
When the seer Himavatprabhārasa beheld the Buddha’s body—which bore the marks of a seer and was the object of offerings from immeasurable sentient beings—he spoke these words:
"A person such as this is truly a Great Seer (maharṣi), worthy of receiving the offerings of the world’s devas and humans."
Why is this? Because it is a mark of merit.
How am I to know whether that person is greater than I, or I am greater than them?
"I shall now inquire about his birth, clan, sacred scriptures, and how long he has been a renunciant.
The Seer Prabhāsa then approached the Buddha and addressed his disciple, the Māṇava:

"That seer’s marks of virtue are fully perfected and clearly discernible; he is intelligent, wise, and capable of understanding profound meanings. You all should give rise to sincere faith. According to what I have seen in the manuals of physiognomy, this man will surely be able to expound the Unsurpassed Way, and he will certainly enable me to cross over from birth and death."
The five hundred disciples exclaimed in unison: "Excellent! Excellent!"
"It is as the Upādhyāya has said.
At that time, Prabhārasa, surrounded by five hundred disciples before and behind him, went to where the Buddha was and spoke these words: "Who are you?"
The Buddha said,
"He is a brahmin. Prabhārasa spoke again:
"What is your clan? He replied, "My clan is Gautama."
He asked again,
"What precepts have you received? He replied:
"I have received the three precepts.
He asked again: "What practices have you cultivated and accumulated?"
He replied, "I practice the three gates of liberation.
He asked again:
“How long has it been since you went forth?
He replied, “Since the time I attained great wisdom.”
He asked again:
"Have you ever read or recited the books on the stars? He replied:
"What benefit have you gained from reciting this now? Prabhārasa replied,
"I teach this Dharma to all sentient beings, and many who receive my words present me with offerings."
The Buddha said, "You know this script; are you perhaps able to transcend birth, old age, and death?
Prabhāsa again asked:
"Gautama! How can birth, old age, sickness, and death be severed?
The Buddha said:
"If you cannot sever birth, old age, and death, what is the use of reciting such astrological texts?
Prabhāsa replied again, "Gautama!..."
If you were ignorant of the science of astrology, why would there be traces of stellar movements upon your body?
Since I know this, I must conclude that Gautama has attained mastery over such astrology.
The Buddha asked,
"What is meant by the 'path of the stars'? Prabhārasa replied:
"It means that the twenty-eight lunar mansions follow the movements of the sun and moon, and the days, months, years, and ages of all sentient beings are entirely dependent upon them.
Gautama! The tracks of all the lunar mansions consist of four divisions."
“Gautama! There are seven lunar mansions in the eastern quarter, namely: Aśvinī, Bharaṇī, Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśiras, Ārdrā, and Punarvasu.
If a person’s birth falls under the constellation Aśvinī, their mouth will be four finger-widths wide, and their forehead will be of equal breadth.”
If there are many black moles on the right side of his body, each with hair upon them, one should know that this person will possess great wealth and nobility.

He will have a broad forehead and a handsome appearance, be intelligent and highly wise, and have a flourishing circle of kinsmen. His neck will be short, his two feet will have long toes, and he will bear a sword-wound on his left side. He will have many wives and children, be of a bad temperament and flighty nature, and live for eighty years.
Every forty years he experiences one period of suffering from decline; his eldest son does not live long; his heart delights in religious matters; and his affliction from decline lies in fire.
Gautama! Those born under the constellation Viśākhā have such characteristics.
"Those born under the constellation Kang (Kṛttikā) delight in religious affairs; they are naturally skillful, intelligent, wealthy, and noble.

They possess much shame and remorse, and enemies cannot harm them. They desire to leave the household life, are gentle by nature, and are light-footed and quick-witted, leaving nothing hidden. Their lifespan is sixty years."
"At thirty-five years of age, his body will encounter a severe illness; there shall be a sore or ulcer around four finger-widths of his neck, and he will not be fit for offspring.
Gautama! One who belongs to the constellation Kṛttikā has such characteristics."
"Those born under the asterism of Di (Jyeṣṭhā) receive bodies that are brave and robust; they will be immensely wealthy and noble, with a lifespan of twenty-five years.
They have a black mole on the left side [of the body], and toward their parents, they harbor a constant evil heart (the *Dandan* edition notes: 'they always give rise to an evil mind')."
"Gautama, one who respects those who have left the household life will be unable to increase their own circle of kinsmen;
such are the characteristics of one belonging to the lunar mansion Jyeṣṭhā."
"One born under the constellation Fangxing (房星) has a naturally corrupt and evil disposition; they are foolish and lacking in wisdom, yet possess great wealth and high status.
There is a mole on the right side [of the body]; their lifespan will be thirty-five years, at which point they shall die by the sword, and they should rely upon their brothers."
"Gautama! One born under the constellation Rohiṇī has such characteristics:
'One born under the constellation Jyeṣṭhā is wealthy and possesses much property, yet is foolish and suffers from wind-disorders (vāta), and lives for thirty-five years.'"
He has sores on his head, yet possesses great renown; poison cannot affect him, and he is not fond of his wife and children.
Gautama! One whose mind is attached to the stars has such characteristics.

"The native of the constellation Mūla possesses all the marks and signs of excellence; he is heroic, wealthy, and attains great sovereignty. He has the mark of wheels on his two breasts, possesses great renown, and the radiance of his body surpasses that of the sun and moon."

He was intelligent and possessed great wisdom such that none could surpass him; delighting in the joy of renunciation, he was able to subdue his afflictions; he increased his circle of followers and was full of shame and remorse; his lifespan was one hundred years.
At forty-five, he will briefly experience suffering; his chest possesses marks of virtue that beings delight in beholding, yet it is not favorable for his parents.
Gautama! One born under the constellation Mūla has such characteristics.

Those born under the constellation Jishi delight in litigation and dispute; they frequently violate prohibitions and precepts, possess a corrupt and evil nature that others loathe to behold, and their greed and desire are intensely burning; their lifespan is sixty years.
"Poor and suffering, always delighting in wandering about, with sparse and small teeth, and a chest that is sunken and emaciated.
Gautama! One born under the lunar mansion of the East has such characteristics."

Those born under the constellation Jingxing (井星) will generally possess abundant wealth and treasures and be respected by others. Their hearts delight in the Dharma, yet they will have sores on their navels. Their lifespan will be eighty years.

They will be compassionate and filial, making offerings to their parents and teachers. They will suffer the loss of their parents first, yet their hearts will be free from stinginess and they will possess great shame and remorse. Calamities and misfortunes will arise through water.
"Gautama! Those born under the constellation of the Well (Kṛttikā) have such characteristics.

Those born under the constellation of the Ghosts (Ārdrā) are stingy and short-lived; they should have a black mole four finger-widths below the navel, are ill-fated toward their parents, and delight in disputes."
"Gautama! Those born under the lunar mansion of Ārdrā have such characteristics as these.
'Those born under the mansion of Punarvasu are wealthy and noble, observe the precepts, delight in Dharma activities, and live for seventy-five years.'"
They increase their retinue and, after death, are reborn in the heavens. They have infants at their waists; those who respectfully receive the Dharma are trusted and submitted to by others.
Gautama! Those born under the constellation of Jyeṣṭhā (the Willow Star) possess such characteristics.

Those belonging to the Seven Stars delight in being bandits; they take the theft of goods as their occupation, are treacherous, deceitful, and crooked, possess meager merit and short lifespans, and are coarse and violent in their conduct; being foolish and demented, they will surely die by the sword.
"Gautama! Those born under the Seven Stars possess such characteristics:
'One who belongs to the Star of the Net (Jyeṣṭhā) will have a lifespan of eighty years, be skilled in music, have sparse hair on the head, and suffer decline at ages twenty-seven and thirty-three.'"

He will be wealthy, noble, brave, and robust, possessing great renown; he will be intelligent and free from stinginess, delighting in the Dharma and possessed of a sense of shame and remorse. He will not be in harmony with his parents or brothers. There will be a sore or ulcer on the crown of his head (the *dan* edition states it is on the nape of his neck). Only after the age of thirty-five will he have offspring. He will have a black mole on his private parts and a yellow mole on his thighs.
"Gautama! Those born under the constellation Āśleṣā have such characteristics:

'Those born under the constellation Phalgunī are skilled in calculation, yet they are stingy, of evil nature, dull-witted, and hold wrong views; they have a black mole on the right side of their body, their lifespan is thirty-three years, and they will utterly lack offspring.'"
"Gotama! Those born under the constellation Śraviṣṭhā possess such characteristics.
Those born under the constellation Jyeṣṭhā are immensely wealthy and noble, have many kinsmen, servants, slaves, and attendants, are intelligent and courageous, and delight in and love the Dharma."
Those who respectfully receive the Dharma live for a hundred years; after death, they are reborn in heaven. Gautama!
Those belonging to the southern stars possess such characteristics.
"Those belonging to the constellation Wei (Kṛttikā) shall have black moles on both cheeks; they observe the precepts and delight in the Dharma.
Those who respectfully receive the Dharma will be wealthy and noble, enjoy giving, suffer from inflammatory sores on the body, and live for fifty years."
"Gotama! One who belongs to the constellation Aśvinī has such characteristics.

One who belongs to the constellation Bharaṇī has a short lifespan, is poor and afflicted by hardship, delights in seeing those who break the precepts, is stingy in heart, has sores on the knees, lives for thirty years, and is not harmonious with his elder brother."
"Gautama! One born under the constellation Rohiṇī has such characteristics as these.

One born under the constellation Ārdrā is not favored by his parents; he frequently loses wealth, treasures, fields, and houses. He has a black mole on his knee; after the age of twenty-two, he attains great wealth and honor, and being free from stinginess, he delights in giving."
"Gautama! Those born under the lunar mansion of Ārdrā possess such characteristics.

Those born under the lunar mansion of Punarvasu delight in the True Dharma; they are eloquent and skilled in speech, intelligent and wealthy, highly renowned, and they uphold the prohibitive precepts."
"Respected and trusted by others, after death he will be reborn in heaven; his knees have blue moles, and his lifespan is fifty years.
Gautama! One who belongs to the constellation Kṛttikā has such characteristics."

Those born under the constellation Piṣṭhā are trusted and submissive by others, yet are of a wicked nature and fond of fighting. They harbor greedy desires toward their own sisters, possess much resentment despite wealth and status, and constantly suffer from chest pains. They are ill-suited for money and fortune; they have a black mole on the left side and live for seventy years.
"Gautama! One who belongs to the constellation Pi (Pūrvaphalgunī) has such characteristics.

One who belongs to the constellation Zi (Mṛgaśirā) is wealthy and noble, delights in giving, possesses a sense of shame and modesty, and is free from greed; they suffer no illness or pain, are a joy for sentient beings to behold, and after death are reborn in heaven. Their decline begins at seventy, and their lifespan reaches eighty."
"Gautama! Those born under the constellation Jyeṣṭhā have such characteristics as these.

'Those born under the constellation Mūla are of a wicked nature; they frequently commit evil deeds, serve as jailers, and are excessively prone to greed. They are intelligent yet suffer from poverty, live for sixty-five years, and have many black moles.'"
"Gautama! Those belonging to the Western asterisms have such characteristics:

'Those belonging to the Dipper asterism (Dhruva) are by nature foolish and ignorant; they are greedy and never satisfied; they are poor and of evil character; their lifespan is short; they shall die from illness or hunger; and they are dark-complexioned and emaciated.'"
"Gautama! Those who belong to the lunar mansion of the Dipper (Ursa Major) possess such characteristics.

Those who belong to the lunar mansion of the Ox (Taurus) are by nature dull-witted and impoverished; they delight in theft, their minds are full of envy, they live for seventy years, and they have neither wife nor children."
"Gautama! Those born under the constellation Rohiṇī possess such characteristics.
Those born under the constellation Revatī uphold the precepts and delight in giving; they have many moles on the soles of their feet, increase their circle of kinsmen, and live for eighty years."
He will possess great renown, be free from illness, and be well-disposed toward his parents and brothers.
Gautama! One born under the constellation Viśākhā has such characteristics.

"One born under the constellation Śravaṇā will possess merit and wealth, be beloved by their kin, yet be stingy and not practice generosity; they will live for sixty-five years, and there shall be a black mole on the soles of their feet."
"Gautama! One who belongs to the constellation Śravaṇā has such characteristics as these.

One who belongs to the constellation Ārdrā is free from physical illness and suffering, is intelligent and observant of the precepts, is proficient in worldly affairs, is wealthy and possesses much property, lives for eighty years, and is well-suited to his kinsmen."
"Gautama! One who belongs to the Ārdrā asterism has such characteristics.

One who belongs to the Rohiṇī asterism is of a base and evil nature, frequently violates the prohibitions and precepts, is wealthy and noble, lives for a hundred years, falls into the evil realms after death, and is ill-fated toward his parents and brothers."
"Gautama! Those born under the constellation Ārdrā have such characteristics.

Those born under the constellation Punarvasu are heroic and possess great strength; they are honorable, wealthy, and noble, possessing great renown. Their kinsmen increase, yet they are not in harmony with their parents. They shall live for a thousand years, their fame shall be immeasurable, and they will delight in the Dharma and leave the household life."
"One who respectfully receives the Dharma is intelligent and possesses great wisdom, being well-versed in worldly affairs. Gautama!
One who belongs to the Northern Constellation has such characteristics; if there is one who thoroughly understands these characteristics, they will reach the other shore and attain great wisdom."
The Buddha said:
“Sentient beings wander in darkness, attached to the bonds of perverted afflictions, following such astrological treatises. O Seer!”

Although one may be born under an auspicious constellation, one may still be reborn as an ox, a horse, a dog, or a pig; furthermore, even among those born under the same constellation, there are disparities of poverty and nobility, or wealth and status.
Therefore, I know that this is an indeterminate dharma. O Seer!
Although you have attained meditative concentration, I am one who possesses all-encompassing great wisdom.
"Why do you not ask about the causes and conditions for liberation, but instead ask about this matter?
Light Flavor spoke again:
"Your present body is no different from that of a worldly person, yet your venerable conduct is no different from that of a seer; I truly do not know now whether you are a deva."
"Are you a seer? A nāga?
Or a ghost?"
Your voice is like the Brahma-sound and your appearance is like that of an ancient seer; since time immemorial, I have never seen or heard of such a physical form or such deeds. Therefore, I now ask:
who are you, and by what are you bound?
To whom does it belong?
What is its lineage?
What subject matter does it proclaim?
"I only wish that you would explain this extensively; I shall listen and receive it.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"If there are those who study and cling to written characters, Such people cannot know this or that."
If one is bound by afflictions, one cannot attain liberation and will constantly suffer.
Now that I am fully endowed with the six supernormal powers, I am therefore called a Great Brahmin.
The six perfections are my clan; through the six ways of respectful harmony, I discipline all my faculties.
Having received and upheld the threefold precepts, I practice the three gates of liberation: emptiness and signlessness;
From the time I first gave rise to the bodhicitta, At that moment, I was named a great renunciant.
I do not perceive the characteristic of a single dharma; therefore, I do not speak of the treatises on constellations.
There is no sentient being and no life-span in dharmas; therefore, I proclaim the purity of non-self.
Having already crossed to the further shore of the three feelings and three modes of conduct, and because all faculties have been severed, there are no signs;
I have truly known all phenomena, and therefore I have attained great tranquility.
If one is without hindrance like space, though practicing bodhi, one does not perceive dharmas;
by cultivating and accumulating the precepts and great forbearance, one immediately attains the great wisdom of non-conceptualization.
If one does not seek the retribution of karma through awakening, And does not turn away from the Dharma to attain bodhi,
If the mind does not cling to any of the aggregates (*skandhas*), Nor again observes this or that,
And furthermore does not conceptually know the path to bodhi— This is how one can swiftly attain the path to bodhi.
Without marks and without conceptual thought, Free from applied and sustained reflection regarding all phenomena,
And without attachment to any dharmas, One is able to attain all-encompassing awakening.
If one cultivates and accumulates the pure Brahma-faring, that person is named a Brahmin;
observing all phenomena as being like space, that person is then named the Great Awakened One.
When the World-Honored One had spoken these verses, the seer Prabhārasmi and his entire retinue all beheld the true body of the Tathāgata.
Having seen his true body, they pursued what was wholesome and each immediately attained the Jewel Banner Samādhi (Ratnaketu-samādhi).
Having attained this samādhi, one is able to universally observe all samādhis; therefore, it is called a "banner.
One attains mastery over all samādhis and enters the spheres of all samādhis; for this reason, it is named the Jewel Banner Samādhi (Ratnaketu-samādhi).
At that time, Prabhārasmi joined his palms in reverence and, holding a handful of exquisite flowers, spoke these verses in praise of the Buddha:
“The Tathāgata has accomplished immeasurable virtues, Like the waters of the great ocean, filling it to the brim.
The radiance of his merit is most subtle and wondrous, Illuminating the entire trichiliocosm.”
With courageous diligence and great wisdom, Surpassing all sentient beings,
Possessing a heart of great loving-kindness and great compassion— Therefore, I pay homage to the Unsurpassed Honored One.
The Tathāgata has forever severed all afflictions; therefore, I bow my head to the Great Sage, Teacher.
With the pure golden light of his precepts, I now pay homage to the Buddha-Sun.
Able to dry up the various afflictions of sentient beings, Able to expound the true practice of bodhi,
Able to destroy all mountains of affliction, He turns the unsurpassed wheel of the True Dharma.
Now as I cultivate the path to enlightenment, In order to attain supreme, great wisdom,
And become a Tathāgata endowed with all marks— I pray that you grant us the prediction of our time for enlightenment.
How shall I sever afflictions and deliver all suffering beings,
proclaiming the true and authentic Path, equal in every way to the Buddhas of the ten directions?
Sentient beings have created evil karma throughout the three periods of time; how may I cause them to sever it?
If my own body, speech, and mind perform wholesome deeds, I vow that through these causes and conditions, their fetters shall be severed.
Forever severing all diseases of affliction, may they experience sublime bliss in their bodies as did the Buddhas of old;
may they be endowed with exquisite physical forms and all faculties, remaining far removed from all evils and cultivating wholesome dharmas.
Severing all false views of sentient beings, Cultivating and perfecting right view,
Attaining the knowledge of past lives and delighting in wholesome conduct, They cross the river of birth and death to reach the further shore.
Having fully perfected the six pāramitās, Knowing that the Buddha’s profound Dharma abides eternally in the world,
He delights in raining down the supreme great Dharma rain, Causing all sentient beings to be free from poverty and thirst.
Whatever evil karma I have committed through body, speech, and mind, I now repent of it all before the Buddha.
By the power of all the merit I now possess, I bestow it upon all sentient beings so that they may quickly attain Buddhahood.
I entreat all sentient beings, exhorting them to plant the seeds of bodhi;
when I undergo suffering for the sake of sentient beings, may no regret or backsliding arise.
May the worlds and sentient beings be purified, and may unimpeded wisdom and the pure dharma-realm be attained;
if I truly attain the path of the Buddha, may these scattered offerings become a flower canopy.
At that time, Prabhārasa immediately scattered flowers.
Thereupon, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways, and immeasurable sentient beings gave rise to hearts of reverence and joy.
There were sentient beings who worshipped elephants; seeing the Buddha as an elephant, they said:
"How is it that this elephant possesses such great merit that this seer pays him respect and makes offerings?"

"Furthermore, if there are those who revere and serve the Buddha, and they see that seer making offerings with a reverent mind, upon seeing this, they will give rise to faith, prostrate themselves, and offer praise.
At that time, the World-Honored One emerged from the Śūraṅgama Samādhi; having arisen from concentration, the bodies of all sentient beings beheld the Buddha’s form."
Having seen this, their hearts were filled with joy and a desire to make offerings; each, according to his own ability, performed an offering.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Prabhārasa, saying: "Good son!
Because all the devas saw that you had resolutely resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and leaped for joy, they caused this earth to quake in six ways.
"Good son! You shall achieve immeasurable wisdom, and thereafter attain the unsurpassed path of the Buddha; only then shall you again kindle the great Dharma-torch throughout immeasurable worlds."

“Good son! In a future age, after three asaṃkhyeya kalpas have passed, you shall become a Buddha in a world to the north of this land named Fragrant Flower (Gandhapuṣpa). That realm will be adorned like that of Amitābha; therein you shall attain Buddhahood with the name Light of Merit (Prabhāguṇa) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.”
"Throughout immeasurable ages, he has proclaimed the Mahāyāna, never speaking of the Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha vehicles.

At that time, the great assembly, having heard with their ears and seen with their eyes the seer Arciṣmān receive his prediction of enlightenment, all rejoiced together, making offerings and paying him respect.
Five hundred disciples and immeasurable sentient beings resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, their intentions becoming firm and steadfast without any regression.

Chapter Five: On Characteristics (*Lakṣaṇa-parivarta*) In the *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*, within the "Jewel Banner" section, Chapter Five: On Characteristics. At that time, the Buddha, having known the thoughts of all the Māras, immediately entered into samādhi. By the power of this samādhi, he caused the city of Rājagṛha to have twelve gates, and within each gate there was a Tathāgata.

At that time, the various Māras saw the twelve Buddhas; they manifested their own bodies in the likeness of those possessing the five supernatural powers, even manifesting in the likeness of Brahmā kings, and made offerings to the Buddhas with exquisite incense, flowers, banners, canopies, and musical performances.
When the Buddha entered the city, he pressed the earth with his toe, causing this trichiliocosm to quake in six ways.

Among them, the devas, asuras, Śakra, Brahmā, the four heavenly kings, and all sentient beings were all able to see the worlds of the ten directions and the sentient beings therein, all of whom had gathered at the great city of Rājagṛha, bringing fragrant flowers to make offerings to the Buddha.
By the spiritual power of the Buddha, these verses were uttered from within the incense and flowers:
“If one wishes to forever sever the three evil realms, One should give rise to the bodhicitta;
If one awakens alone amidst birth and death, This is the means to deliver all sentient beings.”
If one wishes to be free from evil and urgent affairs, one should cultivate and assemble the True Path;
if one encounters any of the Tathāgatas, that person shall immediately receive the prediction of attaining the Way.
The Tathāgata, the Great Being, benefits all sentient beings; now he has entered this city of Rājagṛha.

Desiring to crush the hosts of all Māras and desiring to turn the unsurpassed wheel of the True Dharma, the Buddha proclaims for the sake of sentient beings in the age of the five corruptions the Śūraṅgama of the Three Vehicles.
"The Tathāgata now wishes to bestow a great prophecy; those who wish to hear the true meaning should go there.
This verse resounded and was heard everywhere.

Then, from the Karanda Bamboo Grove Monastery, all the bodhisattvas, arhats, and others gathered together in the great city of Rājagṛha. Furthermore, from immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions—whether pure lands or defiled lands, whether where a Buddha resides or where there is no Buddha—all sentient beings came and assembled.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Buddha-Adornment Necklace Samādhi; having entered this samādhi, he caused this Sahā world to become pure and adorned, just like the land of the Tathāgata Samantadarśin of the future.

At that time, the World-Honored One’s radiance was pure and sublime, and sentient beings delighted in beholding it. Throughout the infinite worlds as numerous as motes of dust in the ten directions—whether pure or defiled lands, and whether places where a Buddha resided or not—all sentient beings likewise delighted in beholding the Tathāgata’s pure and sublime radiance, and they also delighted in hearing the Tathāgata’s voice.
At that time, from each of the ten directions, immeasurable bodhisattvas from immeasurable buddha-fields all came to this Sahā world, to the great city of Rājagṛha.
At that time, this world-system was filled with a great multitude of immeasurable bodhisattvas, all of whom together made offerings to the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One.

Some bodhisattvas rained down various blended incenses upon the Sahā world to make offerings to the Buddha; some bodhisattvas rained down genuine jewels and pearls upon this world to make offerings to the Buddha; some bodhisattvas rained down exquisite necklaces, or rained down gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, musaragalva, and agate; some rained down sandalwood and aloeswood incenses; others rained down ox-head sandalwood; and still others rained down various flowers, such as sumanā flowers, to make offerings to the Buddha.

Some bodhisattvas praised the Buddha with the Dharma of ultimate reality; others manifested as the image of Śakra, Lord of Devas; the image of Brahmā, King of Devas; the images of the Four Heavenly Kings; the forms of Māra; the image of Maheśvara; the image of Vedha; the image of the Eight-Armed Deva; the image of a Universal Monarch (Cakravartin); the image of a mountain of jewels; and the images of groves and forests, as well as the images of ministers, elders, men and women, teachers and masters, oxen, sheep, elephants, horses, and water buffaloes. Manifesting such forms, they proceeded to the Great Lotus Grove in Rājagṛha, whereupon they touched the lotuses with their hands and the flowers immediately trembled.
At that time, all the hosts of Māras—men and women, great and small, along with their retinues—were all shaken and filled with great terror, and they spoke these words:
"By what cause and condition do our palaces tremble and shake in this way?"
"Is that which we revere about to perish and vanish? Shall we lose our heavens?
Do we, too, not wish for extinction and downfall?
We have always seen such worlds possessed of the five turbidities; by what cause is it now so tranquil and pure?"
At that time, all the Māras saw the pure Bodhisattvas from the ten directions all gathering in the Sahā world; having witnessed this event, they spoke again, saying:

"Because of the Buddha, the World-Honored One’s majestic and beautiful radiance, and due to the causes and conditions by which sentient beings delight in seeing it, not even a single person among our own retinues can be seen."
Again, he thought to himself:
"Why do I not now go to the place where the Buddha is, to attend upon and make offerings to him?
At that time, Māra Pāpīyas went immediately to the Buddha's location, joined his palms in reverence, and spoke these verses:
"I now take refuge in the Tathāgata; having attained joy, my heart is filled with delight.
I pray that you will release me to return to my original place; once I have returned, I shall listen to the True Dharma."
At that time, the World-Honored One replied in verse:
"I do not urge you to go or come; The nature and characteristics of all dharmas are likewise so.
If you now possess great supernormal powers, You may act as you wish with complete freedom, without hindrance."
At that time, Pāpīyas again spoke in verse:
"As the Buddha, the World-Honored One, speaks words of truth, there is indeed no one now who can obstruct me.
Yet, just as I was about to return to my own abode, I immediately found my body bound by five fetters."
The Buddha said:

“I have eternally severed all fetters; desiring to untie the fetters of all sentient beings, I do not dwell upon the various evils of sentient beings. For this reason, I am named ‘Liberated from Fetters.’”
At that time, the World-Honored One, seeing that the sentient beings of the ten directions had all gathered together, spoke these verses:
"Let the entire great assembly listen with a sincere mind, Freeing their hearts from all webs of doubt.
What I shall now speak is inconceivable; You should contemplate it carefully as the causal conditions of karma."
The Unsurpassed World-Honored One is most rare to encounter; so too are the two treasures of Dharma and Saṃgha.
A human body is difficult to obtain, and faith is likewise so; a mind intent on giving and the field of merit are also difficult to find.
The Unsurpassed World-Honored One is difficult to behold, and having beheld him, it is likewise difficult to hear his Dharma.
It is difficult to be far removed from the eight difficulties; it is likewise difficult to attain patience in accordance with the Dharma.
It is difficult for the mind to be tamed and subdued; it is likewise difficult to cultivate the samādhi of emptiness.
To cultivate wholesome reflection and abide according to the Dharma—these two matters are likewise difficult.
All afflictions are difficult to abandon, and the attainment of Bodhi is likewise difficult.
I now speak of the matters pertaining to the path to Bodhi, just as worldly people speak of magical transformations.
That which I have taught is the distancing from craving; it can destroy the darkness and cultivate wholesome dharmas.
Regarding the unsurpassed, true, and right path that has been shown, one should practice it with a sincere mind and diligent effort.
If you wish to distance yourself from the three defilements of evil, as well as all other demonic activities,
and not be harmed by afflictions, you should listen to the True Dharma from the Buddha.
If one wishes to fulfill the three types of precepts, one should study the fulfillment of the three gates of liberation;
thus one can destroy the fetters of the triple world and also transcend the three evil realms.

If one does not sever the nature of the Triple Gem, and sacrifices body and life for the sake of the True Dharma, one will be able to fulfill immeasurable supernormal powers; such a person is said to abide in accordance with the Dharma.
If one has no discursive thought or investigation regarding the three periods of time, and likewise does not cling to the phenomena of the three periods,
such a person can transcend the triple world and further attain the patience that accords with the Dharma.
All ordinary beings are shrouded by ignorance and are constantly surrounded by the four inversions;
they conceive the notion of phenomena within that which is non-existent, and they conceive the notion of things within that which is nothing.
For these reasons, they are called "inverted," and such people walk upon the path of error.
If there are those who say that the eye sees forms, And so on, up to the mind being able to know all phenomena,
Such people practice in perversion, Cycling through birth and death for immeasurable eons.
If one cultivates and accumulates the four dhyāna concentrations, this is called worldly wisdom;
it can transcend all inversions and also attain liberation from birth and death.
If one can subdue all sentient beings and likewise remain far removed from the four floods,
such a person dries up birth and death and is further able to reach the other shore.
If one can fully possess the four bases of supernormal power, this is called the bodhisattva’s fearlessness;
they are also able to forever sever birth and death, causing all sentient beings to escape from terror.
If one can clearly understand the five aggregates, this person can reach the limit of the outflow-free state;
by thoroughly knowing that they neither arise nor cease, they can cause sentient beings to reach the other shore.
If one can, before the Buddha, the World-Honored One, repent and disclose all transgressions,
that person will be far removed from wrong views and shall be able to reach the other shore of birth and death.
If one contemplates how birth and death involve much suffering, and how the causes and conditions of one's actions lead directly to the three evil realms—
due to the influence of associating with evil friends— one creates immeasurable evil karma.
If one can distance oneself from evil associates and likewise distance oneself from all false views,
such a person can perceive the faults of birth and death, and is also able to inquire about the ultimate truth.
If there is one who can contemplate the foremost emptiness, this person can partake of the flavor of ambrosia.
I constantly preach the primary truth; those who listen with a sincere heart will find no marks of duality.
I say that the six sense bases are truly empty; there is no agent and no experiencer.
Sentient beings, through their inversions, claim they possess characteristics, yet the true nature of phenomena is utterly non-existent.
If there are sentient beings who possess the craving for the six sensations, these are the causes that give rise to the six contacts;
yet these six contacts are truly empty, and all phenomena are likewise so.
As the nature of one dharma is so for all dharmas, and as all dharmas are thus in one dharma, all dharmas are without arising or ceasing; they have no characteristics and possess no substantiality.
The unsurpassed path that I have proclaimed is that all phenomena are one and the same;
if one perceives that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature and characteristics, such a person attains the true meaning.
If one practices the thirteen kinds of patience, One can immediately cross to the far shore of birth and death;
Truly knowing the nature of dharmas and the nature of sentient beings, One attains the unsurpassed path, just like the Buddhas of the past.
Then, as the World-Honored One spoke these verses, all sentient beings throughout the five-defilement worlds in the ten directions—as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—heard them.

In each and every world, immeasurable sentient beings, upon hearing this, immediately attained the mind of non-retrogression; some obtained dhāraṇīs, others attained samādhi, and still others achieved the various levels of patience (*kṣānti*).
Upon hearing this, immeasurable sentient beings in this Buddha-world also attained the mind of non-retrogression and began to teach and transform sentient beings within the three vehicles.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Light Flavor (Prabhārasa) constructed a staircase of the seven treasures adorned with various flowers beside a lotus flower; joining his palms in reverent homage, he addressed the Buddha, saying:

"The Tathāgata is the sun of Buddhas and the light of great compassion. Immeasurable sentient beings endure much suffering and affliction; I only pray that you will pour down the unsurpassed rain of Dharma to eliminate the diseases of the afflictions of sentient beings."

There are sentient beings who serve as vessels for the Dharma and are capable of receiving the unsurpassed flavor of the Tathāgata’s teaching; may you preach the Eightfold Path to purify their Dharma-eye, so that they may ascend upon the lotus flower and subdue all demons.

The immeasurable bodhisattvas of the worlds in the ten directions all serve as witnesses; they clearly perceive that all phenomena are empty and quiescent, devoid of characteristics like space, and know that there is no self in phenomena. We only pray that the Tathāgata will remember the vows he established when he first resolved to attain bodhicitta in the past.
At that time, the Tathāgata said of himself:

"If I am fully endowed with the ten powers and the four fearlessnesses, I shall bestow upon sentient beings the ambrosial flavor of the Dharma, causing them all to cross over the great ocean of birth and death."
"Now that this has already been accomplished,
we only pray that you will expound the Dharma of purity, to ferry all sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death, and to transform immeasurable people for the path of Bodhi."
At that time, the World-Honored One ascended the precious staircase and sat upon the lotus flower; surveying the ten directions, he addressed Pāpīyas, saying:
"Pāpīyas! You too should give rise to a heart of joy."

Why is this? It is because of you that this great assembly has come to be; it is also because of you that I am moved to preach the Dharma. Through the causes and conditions of preaching the Dharma, all birth and death are severed and one crosses over the four torrents, enabling all sentient beings to attain the Right Path and realize the mark of emptiness.
"All such matters as these depend upon you; you should entreat me, and I shall preach the Dharma. Māra Pāpīyān said, "Gautama!"
If you were free from anger, pride, and jealousy, why would you trouble me by preaching the Dharma?
If you possess anger, pride, and jealousy, how can you say of yourself that you have attained liberation?
The Buddha said, “Pāpīyan!
I dwelt in my mother’s womb for ten months; at that time you sought to come and kill me, yet my mind harbored no anger toward you.”
"When I was first born, the earth shook in six ways; at that time, you brought down a rain of stones.
When I was drinking milk, you placed poison within my milk."
In the past, when I first mounted the fragrant elephant, you shook this earth, causing it to quake in six ways, wishing to cause me to fall.
When I was practicing worldly dhyāna in the forest wilds, you brought forth celestial maidens, wishing to come and disturb my concentration.
"When I went out for alms, you brought me stinking beans as an offering; although I accepted them at that time, I did not eat them.
When I first left the city, you transformed yourself into a black venomous snake and further manifested as evil bandits surrounding the city on all four sides."

When I walked through the air, I released wind and rain; when I dismounted from my horse, I unleashed a great and fierce fire; while I was practicing austerities, I produced evil sounds, thereby causing the five men to become terrified and abandon me; when my body became emaciated, I released a cold wind; and when I bathed, I released a massive torrent of water.
After I had crossed the river, you again sought to harm me by transforming yourself into immeasurable lions and ferocious beasts.
When I accepted the milk-gruel offered by the cowherd girl, you once more placed poison within it and departed.
When I was proceeding toward the Bodhi tree, a rain of vajras fell upon me midway along the path.
Furthermore, as I sat beneath the tree upon the vajra-seat, he dispatched four daughters to come and disturb me.
"Although you wish to come and harm me in this way, I harbor no ill will toward you at all; matters such as these can never disturb my mind."

Furthermore, leading immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of beings, they committed all manner of immeasurable evil deeds, desiring that I should not attain Bodhi; yet once I had already attained Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, they came again to entreat me to relinquish my life-span.

It was because of you that I was unable to obtain alms in the great village of Śālā; it was because of you that Ajātaśatru released a large, intoxicated elephant with the intent to harm me; it was because of you that Devadatta dropped a massive boulder; and it was because of you that I accepted the invitation of those brahmins and ate barley for three months.
Furthermore, it was because of you that I was falsely slandered by the woman Sundarī; and it was because of you that Śirigupta invited me with a fire pit and poisoned food.

"At that time, you committed such immeasurable evil deeds as these, yet you could not harm me; now again you have gathered such a host of Māras, desiring to come and harm me. However, I harbor no anger toward you at all. I shall now deliver immeasurable billions of Māras, for I constantly and diligently cultivate and accumulate loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity for the sake of sentient beings."

If you do not believe me, the Buddhas of the ten directions and the great Bodhisattvas may serve as clear witnesses; it is solely for your sake that I have performed the work of a Buddha within this degenerate world.
"Although you have committed immeasurable evils against me, I nevertheless continue to follow after you.
I truly harbor no anger, envy, or pride; I have cultivated a mind of loving-kindness toward you, yet you have conceived a great heart of malice toward me."
“Excellent, Pāpīyas!

You should abandon your evil intent and request from me the unsurpassed Dharma; I wish to bestow upon you the prediction of enlightenment (bodhisattva-vyākaraṇa), and once you have received that prediction, I shall extensively proclaim the essentials of the Dharma for you.”
"Having heard the Dharma, you shall be able to distance yourself from all evil karma.
I have constantly contemplated various skillful means to bring about your liberation, yet you have consistently harbored ill will toward me."
I have always harbored thoughts of compassion for you; you should now abandon your evil views and evil intentions, and I shall bestow upon you the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, having heard these words, Pāpīyān gave rise to a mind of malice and anger, desiring to return to his dwelling; yet he again saw himself bound by five fetters. He wished to let out a great cry but was unable to do so, and immediately spat out foul breath, intending to suffocate the Buddha to death.

At that time, the Tathāgata transformed that foul odor into *sumana* flowers. By the Buddha’s supernatural power, he caused these manifested flowers to reach the abodes of all the Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions—as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—to serve as offerings; above each of those Buddhas, he further manifested a *sumana* flower canopy.
At that time, immeasurable Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and immeasurable Bodhisattvas each asked the Tathāgata of their own land:
"By whose divine power was such a transformation produced?"
The immeasurable Buddhas each spoke, saying:

"In the Sahā world, Śākyamuni Tathāgata desires to expound the essentials of the Dharma for sentient beings who are fully possessed by the five corruptions. These are the dharanis of the gateways to the phrases of the Dharma-seal, which can destroy all the powers of the realms of Māra, reveal all the powers of the merits of the Buddhas, erect the great Dharma-banner, and ensure that the lineage of the Buddhas is never severed."

It can cause all wholesome dharmas to increase; it can destroy all sentient beings with false views; it can destroy all evil dreams and inauspicious omens; it can sever illness, warfare, famine, litigation, and other such calamities; furthermore, it can subdue all devas, nāgas, gandharvas, and humans, and kindle the torch of wisdom to guide all toward the path of equality.

It can cause all beings to distance themselves from evil views; it can sever all evil natures; it can cause all to become of one nature; it can protect all cities, villages, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas; it can know the movements and cycles of all the stars and constellations; it can learn all worldly affairs; it can cause all to distance themselves from harsh speech and attain unimpeded eloquence; and it can contemplate all dharmas, penetrating their nature and abiding in accordance with the Dharma.

He is able to expound the Mahāyāna to comfort bodhisattvas, causing them all to attain a mind of non-retrogression; he is able to bestow the flavor of the unsurpassed nectar of the Dharma, enabling them to obtain the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*); he turns the wheel of the true Dharma to benefit and subdue immeasurable sentient beings, causing them all to abide in the six *pāramitās*.

It enables sentient beings to see the unsurpassed path; it can bring down the rain of Dharma and manifest the deeds of all Buddhas beyond the realms of the four Māras; it is the dhāraṇī of the causal conditions for mastery over the adamantine mind of the Dharma that enters great nirvāṇa.

To uphold and expound such dharmas as these—just as they were proclaimed by the Buddhas of the past and will be proclaimed by all Buddhas of the future, and as the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in the ten directions, preach the Dharma and transform sentient beings—all are the Vajradharmacitta-pratyaya-vaśitā-dhāraṇī;
it is likewise for all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the past and the future.
At that time, immeasurable bodhisattvas from all directions each addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We have never before heard of the *Vajradharmahṛdayapratyayasvatantra-dhāraṇī*. What is meant by the ‘*Vajradharmahṛdayapratyayasvatantra-dhāraṇī*’?”
"We only pray that the Tathāgata will analyze and explain this, even unto leading [beings] into Great Nirvāṇa, for the benefit of immeasurable multitudes of humans, devas, and other classes.
At that time, the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions each addressed their respective bodhisattvas, saying:
"O sons of good family!"

I, too, wish to see Śākyamuni Tathāgata and receive this Dharma, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, for the sake of destroying the evil karma of all sentient beings, and even for the sake of entering great parinirvāṇa.
At that time, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
“Sons of good family!

If you wish to make offerings to the immeasurable Buddhas of a single Buddha-world, and if you each desire to hear and receive the unsurpassed true Dharma—the teachings never heard before—and to behold this great assembly, you should proceed to the place where Śākyamuni Tathāgata dwells in the Sahā world.”
At that time, immeasurable bodhisattvas accepted the Buddha’s instructions in silence, each saying: "We wish to offer worship and respect to immeasurable Buddhas in those single Buddha-worlds;

we also wish to hear and receive various immeasurable meanings of the Dharma from those immeasurable Buddhas; and we wish to behold immeasurable supernormal powers and immeasurable inconceivable matters. We do not know, however, whether there will be sufficient seating in those lands."
"If there is a place where one may sit, then one shall be able to make offerings and listen to and receive the True Dharma.
At that time, the Buddhas addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"O sons of good family!"
"You all should not give rise to thoughts of doubt or uncertainty regarding the Tathāgata. Why is this?
The realm of the Buddhas is inconceivable; their wisdom and skillful means are inconceivable."
"O son of good family! In order to subdue all sentient beings, the wisdom and skillful means of Śākyamuni Tathāgata in the Sahā world are immeasurable."

"Good son! The bodies of all sentient beings, comprised within the aggregates (skandhas) of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, each as vast as Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains—yet he can cause a mustard seed to contain their seats. This is called the Tathāgata’s wisdom and skillful means."

Furthermore, he causes the multitude to see that the mustard seed is neither expansive nor does the seat become cramped; yet the substance of the mustard seed remains as it was, without any sign of increase or decrease. "Moreover, good son!

To cause all the great earths of every world-system to enter entirely into a single minute atom, while ensuring that the atom shows no sign of increase or decrease—this is called the Tathāgata’s wisdom and skillful means.
"Furthermore, good son!

All the waters existing in all worlds can be made to enter into a single minute atom (*paramāṇu*), yet this does not cause the atom to undergo any increase or decrease; this is called the Tathāgata’s wisdom and skillful means (*upāya*)."
"Furthermore, son of good family!

All the winds that exist in all worlds can be made to enter into a single pore, yet without causing the pore to undergo any increase or decrease; this is called the Tathāgata’s wisdom and skillful means."
"Furthermore, good son!

All the fires that exist in all worlds can be made to enter into a single pore, yet the pore remains without any sign of increase or decrease; this is called the Tathāgata’s wisdom and skillful means."
"Furthermore, good son!

All sentient beings throughout the ten directions can be made to enter into a single minute atom, yet this does not cause the atom to exhibit any sign of increase or decrease; this is called the Tathāgata’s wisdom and skillful means."
"Furthermore, good son!

All the physical, verbal, and mental karmas of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time; the sensations of suffering, pleasure, and neither-suffering-nor-pleasure experienced throughout the three periods of time; the karmic fruits and retributions received from the physical, verbal, and mental karmas of sentient beings throughout the three periods of time; and all the earth, water, fire, and wind throughout the three periods of time, extending to the entire dharma-realm."
The Tathāgata Śākyamuni, in a single thought-moment, attains clear and thorough penetration; yet he does not claim, "I know" or "I am awakened," nor does he know by first applying deliberation.
“Good son! Śākyamuni Tathāgata, fully endowed with such wisdom and skillful means, dwells in the Sahā world.

At that time, immeasurable bodhisattvas from immeasurable buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, having heard of the Buddha’s immeasurable merits, each became fully possessed of immeasurable supernormal powers.
The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra, Scroll Twenty;
The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra, Scroll Twenty-one.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang Dynasty.
Chapter Six: The Dhāraṇī Section, Part Nine of the Jewel Banner Division, Section Six:

The Dhāraṇī Chapter. At that time, in the eastern direction there was a world named Abhirati. Its Buddha was named Akṣobhya. Together with immeasurable bodhisattvas endowed with supernatural powers, he departed from that world and arrived at the site of the Great Assembly of Śākyamuni Tathāgata in the Sahā world in a single thought-moment.
Having arrived, he sat upon a manifested lotus flower; immeasurable bodhisattvas did likewise, each sitting upon their own manifested lotus flower.
In this way, immeasurable Buddhas and immeasurable Bodhisattvas from the eastern direction each came to the Sahā world; having arrived, they all sat upon transformed lotus thrones.
It was likewise so for the two directions of the south and north.

At that time, Amitāyus Buddha of the Western World of Peace and Bliss, together with immeasurable Bodhisattvas endowed with supernatural powers, departed from that world and arrived at the site of the Great Assembly of Śākyamuni Tathāgata in the Sahā World in a single thought-moment. Having arrived, he sat upon a manifested lotus flower;
the immeasurable Bodhisattvas did likewise, each sitting upon a manifested lotus flower, and each, by means of their own supernatural powers and merit, created articles for making offerings.

Some fashioned fine sand mixed with exquisite incense and scattered it over the Buddha; some fashioned various kinds of subtle and wonderful fragrant flowers; some rose and circumambulated the Sahā world to the right; some knelt and praised him with verses; some focused their minds in skillful contemplation; some rained down golden flowers, even unto blue utpala lotuses; and some gazed upon the Buddha’s body with wondrous eyes.
At that time, there was a youth named Subhūti who, by means of his own supernatural power and the Buddha’s supernatural power, produced a great sound and spoke these verses:
“The immeasurable great jewel banners of all Buddhas, Which can destroy the mind’s web of all doubts—
Never before have I seen or heard of such An immeasurably vast assembly.”
This world is filled with immeasurable Buddhas and Bodhisattvas endowed with perfect merit;
this very ground is a great jeweled stūpa, through which all may make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
For what cause and condition have immeasurable Buddhas all come to assemble in this evil world?
Furthermore, the sentient beings in this land are likewise unable to believe in the Buddha’s work.
To destroy all the great works of Māra, To fulfill all great merits,
And to manifest great supernormal powers— For these reasons, the Buddhas have gathered here.
If there are sentient beings in this assembly who, with a sincere heart, give rise to faith and joy,
and listen to and receive the Dharma with such a mind, these people will be able to destroy the works of Māra.
If they wish to penetrate the Unsurpassed Vehicle and desire to practice the Eightfold Noble Path, [they shall attain their goal].
If you wish to forever sever all afflictions, You should listen to the True Dharma with a sincere heart.
The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions Have all come here and sat upon transformed lotuses;
Śākyamuni Tathāgata wishes to preach the Dharma, And to protect the True Dharma, he abides for immeasurable eons.
This sound pervaded the great assembly, and immeasurable bodhisattvas attained immeasurable patiences (*kṣānti*). With one voice and in unison, they spoke these words: “We are now seated;

we only pray that the Tathāgata will proclaim the True Dharma—subtle and fearless, encompassing all phenomena—which can destroy the works of Māra and transcend the path of Māra; which can topple the banner of Māra and raise the supreme standard; which can destroy all afflictions (*kleśa*) and subdue enemies; which can tear asunder the net of doubt and enter the gate of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); which transcends all fears and protects all bodhisattvas, causing them to experience every joy, and enabling them to attain the gates of wisdom and skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), as well as all places of peace and happiness.”

The gates of all samādhis, patience, radiance, wisdom, and skillful means, as well as the heart-dhāraṇī of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment—may the Tathāgata please explain these in detail for the sake of enabling sentient beings to receive all forms of peace and happiness, and to attain supreme appearance, supreme strength, supreme bliss, supreme touch, supreme eloquence, supreme mindfulness, and supreme intention; so that they may not forget what they have heard of the Dharma, may destroy the evil omens within their lands, uphold the precepts, cultivate and accumulate the Path, and never lose the unsurpassed mind of bodhi.
I only pray that the Tathāgata, for the sake of such matters, will proclaim and extensively expound this dhāraṇī: to protect the Dharma;
to ensure that the seeds of the Triple Gem are never severed;
and to show all bodhisattvas the path to enlightenment.
This is because they do not discriminate the emptiness of the nature of space or the characteristics of emptiness;
because they manifest light and darkness, the presence of marks and the absence of marks, by contemplating the mark of equality between this and that phenomenon;

and because they do not discriminate phenomena such as sentient beings, life-span, or the person, but rather give rise to neither birth nor cessation, severing all marks, wherein all marks of transformation and change are non-substantial, being the true nature of space.

We only pray that Śākyamuni Tathāgata, together with all the Buddhas, will extensively proclaim and analyze this great dhāraṇī, so that immeasurable and boundless sentient beings may truly behold the nature of the Triple Gem, and so that immeasurable and boundless sentient beings may give rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, all the immeasurable Buddhas silently granted their consent;
having so consented, they immediately entered the samādhi of the merit of the vows within the supreme and wondrous realm of all Buddhas.
At that time, all the sufferings of the hells, animals, and hungry ghosts within this Sahā world were immediately extinguished, and they were able to behold the various Buddhas.
There were sentient beings who, possessed by nets of doubt and lacking faith, immediately attained pure faith.

All sentient beings saw that [the Buddha] was entirely free from the maladies of greed, anger, ignorance, pride, evil views, the nets of doubt, and mental derangement; his body and mind were tranquil, and each of them thought to themselves:

"I alone am sitting before the Buddha to hear and receive the True Dharma. The Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, speaks only for me; he alone tames me and cuts off all my afflictions, speaking to me exactly as I have requested."
At that time, all sentient beings in the world, with one voice and in unison, spoke these words:
"We pray that the Buddha will preach the Dharma; we shall receive it upon the crowns of our heads."
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata exhorted all sentient beings in this world to make offerings to the Buddhas.
Having heard this exhortation, the sentient beings immediately each made offerings to all the Buddhas with incense, flowers, banners, canopies, music, and hymns of praise.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these words:
"Buddhas of the ten directions, listen attentively, listen attentively!
By virtue of my original vows made in the past, I have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi here in this world, amidst sentient beings who are fully possessed of the five corruptions."

These sentient beings have lost their way, being shrouded by ignorance; they have lost right mindfulness and allowed afflictions to increase. Dwelling securely within the three realms of existence, they delight in committing the ten unwholesome deeds; they distance themselves from roots of goodness and abandon meritorious karma. They take pleasure in creating the five heinous crimes and are addicted to what is not the Dharma; they slander the true scriptures and revile the sages. Their anger is fierce and they take no joy in cultivating loving-kindness; they use the property of the Saṃgha at will and lack deep faith in the retribution of karmic results.

Because such people take no pleasure in making offerings to teachers, elders, superiors, and those of virtue, one cultivates and gathers this great mind of compassion for the sake of these wicked individuals.
By these causes and conditions, he attained enlightenment in this world.

Having attained enlightenment, he constantly delighted in cultivating and accumulating the dharma of diligent vigor; enduring the sufferings of hunger, thirst, cold, heat, and so forth, he traveled through various kingdoms, cities, towns, and villages, proclaiming the True Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.

There may be sentient beings who are impoverished, afflicted by illness and suffering, and possess ugly bodies; out of compassion for them, [the Bodhisattva] accepts the foul and filthy food they offer, consuming it all in order to increase the donors' merit.
He likewise accepts from sentient beings coarse, rough, foul-smelling, and tattered clothing.

He also accepts any dwelling place found among mountains, river valleys, or vast forests and wilds—whether of grass, leaves, stones, or bricks—and for the sake of sentient beings, he accepts whatever is given and lies upon it, cultivating skillful means through diligent vigor.

"For the sake of the kṣatriyas, he expounds upon the affairs of kingship; for the brahmins, he explains the four Vedas, the stars, and the sacrifices to the gods; for the great ministers, he speaks on the matters of governance and transformation; for the physicians, he expounds on illnesses such as the increase or decrease of the four great elements; for the farmers and merchants, he speaks on the protection of wealth and grain; and for the women, he speaks on the protection of their necklaces and ornaments, teaching that by diligently practicing all forms of goodness, they shall not be shared with another husband."

For those who have left the household life, he teaches patience; for the sake of subduing them, he teaches such a Dharma. He exhorts those who have not yet attained wholesome benefits to attain them; he exhorts those who have not yet attained realization to attain realization; he exhorts those who are not yet liberated to attain liberation, so as to undergo various sufferings and afflictions for the sake of taming sentient beings.

I have cultivated and accumulated compassion for the sake of sentient beings; yet these sentient beings still give rise to unwholesome thoughts toward me—beating me, reviling me, or giving rise to jealousy.

Some even say: "The śramaṇa Gautama is a magician; though he praises the observance of precepts, he keeps a wife; though he praises a compassionate heart, he harms sentient beings; and though he praises the renunciation of wealth and status, he goes to royal palaces himself."
The śramaṇa Gautama is well-versed in arts and techniques; though he maintains a wife, he has no offspring.
Because the śramaṇa Gautama can heal women's bodies, he causes Mallikā to give rise to love and respect.
Because the śramaṇa Gautama is skilled in incantations and rituals, he causes Sudatta to conceive thoughts of veneration and reverence.
“The śramaṇa Gautama is well-versed in the methods of medicinal herbs; therefore, his body always possesses radiance.

Having acquired such immeasurable ill repute as these, some people, seeing me from afar, would strike or hurl stones, earth, wood, knives, or poison at me, desiring to kill me. For the sake of killing me, they release fierce elephants and venomous snakes; they set great, raging fires and filth and impurities upon my dwelling place. They employ all manner of evil expedients, wishing to destroy my Dharma, to extinguish my Dharma, to topple the banner of the Dharma, to wreck the ship of the Dharma, to ruin the nature of the Dharma, and to shatter the treasury of the Dharma.
“Buddhas of the ten directions, we pray that you will observe us: Among the Buddhas of the past, there were none who,
having attained the Way of the Buddha in such a world of five corruptions,
did not preach this Great Collection Vajra Dharma-Mind Causal-Condition Sovereign Dhāraṇī, for the sake of destroying all the powers of Māra.”
Because the lineage of the Triple Gem shall not be severed; because it increases wholesome dharmas for all sentient beings; because it destroys all enemies of the Buddha-dharma;
because it causes sentient beings to distance themselves from suffering; because it extinguishes all evil karma of body, speech, and mind;
because it causes the natures of human beings to become harmonious and supple; and because it brings peace and happiness to all lands.
Therefore, it is for the purpose of destroying all evil signs in the world; for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to fully attain the six pāramitās;
for the purpose of inspiring the aspiration for unexcelled bodhicitta; for the purpose of teaching bodhisattvas skillful means;
and for the purpose of causing bodhisattvas to abide in the successive stages.
For these and other such reasons, the Buddhas of the past have, for the sake of sentient beings of the five dregs, preached this Great Assembly Vajra Dharma-Mind Causal Sovereignty Dhāraṇī.

Now all the Buddhas of the ten directions have gathered together in this world; we pray that each of you Buddhas will speak such a dharani mantra out of compassion, for the sake of causing the Mahayana sutras to circulate, so that the Dharma may long endure in this world, and so that the various evil maras shall find no opportunity.
At that time, all the Buddhas spoke these dhāraṇī phrases with one voice:
"Aṅgala 1, Aṅgala 2."
