A second and a third time he spoke likewise.
"How extraordinary! How marvelous!"
The great assemblies of all Buddhas are inconceivable, and the deeds of all Bodhisattvas are likewise inconceivable.

We have never before heard of such a dhāraṇī-name; having now heard it, it can destroy the power of all realms of Māra, perpetuate the nature of the Triple Gem, and sever the net of Māra. It enables one to attain all wholesome dharmas and fulfill the Buddha-work. For these reasons, this Great Dhāraṇī is preached: as a seal for the minds of all sentient beings, it seals the dharmas of the aggregates, bases, and elements of all sentient beings, leading them even unto the attainment of Great Parinirvāṇa.

At that time, there was a youth-bodhisattva in the assembly named Candraprabha (Moonlight). Rising from his lotus seat, he joined his palms with single-minded devotion and surveyed the ten directions. By the power of the Buddha, he uttered a great sound whose resonance was heard throughout the Sahā world, and he spoke these verses:
"Such a great assembly as this is extremely rare to encounter; To be endowed with wisdom is likewise difficult.
It is hard to draw near to a virtuous friend (kalyāṇamitra), And such a Dharma-seal is likewise hard to hear."
The Tathāgata, out of compassion for all sentient beings, For the sake of sentient beings, protects the True Dharma;
He proclaims this unsurpassed dhāraṇī To destroy the various powers of Māra.
The Buddhas of the ten directions proclaim this upholding: To ensure that the nature of the Triple Gem is never severed;
To be able to harmonize all strife and contention, And to be able to increase unsurpassed patience;
To augment the various roots of goodness in sentient beings, And to eliminate all evil signs within the lands.
It can destroy the three evil karmas of sentient beings, And cause them to distance themselves from all wrong views.
The Tathāgata speaks this unsurpassed dhāraṇī Wishing to reveal the unsurpassed path;
It is also for the sake of fulfilling the six pāramitās And truly cultivating the path to bodhi.
This upholding is itself a skillful means, And it can also increase unimpeded wisdom;
It gathers and sustains all wholesome dharmas, Therefore it is called the "Unsurpassed Upholding.
Fully cultivating the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment Is called the "Stainless Path to Bodhi."
Able to sever the net of all doubts and minds, And to sever the various afflictions of sentient beings—
This upholding is itself true speech, Clearly beholding the path to Bodhi.
I now wish to proclaim this dhāraṇī, which is named the Unsurpassed and Supreme;
it is for the purpose of protecting the Dharma-preacher as well as those who hear and uphold this dhāraṇī.
Whoever wishes to receive or hear it, I shall now speak; do not give rise to doubt.
This unsurpassed and peerless dhāraṇī is itself the most supreme wisdom.
At that time, there were bodhisattva youths as numerous as the sands of the Ganges who, with one voice and in unison, spoke these words:

"We, too, wish to proclaim dhāraṇīs. If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās first bathe to purify their bodies and minds, put on new garments, and offer exquisite incense and flowers to the Triple Gem, they may ascend the Dharma seat and proclaim the dhāraṇīs."

Thus, among these four assemblies, there is no sentient being capable of instigating evil deeds to inflict upon them; their bodies and minds are free from turbidity, the four great elements are pure, and all physical ailments and sufferings are entirely eliminated.
In this way, if such a Dharma teacher has any illnesses resulting from past karmic causes and conditions, they will all be completely extinguished.
Those who listen to this Dharma shall likewise extinguish the suffering of illnesses resulting from past karmic causes and conditions.

Why is this? Frivolity is the characteristic of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*); the Tathāgata has already transcended the activities of ordinary beings. All conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛta-dharma*) are impermanent; the Tathāgata does not increase conditioned phenomena, but only increases emptiness and the cessation of sounds, words, and phrases.

The Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, is likewise thus: he is without obstruction regarding all phenomena (*dharma*).

Why is this? This Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra is the seal and certification of all Buddhas of the ten directions.
If one can make offerings to such a Mahāsaṃnipāta, it is equivalent to making offerings to all Buddhas of the ten directions.

After the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, wherever this sutra circulates, if there are those who hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, copy, or even transcribe a single verse, a single phrase, or a single word from it, all the evil deeds of that country’s ruler shall immediately be extinguished.
All trees, grains, and medicinal herbs are nourished by the Four Great Heavenly Kings, who bestow upon them ambrosia.

The laws of the kingdom and its sovereign flourish, while the wicked kings of neighboring states diligently seek harmony; each gives rise within themselves to a heart of joy and a heart of compassion.
All the devas who are disciples of the Buddha shall come to protect such a land, and the princes, queens, and great ministers shall each give rise to a heart of compassion.

Grain and rice will be abundant and ripe; those who consume them will be free from illness. There will be no strife or litigation, and no wars shall arise. There will be no predatory beasts nor calamitous winds and rains, and one shall be distanced from all past evil karma.
If there are sentient beings who possess female karma—whether to be experienced in the present life, the next life, or in subsequent lives—he can cause it to be extinguished.

With the exception of those who have committed the five heinous crimes, those who slander the Vaipulya sutras or the noble ones, or those who violate the four grave prohibitions, and the icchantikas; as for all other evil karmas, even if they were as vast as Mount Sumeru, he can cause them to be entirely distanced from. He causes them to increase wholesome dharmas, to be endowed with the faculties of body, speech, and mind, to distance themselves from wrong views and destroy afflictions, to cultivate and collect the right path, to make offerings to all Buddhas, and to be fully possessed of wholesome dharmas and internal and external matters. Thus, he causes the lifespans of all sentient beings to increase and brings about the perfection of mindfulness and wisdom.
At that time, ninety-seven billion bodhisattvas, including Maitreya Bodhisattva, who had attained the patience of non-arising (anutpattika-dharmakṣānti), spoke these words:

"We, too, shall be able to protect and uphold the True Dharma after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa. Out of compassion, we shall extensively expound this sutra in capitals, cities, towns, villages, and settlements."
At that time, immeasurable Buddhas of the Sahā world spoke with one voice,
praising him: “Excellent, excellent,
son of good family!”
The humans and devas of the Sahā world further spoke thus:
"We, too, shall be able to protect and uphold the True Dharma after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, as well as those among the fourfold assembly who receive, uphold, and expound it."
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions further praised them, saying: "Excellent, excellent!
You all are truly able to protect and uphold the True Dharma."
“Good sons! If you are able to protect and uphold the True Dharma, you should make offerings to such Buddhas, World-Honored Ones.

“We shall surely provide protection wherever this sutra circulates—be it in capital cities, towns, or villages—and we shall ensure that the people, their families, and those who receive and uphold it are blessed, so that the land’s grain will ripen in abundance and medicinal herbs and trees will flourish.”

Why is this? Wherever this sutra circulates, I shall possess great power and influence therein; by means of that power and influence, I am able to protect it, causing all calamities and misfortunes to depart, and also causing all sentient beings within that land to distance themselves from evil karma and give rise to a sense of shame and remorse.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!

You are now truly able to protect and uphold the True Dharma, and you are also able to make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions, as well as to those who protect the Dharma and those who listen to and receive it."

11. Chapter Eleven: The Four Heavenly Kings Protecting the Dharma. From the *Ratnaketu-parivarta* of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*, Chapter Eleven: The Four Heavenly Kings Protecting the Dharma. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed the Brahmās, Śakra, and the Four Heavenly Kings:
"O sons of good family!
For the sake of such evil sentient beings, by the power of my original vow and out of great compassion, I have attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in this evil place.

Desiring to benefit sentient beings who are shrouded in the darkness of ignorance and parched for the Dharma, and those who constantly delight in increasing their afflictions; to destroy the hosts of Māra and establish the banner of the Dharma; to bestow the rain of the Dharma so that all sentient beings may be freed from the suffering of afflictions; and to cause immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Immeasurable Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have all come to assemble in this world-system in order to destroy the immeasurable evil karma of sentient beings and to perpetuate the lineage of the Triple Gem.
"After my parinirvāṇa, all the True Dharma shall be entrusted to you; you must protect it with a profound mind.
If there are bodhisattvas who have accomplished merit, such as these, they too will be able to uphold my True Dharma."

If there are sentient beings who have already planted various roots of goodness under the Buddhas, these persons, during the final fifty years when the True Dharma is about to perish in the future age, will protect the True Dharma, faithfully revering, receiving, upholding, reciting, copying, and explaining its meaning.

If such a Dharma master, wishing to greatly benefit immeasurable sentient beings within a capital city, town, village, or settlement, should bathe himself clean, put on new and fine garments, and adorn himself with incense and flowers; he should then place various kinds of sweet juices upon a single table and set it before a high seat.

If you had not gathered at that time to protect the Dharma Master, to ward off all evil deeds, and to listen to and receive the True Dharma for your own benefit and the benefit of others, you would have been deceiving the Buddhas of the ten directions.
At that time, Brahmā addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
In whatever cities, towns, or villages this sutra circulates, I shall protect it with a sincere heart.”

If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās wish to expound this sutra, they should bathe and purify themselves, don new and clean robes, and gather fragrant flowers and even sweet drinks, placing them before a high seat; I, together with my retinue, will certainly go to that place.
If I do not go, I would be deceiving the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions.

In this world, wherever this sutra circulates, I shall cause that land to be free from all warfare and evil events; I now stand before the Buddhas of the ten directions with utmost sincerity and make this profound and solemn vow.
He then spoke the mantra:
“An-k’u-ha 1, Deng-ka 2, Fu-lo-na-ha 3, She-mie-chü 4, Chü-chü 5, Po-chü 6, Pi-chü-pi 7, Chü-li-na-chü-pi 8, Svāhā. At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra spoke the mantra:

“1. Piṇḍaśana, 2. Kṣapaśana, 3. Ramukha, 4. Kṣasara, 5. Punāha, 6. Amakapāṭa, svāhā. At that time, the Southern Heavenly King Virūḍhaka spoke this mantra:
“1. Ukkhanavajata, 2. Samudrasaya, 3. Tacchudata, 4. Varanada, 5. Varaja, svāhā. At that time, the Western Heavenly King Virūpākṣa spoke this mantra:
“*Jaruga* 1, *Aykaga* 2, *Amamūga* 3, *Amamasaraja* 4, *Bapyemūja* 5, *Svāhā*. At that time, Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King of the North, spoke this mantra:

“*Cḷi* 1, *Cḷicḷi* 2, *Khaḷi* 3, *Anicḷi* 4, *Hīriddhaḷi* 5, *Sakarahīriddha* 6, *Cḷi-sañjūsa-cḷi* 7, *Dhamakhacḷi* 8, *Svāhā*. At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions praised Brahmā, Śakra, and the Four Heavenly Kings, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”
"You all are now truly able to protect and uphold the True Dharma.
At that time, Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and others addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Wherever this sutra circulates, we shall, with a sincere heart, protect and uphold it.
The Buddhas of the ten directions and all the Bodhisattvas spoke in unison, praising them:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Vaiśravaṇa and the rest!
You are truly able to protect and uphold the True Dharma.

At that time, there were twelve thousand great ghost-generals in the Sahā world who protected this world; furthermore, there were forty-four thousand minor generals who had achieved great power and great merit, and they spoke with one voice:
“World-Honored One!
We, too, shall in future ages, wherever this sutra may circulate, provide protection accordingly. When the Dharma is being preached, we shall also go there;
for those who listen to the Dharma, we shall destroy their various demonic activities and protect the preachers of the Dharma, causing them to increase in all wholesome dharmas.”

One should exhort the kings, great ministers, and elders to provide them with clothing, food, and all manner of necessities for sustaining life; furthermore, one should cause that land to be free from the calamities of war and invasion, as well as from adverse winds and rain.
"If my words were false, I would be deceiving the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the Sahā world named Śaṅkācitta (Doubting Mind), who addressed the Buddha Śākyamuni, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"In this Sahā world, are there ten billion Māras?
If there are, will they all come to assemble?
The Buddha said:
“Everything has gathered together.
“World-Honored One,
if everything has gathered together, is there faith?”
The Buddha said:

"Good sons! All possess the mind of faith, with the sole exception of the thousand followers of Pāpīyān, who, in the future, shall destroy my Dharma and constantly seek out faults and transgressions."
This Māra Pāpīyān and his retinue destroy the Triple Gem. Why is this?
It is because of their past evil causes and conditions; they failed to plant roots of goodness in the past.

"Good son! When my Dharma is extinguished, Māra Pāpīyān and his retinue will gain faith in such a Dharma as this; they will plant the seeds of Bodhi, cultivate the path of a Bodhisattva, and eventually attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

At that time, there was a Māra-deva in the assembly named Śukra, who had already accomplished meritorious virtues under immeasurable Tathāgatas. His faculty of faith was unshakable, and he venerated the Triple Gem. Having received the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* from the various Buddhas, he manifested in the form of a rishi; rising from his seat, kneeling with palms joined, and with a great voice that reached throughout all Buddha-fields, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

Due to the causal conditions of Śākyamuni Tathāgata’s original vows and out of his great compassion, he attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi within this world-system of five corruptions amidst a multitude who slander the Dharma; out of compassion, he teaches the Dharma of the three vehicles to liberate beings from the three evil realms.

Furthermore, for immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas, I shall preach the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), so that the lineage of the Buddhas of the ten directions shall not be interrupted.

Therefore, in future ages, I shall protect [this teaching] with a sincere heart, causing the Dharma of Śākyamuni to abide long and not perish, ensuring that the hosts of Māras find no opportunity, and I shall never destroy the True Dharma of the Tathāgata.
If there are no upholders, the Buddha-dharma will perish; if among the fourfold assembly there are none who preach or listen, the Dharma will decline and vanish.

If, in future ages, sons and daughters of good family cultivate and establish the three karmas to perpetuate the nature of the Triple Gem, practicing the Right Path to destroy all evil afflictions of the triple world, they will be able to eliminate the suffering of the three evil realms for sentient beings, such that no hosts of Māras can prevail against them.

I only pray that the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions will bestow upon me the two powers of merit and wisdom; I wish to recite this mantra in order to destroy all the retinues of evil Māras.
Then the Buddhas of the ten directions praised him in unison, saying: "Excellent, excellent!

At that time, the Māra asked Dṛḍhamati:

Now as I behold this, my heart feels as if it would vomit; all four directions are dark, and my body and mind are in agony, yet he perceives it with sweet pleasure and attachment. I only pray that you will have compassion for me and explain this to me.
The Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati said: “Pāpīyān!

It is entirely through the majestic spiritual power of all the Buddhas that this Venus possesses such strength; by means of this strength, it destroys the hosts of Māras and increases the unsurpassed True Dharma of the Tathāgata.”
This is the power of the virtues possessed by the Bodhisattva Śvetaketu; even among gods and humans, none can destroy it. Pāpīyān!
You should give rise to faith in the Triple Gem and resolve for Bodhicitta, remaining far removed from all evil of body, speech, and mind.
Pāpīyān said: "O Great Being!
I am now just about to accomplish various evils of body, speech, and mind; I truly cannot give rise to the bodhicitta."

Chapter Twelve: The Wilderness Spirits (*Āṭavaka*) In the *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*, within the "Jewel Banner" section, Chapter Twelve: The Wilderness Spirits. At that time, the Bodhisattva Āṭavaka manifested the body of a spirit; the Bodhisattva Saṃjñeya manifested the body of a deer; the Bodhisattva Prajñāolkā manifested the body of a monkey; the Bodhisattva Vītarāga manifested the body of a black sheep; and the Bodhisattva Kṣīṇāsrava manifested the body of a king of geese. In this manner, these five hundred bodhisattvas each manifested and assumed various different bodies.
From their bodies issued forth great fragrant light, and each of these bodhisattvas held a lamp in their hands, desiring to make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Susīma observed these five hundred people with a sincere mind and immediately knew them all to be bodhisattva mahāsattvas. He spoke to the wilderness spirit, saying:
"O son of good family!
"For what reason have you manifested such bodies to make offerings to the Buddhas?
The wilderness spirit replied,
"O son of good family!"

In the distant past, ninety-one kalpas ago, there was a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled Vipaśyin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara-puruṣa-damya-sārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.

At that time, I was one of those very people who shared the same parents as brothers; I upheld the five precepts, practiced with diligent vigor, possessed clear intelligence and wisdom, delighted my heart in wholesome dharmas, and made various kinds of offerings to that Buddha.
Having made these offerings, they all resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* (unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment) out of a desire to discipline and transform all sentient beings;
and it was likewise with Śikhin, Viśvabhū, and Krakucchanda Buddha—they all made offerings in this same manner.
The Mahāsattva Saṃjñeya made this great vow before that Buddha:

"May I, in a future age, teach and transform sentient beings with the body of a ghost or spirit. If there are wicked, evil ghosts or sentient beings, I shall expound the Dharma of the Three Vehicles to subdue them; even unto the countless *gaṅgā*-sands of evil ghosts and evil beasts, I shall cause them all to be subdued. Only after that shall I achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
There were also twelve thousand great spirits who made great vows in this world to subdue sentient beings.
At that time, I too made a great vow:
"If there are evil spirits who wish to destroy such Right Dharma of the Tathāgata, I shall subdue them."
"For this reason, I have received such a ghostly body.

If there are evil ghosts who can kill sentient beings and cause their minds to become deranged, who kill with malicious intent and are deeply attached to false views; who can cause Kṣatriyas, Brāhmaṇas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras to lose their minds and commit evil; who can shift the sun and moon within a kingdom, alter the years and seasons so that the land falls into chaos; who cause cold and heat to be misplaced and the seasons to change out of order; who send down calamitous winds and rains so that grain does not ripen, and who destroy all trees and fruits."

May I be able to fully tame and transform all beings, causing them to abide in the Three Vehicles; may I never harm or deprive them of their life-force, but rather share their physical form with them, converse and jest with gentle speech, and teach them through the Dharma of the Three Vehicles so that they may leave the evil realms behind.

"If there are sentient beings who distance themselves from wholesome dharmas and perform unwholesome deeds of body, speech, and mind, they will, after casting off this body, be born in the three evil realms. Or, if there are those who perform a mixture of wholesome and unwholesome deeds, such persons, upon the end of their lives, will receive the body of a hungry ghost."
Therefore, at that time, malevolent spirits were numerous while benevolent spirits were few.
For this reason, I desired to subdue the malevolent spirits and manifested this body, so as to cause the kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, and śūdras to remain far removed from evil thoughts.
“Good son! There is a Vajra-hammer mantra; by the power of this mantra, all evil spirits will be unable to do harm to those of the four castes. Good son!”
In whatever cities, towns, villages, or settlements this incantation exists, no evil spirits shall be able to cause harm.

The sentient beings in those places will all cultivate a mind of loving-kindness, remaining far removed from all unwholesome deeds, as well as from malignant diseases, calamitous rains, droughts, and strife.
Even down to the birds and beasts, they all give rise to wholesome minds and remain far removed from all evil and fear.
Now, before these Buddhas of the ten directions, I make a great vow and wish to recite this mantra.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata addressed the forest-dwelling yakṣa:
"Good son! The Buddhas of the ten directions have now bestowed upon you the power of supernatural faculties; you may speak accordingly."
Then the wilderness spirit immediately arose, joined his palms, and spoke this mantra:
"Doma 1, Doma 2."

"Rāja-kūṣmī (52) Satatu-kūṣmī (53) Svāhā. 13. Chapter Thirteen:

Returning to One's Own Realm, from the "Jewel Banner" Section of the *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*. At that time, the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions each desired to return to their own Buddha-worlds.

At that moment, the earth shook in six ways; various flowers rained down from the sky above, subtle and exquisite music resounded spontaneously without being struck, and all manner of fragrances were offered as an act of worship.
The entire great assembly all joined their palms together and paid homage to the Buddhas.
At that time, Brahmā addressed the Buddha Candragandha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"By whose spiritual power and by what amount of merit will there be those who, in future ages, are able to believe in, accept, uphold, recite, and transcribe such a sutra as this? "Brahmā!

All of this is due to the power of the original vows of the Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions; they destroy the hosts of Māra, eliminate frost, hail, violent winds, and calamitous rains from the land, protect and uphold the True Dharma, and proclaim the Right Path for the sake of harmonizing sentient beings.

Furthermore, by the power of the original vows of all Buddhas, sentient beings of future generations who accomplish these ten dharmas will be able to protect and uphold the True Dharma in the future; such persons shall also be protected by the devas.

“Brahmā! If there is anyone who can be fully endowed with mindfulness, a benevolent mind, and skillful means, that person will be able to protect the True Dharma; they will not crave the five desires but constantly practice emptiness, possess patience like the earth and attain profound, great forbearance, and gather in sentient beings through the four methods of attraction. Being unimpeded in both this world and the next, they shall cultivate the pure path of Bodhi and the Ratnaketu Samādhi.”
Such a person will, in future ages, be able to protect the True Dharma by copying, receiving, upholding, reciting, and explaining it.

When this person casts off their body, they will behold the Buddhas of the present in the ten directions, along with the assemblies of bhikṣus and bodhisattvas, and they will also hear the sublime Dharma preached by those Buddhas.

Having heard this, they immediately attain the joy of the sages, extinguish all unwholesome dharmas, and are born in the pure lands of the Buddhas; there they constantly hear the exposition of Mahāyāna sūtras, never again being born in worlds of the five corruptions, and always remaining in close proximity to such Buddhas as these in the Sahā world.
"In the remaining fifty years thereafter, by the power of the Buddha, this person will be able to protect and uphold the True Dharma of the Tathāgata.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed the Brahmā, saying:

"Wherever this sūtra circulates, in those lands there shall be no evil deeds, calamitous rains, or diseases; those who receive and listen to it shall have no physical suffering, nor shall they lack food or clothing."
At that time, the Buddha Padmāketa addressed the great assembly:

"If one were to bestow upon the Buddhas of the ten directions a full world-system of this Sahā world filled with exquisite seven treasures, it would not equal the merit obtained by someone who, during the final fifty years after a Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, receives, upholds, reads, recites, and transcribes this sutra; the latter's merit is far greater than the former's."
The Buddha again addressed the great assembly:

"Suppose there were someone who offered the seven kinds of supreme and wonderful jewels, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, to the Buddhas of the ten directions; this would not equal the vast merit obtained by someone who, during the final fifty years after the Buddha's parinirvāṇa, receives, upholds, recites, and transcribes this sutra."
When the Buddha had finished speaking these words, the devas and the people of the world, having heard them, rejoiced, accepted them with faith, and practiced accordingly.

Section Ten: The Division on Ākāśamati. Chapter One: The Disciples. Part One of Ten.

At that time, the World-Honored One was staying in the Great Jewel Enclosure between the realms of desire and form, surrounded by an immeasurable assembly of bhikṣus and great bodhisattvas, preaching the Dharma.

At that time, Śāriputra, Maudgalyāyana, and others had not long been ordained; for the sake of Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, he preached the Dharma for śrāvakas, interspersed with the four noble truths.

At that time, there were among the assembly certain individuals who had originally been followers of external paths; their faculties were dull and obscured, yet they considered themselves wise. They gave rise to great arrogance, increasing pride of form, pride of desire, pride of ignorance, pride of superiority, and pride in what is contrary to the Dharma, and they had not yet attained the second, third, or fourth fruits of the śramaṇa.
Therefore, for the sake of such individuals as these, the Tathāgata proclaims the Middle Way in order to bring about detachment from such evil afflictions.
When the Tathāgata teaches the meaning of this Middle Way, these people each engage in discourse concerning the view of annihilationism and the view of a self.
At that time, the World-Honored One had this thought: "Alas!

Because these people were originally followers of external paths, even though they have entered the Buddha-dharma, they still give rise to great arrogance; they conceive the notion of attainment regarding what has not been attained, and they conceive the notion of knowledge regarding what has not been known, failing to practice within the Dharma of the Tathāgata."

"Although one may accord with the Four Noble Truths, one cannot attain the four kinds of unimpeded knowledge, nor can one even attain the realization of the fourth fruit. At that time, the World-Honored One took up a garland of campaka flowers with both hands and made a great vow. 4. Jewel that Surpasses All Radiance.
From each and every jewel, a great radiance issued forth, illuminating this Sahā world in its entirety; having emerged, the light was cast into the void.
At that time, from within the flower garlands, these verses were spoken:
"Though one has shaved off beard and hair, the fetters are not removed; Though one wears dyed robes, one is not free from passion."
One who shows the Buddha as their teacher yet does not follow his instructions is a person who defiles the great assembly.
When the Tathāgata proclaims the True Dharma, if one cannot listen with a sincere heart,
such a person will not attain the true meaning and will likewise be unable to free themselves from all afflictions.
If one can perceive the true nature of phenomena, one can destroy ignorance and pride;
if one draws near to virtuous friends, such a person will swiftly attain the flavor of the nectar of immortality;
if one can revile the cycle of birth and death, then one shall be able to reach the further shore.
This person is fully endowed with precepts and great learning, And likewise possesses the accumulation of meditative concentration and wisdom.
If one wishes to destroy the demon of afflictions, To distance oneself from the demons of the aggregates and death,
And to subdue the celestial Māra and his retinue, One should always draw near to the Unsurpassed Honored One.
Having spoken this verse, those śrāvaka disciples who possessed pride all thought to themselves:
"The Tathāgata knows that we all have defiled minds; for this reason, he has spoken such a verse for our sake."
Immediately, great shame and remorse arose within his heart;
likewise, the disciples of the Buddhas throughout the four continents also gave rise to such feelings of shame and remorse, and in a single moment of thought, they all assembled together.
At that time, an immeasurable assembly of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of śrāvakas gathered together.
Thereupon, the Buddha, knowing that the assembly was settled, immediately proclaimed for them the mixed Four Noble Truths.

At that time, this jewel garland proceeded directly toward the southern direction, passing through ninety-two thousand Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. There was a world there named Vajraprabhāgarbha, and the sentient beings in that land were fully possessed of the five corruptions.

There is a Buddha, a World-Honored One, named Vajraprabhāguṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, World-Honored One, who likewise proclaims for the fourfold assembly this Dharma of the mixed Four Noble Truths.

Then, within that assembly, there were various bodhisattvas and the fourfold community of śrāvakas—bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—who, having seen this great radiance of the jewel garland, looked toward the four directions.
Looking up, he saw a jeweled garland abiding in the space above the Buddha’s crown, and he addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
From where has this jeweled garland come?”
"By whom were you sent? That Buddha replied,
"O son of good family!"
To the north of here, beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of ninety-two thousand Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Sahā.

There dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān. He likewise expounds and reveals the mixed Four Noble Truths for sentient beings possessed of the five corruptions, no differently than I do now in this land.

“Good son! All sentient beings in that buddha-world are profoundly ignorant and dark, coarse and violent, fickle and flighty, giving rise to great arrogance, frequently committing evil deeds, and being difficult to discipline or transform. For this reason, Śākyamuni Tathāgata has convened this great assembly and expounds the True Dharma within it in order to destroy such great evils.”

All sentient beings in that world conceive the notion of attainment regarding what has not been attained, the notion of realization regarding what has not been realized, and the notion of cultivation regarding what has not been cultivated.

Therefore, that Buddha preached the Dharma for the great assembly; practicing in accordance with the Dharma, he did so in order to destroy such great arrogance, to attain the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) and the knowledge of non-arising (*anutpādajñāna*), and intending to proclaim the practice of the Dharma known as the "Eye of Space" (*ākāśanetra*).
In order to attain the fruits of the Śrāvaka, Pratyekabuddha, and Buddha, and desiring to open the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed Dharma-treasury,
that Buddha has sent this jewel-garland to me, seeking my consent.
I now give this to you, and I also wish to present this Dhāraṇī of the Dharma-Eye as a token of faith.

It can produce immeasurable, subtle, and wondrous great light; it can dry up all evil afflictions; it can maintain all that is heard so that it is never forgotten; it can purify all defilements of the mind; it can protect all wholesome precepts and prohibitions; it can cause one to enter into all great wisdom; it can protect all unsurpassed samādhis; it can protect one’s own mind and generate a heart of joy in others; by receiving and upholding the noble Dharma, one remains far removed from all illnesses, and whatever Dharma one seeks shall be obtained immediately according to one's wishes.

It increases all necessities of life and can also nurture all roots of goodness; it can subdue evil kings and the four castes, as well as all malevolent spirits, birds, beasts, and aquatic creatures; it protects and sustains all roots of virtue, enables one to attain all the dharmas of the Tathāgata, and even enables one to attain the eighteen unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*).
"Therefore, I now wish to dispatch this Dharma-eye Dhāraṇī to that world to be given to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
He then addressed the youth Vajraparvata, saying: "Noble son!..."

"You should go to that Sahā world and, in my name, inquire after the health of that Buddha, the Tathāgata Vajraprabhāśrīguṇa. Present this Dharani-door of Dharmamukha as a gift from afar to the World-Honored One."
The youth Vajraśikhara said:
“World-Honored One!
Excellent, excellent!”
"I also wish to go and pay homage to that Buddha, and furthermore, I wish to receive and learn the Dharma-gate of the Eye of Space, which I have never heard before.
At that time, there were also sixty trillion bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and eighty thousand koṭis of the great assembly of śrāvakas who spoke with one voice:
"World-Honored One!..."

We, too, wish to go to that world to pay our respects and behold that Buddha, and furthermore, we wish to receive and accept the "Dharma-gate of the Eye of Space" (Gagananetra-dharmaparyāya), which we have never heard before. We only pray that the Tathāgata will bestow upon us his supernormal power so that we may travel there and return.
That Buddha replied: "Excellent, excellent,
sons of good family!"
