There was a son of heaven named Mahāsammata, whose physical appearance was peerless and handsome, and who possessed brilliant wisdom and intelligence. He practiced and transformed others through the True Dharma; he constantly delighted in stillness and detachment from worldly glory, and was thus revered and looked up to by all the people, who paid him homage and attended upon him with respect.

That Samata was pure in his compassion and mercy, regarding all sentient beings with pity as if they were his own newborn infants; he took no pleasure in passionate attachment and constantly maintained his own purity.

The king had a consort who was excessively greedy for sensual desire; since the king had passed away, she found no way to satisfy her heart. Once, while wandering through a garden, she rested alone beneath a tree to amuse herself, where she saw a donkey whose sexual organs were exposed; her lustful mind being aroused, she stripped off her clothes and approached it.

Upon seeing him, the donkey immediately mated with him, and she subsequently conceived. When the months were complete, she gave birth to a son whose head, ears, mouth, and eyes all resembled those of a donkey; only his body was like that of a human, yet it was coarse and rough, and his shaggy hair covered his entire frame, no different from that of a beast.

When the lady saw this, her heart was struck with terror and fear; she immediately cast the child away into a secluded corner, but by the power of his merit, he remained suspended in mid-air without falling.
At that time, there was a rākṣasī named Assa-devī who, seeing the child was undefiled, thought to herself:
"A blessed child!"
Thereupon, he caught [the infant] in mid-air, washed and cared for it, and took it to the Snowy Mountains (Himavat) to nourish and raise it, treating it no differently than his own son.
When the child reached maturity, he taught him to take elixirs of the immortals (rasāyana), and they wandered together day and night with celestial youths.

"Furthermore, there was another Great Deva who also came to protect this child. His food, drink, sweet fruits, and medicinal herbs caused his body to undergo a transformation; adorned with merit, he shone with a great light. Thus, the assembly of devas collectively praised him and named him the Great Seer and Sage Kalāśīta (in the language of Sui, 'Donkey-Lipped')."

By these causes and conditions, within that Snowy Mountain and in all other places, there were produced through transformation various excellent flowers, various excellent fruits, various excellent medicines, various excellent fragrances, various clear streams, and various harmonious birds; wherever they traveled or dwelt, everything was abundant. Through the causal conditions of being sustained by these medicinal fruits, their other coarse physical features were all transformed so that their bodies became upright and handsome, with the sole exception that their lips resembled those of a donkey; therefore, he was named the Rishi Donkey-Lipped.
"This Donkey Seer studied the noble Dharma; for sixty thousand years he stood upon one foot, never lowering it day or night, without a single thought of weariness.

When the gods beheld the Great Seer’s such asceticism, the hosts of Brahmās, Śakra, and others from the desire and form realms above all gathered together to pay homage and make offerings. Even the hosts of nāgas, asuras, and yakṣas assembled like clouds, and all the seers and sages who practiced the holy life came to this side of the Holy Donkey."
They made various offerings, praising and extolling him, saying:
"Such ascetic practices as these have never been seen since birth.
Having presented their offerings, they joined their palms and asked:
“Great Seer and Holy One, what do you seek?
We pray that you will tell us, all of us devas; if it is within our power, we shall grant it to you immediately and will never be stingy.”
At that time, having heard these words, the donkey-lipped one felt joy in his heart and replied to the devas:
"If you can truly fulfill what my heart desires, I shall now speak briefly."

I recall my past lives; in a kalpa of the past, I saw in the void of space the various constellations, the sun, the moon, and the five planets, moving day and night, each maintaining its regular course, providing illumination for the world beneath.
I desire to fully understand the discernment and comprehension of consciousness; out of compassion for those in the darkness of ignorance, I do not shrink from toil.

At the beginning of this Bhadrakalpa, such things did not exist. You gods, nāgas, and spirits have all come out of pity for me; I pray that you will explain the methods and applications of the stars, sun, and moon, just as they were established and arranged in the past, and how they were fashioned for convenience, including their auspicious and inauspicious, good and bad qualities—explain them all completely according to my wish.
All the devas said: "O Great Virtuous Seer!
This matter is exceedingly profound and is not within our domain."
"If you would out of compassion for all sentient beings speak quickly yourself, as was done in the past.
At that time, the ṛṣi Kharoṣṭha addressed all the devas, saying:
"The first constellation established was Kṛttikā; the multitude of stars revolve and circulate through space."
He addressed the assembly of devas:
"Is it correct that you say the Kṛttikās are the first?
At that time, the Sun Deva spoke these words:

"This constellation Kṛttikā constantly traverses the void and passes through the four continents, always performing good deeds to benefit us; I know that this constellation belongs to the Fire Deity."
At that time, there was a noble one among the assembly named Mahātejas, who spoke again as follows:

"That Kṛttikā is the son of my sister; its star has six points shaped like razors. In one day and one night, it traverses the four continents for thirty muhūrtas. It belongs to the deity Agni, its lineage is Vaiyānī, and those belonging to that lunar mansion should offer curd as a sacrifice."
The Ṛṣi Kharoṣṭha said to the devas: "So it is, so it is;
as you have said, I now take the lunar mansion Mṛgaśiras as the first."
"Furthermore, setting aside the previous, the constellation Bharaṇī is the second lunar mansion. It belongs to Varuṇa, and its clan name is Bharadvāja.
Bharaṇī consists of five stars shaped like a trident; it moves for forty-five *muhūrtas* in one day and night. For those belonging to the Bharaṇī mansion, deer meat is used for the sacrifice."
"Furthermore, setting aside the previous, Jyeṣṭhā is established as the third lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*). It belongs to the Moon Deity; it is the son of the Moon, and his clan name is Vṛddhakāyani.

Its stars number three and its shape is like the head of a deer. It traverses fifteen *muhūrtas* in one day and one night. Those belonging to the Jyeṣṭhā mansion should offer sacrifices of roots and fruits."
"Next, the constellation *Ardra* is established as the fourth lunar mansion; it belongs to the Sun Deity (*Sūrya*), and its clan name is *Vasiṣṭha*.

Its nature is extremely fierce and prone to anger. It consists of a single star, shaped like a woman's mole. It traverses forty-five *muhūrta*s in one day and night. For those belonging to the *Ardra* mansion, clarified butter (*ghṛta*) is used for the sacrifice."
"Next, the well (Puṣya) is established as the fifth lunar mansion; it belongs to the Sun Deity (Sūrya), and its lineage is Vasiṣṭha.

It consists of two stars shaped like footprints. It traverses fifteen muhūrtas in one day and one night. Those who belong to the Puṣya mansion should offer an oblation of *śāli* rice flowers mixed with honey."

"Next, the constellation of Ghosts (Kṛttikā) is established as the sixth lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity of Jupiter, is the son of Jupiter, and his family name is Pāvana; his nature is gentle, and he delights in practicing wholesome dharmas."

There are three stars that resemble the mark of fullness upon the chests of the Buddhas; they travel for thirty periods in one day and night. Those belonging to the lunar mansion of Ghosts (Kṛttikā) should also be worshipped with offerings of non-glutinous rice flowers mixed with honey.
"Next, Liu (Willow) is established as the seventh lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity of the Snake and thus takes the surname She (Snake).
It consists of a single star, appearing like a woman's mole. It traverses fifteen *muhūrta* in one day and one night. Those belonging to the Liu mansion should use milk porridge for their offerings."
These seven lunar mansions mentioned above belong to the eastern gate.
"Next, place the first mansion of the south, named Saptarṣi; it belongs to the deity Agni, and its clan name is Piṅgāyani."

If there are five stars shaped like a riverbank that traverse thirty *shí* in one day and one night, they belong to the Seven Stars (*Saptarṣi*). For such a case, it is appropriate to offer a porridge made of non-glutinous rice and black sesame as a sacrifice.
"Next, Zhang (Jyeṣṭhā) is established as the second lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity Puṇyabhadra and its clan name is Gautamī.

Its constellation consists of two stars shaped like footprints. It moves for thirty muhūrtas in one day and one night. Those who belong to the Zhang mansion should use the bilva fruit to perform their offerings."
"Next, Yi (Wing) is established as the third lunar mansion; it belongs to the Forest Deity, and its clan name is Kauṇḍinya.

It consists of two stars shaped like footprints. It traverses fifteen muhūrtas in one day and one night. Those who belong to the Yi mansion should offer a sacrifice of raw green beans and black beans that have been thoroughly cooked."
"Next, the asterism Zhěn (Jyeṣṭhā) is established as the fourth lunar mansion. It belongs to the deity Śavitrīdeva; his clan name is Kātyāyana, and he is the son of the Seer Śaka.

This star consists of five stars shaped like a human hand; it traverses thirty muhūrtas in one day and night. Those who belong to the asterism Zhěn should prepare a meal of wild grass and barnyard millet to offer in sacrifice."
"Next, the constellation *Viśākhā* is established as the fifth lunar mansion. It belongs to the Heaven of Joy (*Nandana*), its clan name is *Citrarathāyanī*, and it is the son of a *Gandharva*.
It consists of a single star, shaped like a woman’s mole. It traverses fifteen *muhūrtas* in one day and night. Those who belong to *Viśākhā* should offer various flower-rice as a sacrifice."
"Next, the constellation Kṛttikā is established as the sixth lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity Maṅgala, and its clan name is Kātyāyanī.

It consists of one star, shaped like a woman’s mole, and it traverses fifteen muhūrtas in one day and night. Those who belong to the Kṛttikā mansion should take mung beans, mix them with ghee and honey, boil them, and use this to perform the sacrifice."
"Next, the constellation *Jyeṣṭhā* is established as the seventh lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity Agni, and its clan name is Kṣitiguptāyani.

The constellation *Jyeṣṭhā* consists of two stars shaped like footprints; it traverses forty-five *muhūrtas* in one day and one night. Those who belong to the *Jyeṣṭhā* mansion should take various kinds of flowers, prepare them as food, and offer them in sacrifice."
These seven lunar mansions above should be assigned to the southern gate.
"Next, place the first mansion of the western direction; its name is Ping (房), belonging to the deity Maitreya, and its clan name is Ālambāyanī.

The constellation Fang (Heart) has four stars and is shaped like a jeweled necklace; it travels for thirty muhūrtas in one day and one night. Those belonging to the Fang mansion should offer wine and meat as sacrifice.
Next, the Xin (Mind) is established as the second mansion; it belongs to Śakra Devendra, and its clan name is Kālayana.

The Heart constellation has three stars shaped like barley grains; it traverses fifteen muhūrtas in one day and night. Those who belong to the Heart constellation should offer an oblation of non-glutinous rice gruel.
"Next, Mūla is established as the third lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity Mṛgaśiras, and its clan name is Kātyāyana.

The constellation Mūla consists of seven stars shaped like the tail of a scorpion. It traverses thirty muhūrtas in one day and night. Those who belong to the Mūla asterism should offer a sacrifice of various fruits and roots."
"Next, the constellation *Mṛgaśiras* is established as the fourth lunar mansion; it belongs to Varuṇa, and its clan name is Takṣakācāyani.

*Mṛgaśiras* consists of four stars shaped like the horns of a bull; it traverses thirty *muhūrtas* in one day and night. Those who belong to the *Mṛgaśiras* mansion should take the sap of *nyagrodha* bark to offer as a sacrifice."
"Next, the *Dō* (Ursa Major) is established as the fifth lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity Agni, and its clan name is Moga-rāṇi.

The *Dō* consists of four stars, shaped like a person leveling the ground; it traverses forty-five *ghaṭikās* in one day and night. Those belonging to the *Dō* mansion should offer an oblation of fine rice flour mixed with honey."
"Next, the constellation of the Ox (Go) is established as the sixth lunar mansion; it belongs to Brahmā, and its clan name is Brahmarma.

It consists of three stars shaped like the head of an ox, and it traverses the six periods of the day and night. Those belonging to the Ox mansion should offer an oblation of clarified butter (ghṛta) and rice for their worship."
"Next, the Nakṣatra of the Woman (Strī) is established as the seventh lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity Viṣṇu, and its clan name is Tārikācāyani.

The Woman has four stars, shaped like grains of barley, and it traverses thirty muhūrtas in one day and night. Those who belong to the Nakṣatra of the Woman should offer the flesh of birds as a sacrifice."
The above seven lunar mansions correspond to the western gate.
"Next, place the first mansion of the north, named the Void (Śravaṇā) Star; it belongs to Śakra-devendra, the Son of Heaven of Sahā, whose family name is Kauṇḍinya."

The constellation Xū (Void) consists of four stars, shaped like a crow; it traverses thirty muhūrtas in one day and night. Those belonging to the Xū mansion should offer a sacrifice using the decoction of black beans.
"Next, Bharaṇī is established as the second lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity Tāraṇa, and its clan name is Caṇḍanī.

Bharaṇī consists of one star, shaped like a woman's mole, and it traverses fifteen muhūrtas in one day and night. Those belonging to the Bharaṇī mansion should offer a sacrifice of non-glutinous rice porridge."
"Next, Śravaṇā is established as the third lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity Śiraścaṇḍa, the son of the deity Vṛścika, and its clan name is Jātukaṇi.
Śravaṇā consists of two stars shaped like footprints; it traverses thirty muhūrtas in one day and night. Those who belong to the Śravaṇā mansion should offer a sacrifice of flesh and blood."
"Next, *Bhava* is established as the fourth lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*). *Bhava* belongs to the forest deity (*vanadevatā*), its son is Varuṇa, and its clan name is Dhanaja.

*Bhava* consists of two stars shaped like footprints; it traverses its course in forty-five *muhūrtas* during one day and night. Those who belong to the *Bhava* star should offer a sacrifice of meat to it."
"Next, place the lunar mansion Revatī as the fifth; it belongs to the deity Puṣya, and its clan name is Āśvalāyana.
Revatī consists of one star, shaped like a woman’s mole, and it traverses thirty muhūrtas in one day and night. Those belonging to the Revatī mansion should offer curd as a sacrifice."
"Next, Lou (Aśvinī) is established as the sixth lunar mansion; it belongs to the Gandharva devas, and its clan name is Aśvapati.

Lou consists of three stars shaped like the head of a horse; it traverses thirty muhūrtas in one day and night. Those who belong to the Lou mansion should offer an oblation of barley rice together with meat."
"Next, the constellation Wei (Ursa Major) is established as the seventh lunar mansion; it belongs to the deity Yama, and its clan name is Bhāgavi.

The Wei mansion consists of three stars shaped like the legs of a tripod. It traverses thirty muhūrtas in one day and one night. Those who belong to the Wei mansion should offer sacrifices of non-glutinous rice, black sesame, and wild jujubes."
The above seven lunar mansions correspond to the northern gate.
"Of the twenty-eight lunar mansions, there are five that traverse forty-five muhūrtas, namely: Bi (Jyeṣṭhā), Shen (Āśleṣā), Di (Vṛṣabha), Dou (Uttarā-bhādrapadā), and Pi (Pūrvā-bhādrapadā)."

“The meanings and principles of the twenty-eight lunar mansions are vast and manifold; their profound significance is difficult to comprehend and cannot be fully proclaimed. I shall now explain them briefly.
When he spoke these words regarding the lunar mansions, all the devas who heard it together were filled with joy.
Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra, Scroll 41. Mahāvaipulya Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra, Scroll 42.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui Dynasty.
The Eighth Chapter of the Sūryagarbha-parivarta, "On the Constellations," Part Two.
At that time, the ṛṣi Śuci-rasmi addressed the devas, saying:

"This ṛṣi Khaṇḍa-dravya also committed evil karma in past lives; due to the causes and conditions of those sins, although he obtained a human body, half of it was in the form of a donkey. However, through the power of his compassion, his sin was extinguished, and he further obtained a most excellent and upright body, just like that of Śakra."
He addressed the nāgas and others, saying:
"By virtue of my merit and various causes and conditions, I am like that rishi, acting as a guide for all the devas.
Now it is likewise; I am able to teach you profound and true speech."
"O Nāgas, you should know!
When Kharoṣṭha had assumed a body resembling that of Śakra, the assembly of devas and humans were all filled with joy; with single-minded devotion they joined their palms and spoke thus:
'Now the Great Sage has recounted for us the events of the past: which constellation was foremost in its movement?'"
What food do you eat?
What work do you perform?
And for how long do you travel through the void?
Having been asked thus, the seer replied: "All of you, listen with a sincere heart.

By the power of my compassion, I have regained my physical beauty; now, out of pity for the peace and security of sentient beings, I shall recount from beginning to end the events of one year, so that you who are like the blind may regain your sight."

From the first day of the lunar month through the full moon, I have fully explained the positions of all the constellations. For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, I have placed the Kṛttikā constellation at the forefront of all the stars; do you gods consider this to be so?
All the devas said: "Excellent, excellent!

We have traversed the constellations and know that Mṛgaśiras is the nephew of the most honored and majestic deity; it has six sons who traverse the void. Therefore, Mṛgaśiras should be made the foremost."
The Ṛṣi Kharoṣṭha said: "When the moon conjoins with the various lunar mansions, it begins at Kṛttikā and ends at Āśleṣā;

once the moon has completed its course through the asterisms, one month is nearly full. In the first day of the dark fortnight of the eighth month, the moon conjoins with Maghā; thus it revolves in succession without ceasing."
I shall now further explain the number of kṣaṇas: one thousand six hundred kṣaṇas constitute one kāla; sixty kālas constitute one muhūrta; and thirty muhūrtas make up one day and night.

“The constellation Āśleṣā acts with unrestrained malice like the god Śiva, yet it is able to protect the four quarters so that all attain peace and security. You gods and humans, seeing him commit evil, should not feel resentment or wonder; for he strictly administers laws and punishments precisely to protect sentient beings.”
All the devas said: "So it is, so it is; it is as the Holy One has taught.
By being strict in the laws and regulations, one brings salvation to sentient beings."

"When the moon is in conjunction with the lunar mansion Mṛgaśiras, those who fall ill on this day may suffer either lightly or heavily, making them difficult to treat. Those born on this day are generally prone to anger and indignation; they are fierce, cruel, and resolute, making them difficult to befriend. Yet, they will attain high official rank and be able to overcome all beings."

During the days of the four lunar mansions—Jie (Kang), Xu (Xū), Shén (Shēn), and Wèi (Wèi)—one must not enter battle or engage in combat, nor undertake long journeys; furthermore, one must not shave the head or trim the beard.
On the days of the three lunar mansions Pi (畢), Niu (牛), and Zhen (軫), it is appropriate for combat, as well as for traveling afar, shaving the head, and washing the head.
On the days of the lunar mansions Liu (柳) and Zhang (張), one may undertake the performance of all various activities.

On the days of the lunar mansions Pleiades (Mṛgaśiras), Swan’s Wing (Śravaṇā), and Dipper (Dhaniṣṭhā), one may obtain wealth; it is appropriate to take medicine, observe the precepts, and practice generosity, as well as to make new clothes and fashion necklaces.
On the days of the lunar mansions of Beak (Jǐ), Horn (Jiǎo), Woman (Nǚ), and Seven Stars (Qīxīng)—these four mansions—it is auspicious for travel and movement, ensuring safety and peace on the roads.
On the days of the mansions of Base (Dǐ), Well (Jǐng), and Perilous (Wēi)—these three mansions—one may achieve success even when performing evil deeds.

On the days of the lunar mansions of Pi (Hāng), Mūla (Liǔ), Herzog (Xīn), Ārdrā (Lóu), Śravaṇa (Qīxīng), and Viśākhā (Zhāng)—these six mansions—one may construct carriages, beds, and rope-seated couches, as well as various garments; furthermore, it is essential to establish friendships and alliances.

“Kṛttikā performs various activities with great swiftness; its speed is like that of fire. One who falls ill on this day is cured in four days by offering curd-rice as a sacrifice. Those born on this day will always attain great wealth, and on this day one enters the womb.”

On the days of the lunar mansions Dou (Dhruva), Fang (Rohiṇī), Xū (Śravaṇā), Liù (Śraviṣṭhā), and Shì (Bharaṇī), it is inauspicious to undertake any activities; one may only engage in battle against a great enemy.
Regarding the lunar mansions of Jing (井), Di (氐), and Yi (翼): on the days of these three mansions, all matters, whether good or evil, may be undertaken.
On the day of Bi (畢) as well, one may act with full autonomy.

Regarding the three mansions of Jing (井), Di (氐), and Wei (危): on the days of these three mansions, those born under the mansion of Mao (昴) must not undertake any affairs, travel far, or engage in combat; even in cases of urgent necessity, they must not act.

The three lunar mansions of Nü (女), Jiǎo (角), and Zǐ (觜) are also most inauspicious on their respective days; however, on the day of Yì (翼), one who fights with an enemy will achieve victory, and whether through force or gentleness, reconciliation will be brought about.

On the days of the lunar mansions Jyeṣṭhā and Rohiṇī, one will not find companions; however, the administration of medicine, the compounding of medicines, leaving the household life, giving alms, and the making of new clothing, necklaces, beds, seats, bedding, and other such articles will all be successfully accomplished.
On the days of the lunar mansions Aśvinī, Śravaṇā, and Rohiṇī, one’s travels and arrivals will be peaceful and secure.
On the days of the lunar mansions Mūla, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, and Bharaṇī, one may engage in various evil deeds with others and depart from a mind of loving-kindness.

On the days of the seven lunar mansions—Jyeṣṭhā, Mūla, Rohiṇī, Śravaṇā, and Āśleṣā—it is auspicious to contract marriages, to construct carriages and beds, and likewise for other furnishings. It is also auspicious to undertake tasks on the day of the Ārdrā mansion; however, in all such matters, one must give rise to compassion.

“The constellation Revatī is of the nature of water. On this second lunar mansion day, you shall accomplish all gentle deeds with complete harmony. Those who are ill and offer incense into the fire on this day will recover after five days. Those born under this constellation will be greatly wealthy, possessed of merit, and delight in the Dharma.”

If one conceives on the days of the Ox (Go), the Quail (Kwei), the Seven Stars (Shih-ch'ing), or the Heart (Hsin) lunar mansions, that person will be of meager virtue and constantly perform lowly tasks.

On the days of the Ghost (Kuei), the Tail (Wei), and the Room (Shih)—these three lunar mansions—one must not undertake any enterprise whatsoever; one must not engage in battle, travel far, or go before the authorities. One must also refrain from buying and selling, trading, or performing any craft or labor.
On the days of the lunar mansions Kṛttikā and Śravaṇā, if one undertakes auspicious deeds, they will not result in harmony; these days are suitable only for battle and achieving victory.
On the day of the mansion Ārdrā, undertaking affairs is beneficial; it is advantageous for performing gentle acts and there will be no obstacles.
On days of the lunar mansions Jyeṣṭhā (Zǐ), Viśākhā (Jiǎo), and Anurādhā (Nǚ), all matters are harmonious; whatever one undertakes will be accomplished, and taking medicine will bring efficacy.
If one wishes to practice giving, or to make clothing and necklaces, all such tasks may be performed.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Jing (井), Di (氐), and Wei (危), traveling far away will be peaceful and secure.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Fang (房), Liu (柳), and Bi (辟), one who wishes to depart from a compassionate heart and commit evil will succeed.

On the days of these six lunar mansions—the Dou (Dipper), Ji (Winnowing Basket), Lou (Maiden), Wei (Stomach), Shi (Room), and Yi (Wings)—it is auspicious to form friendships, celebrate marriages, gather with acquaintances, and construct beds, shops, carriages, and litters.

"When the four days of the *Jyeṣṭhā* lunar mansion preside over affairs, all undertakings in this world will quickly and spontaneously succeed. On those days, a sick person may offer a porridge of beans to the moon on the eighth day, and shall be cured."

Those born on this day will be fierce and robust, possessing great wealth and abundance; they should guard themselves against encountering various misfortunes caused by women, for what I say is not false.

For those born under the *Jiǎoxiù* (Beak) lunar mansion, if they enter the womb on days corresponding to the *Nǚxiù*, *Lóuxiù*, *Dòuxiù*, or *Zhāngxiù* mansions, it is considered evil and unfavorable.

On days of the three mansions—*Máoxiù*, *Fángxiù*, and *Liǔxiù*—one must not engage in battle, undertake long journeys, or go before government officials; if one must travel for necessity, one should desist and not go.

On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Jyeṣṭhā, Viśākhā, and Ārdrā, one may commit various evils; through such discordant acts, false speech, flattery, and the intent to kill an enemy, all shall be accomplished.

On the day of the lunar mansion Jiao (角宿), those who wish to undertake an enterprise will find both the firm and the yielding to be favorable. On the day of the lunar mansion Shen (參宿), undertaking an enterprise brings benefit and can lead to mastery.

The two mansions Kang (亢) and Xu (虛) are not in harmony; however, on the day of Shen, one obtains benefit. On that day, it is appropriate to take medicine, leave the household life, practice charity, and fashion necklaces and garments.
Traveling on days associated with the lunar mansions of Ārdrā, Svāti, and Uttarabhādrapadā ensures safety and well-being.
On the days of the three mansions—Punarvasu, Rohiṇī, and Śatabhiṣaj—whoever intends to commit evil will have their wicked deeds succeed.

On the days of the lunar mansions Zhèn (Jyeṣṭhā), Wèi (Anurādhā), Bì (Pūrvabhādrapadā), Niú (Vṛṣabha), and Jī (Śravaṇā), it is auspicious to form friendships, acquire good spiritual teachers, and perform matters concerning marriage; likewise, one may successfully construct carriages, beds, and curtains.

“On the five days governed by the *Aśvinī* mansion, one is able to accomplish various evils; those who wish to engage in undertakings will receive little benefit. If one falls ill on this day, offering a porridge of fresh ghee at the four crossroads will lead to recovery within ten days.
Those born on this day, though naturally intelligent, harbor evil intentions in their hearts; they pursue wealth until they reach death, and they often become thieves who lose their lives.

For those born on this day or entering the womb during this time, as well as on the days of the *Śravaṇā*, *Hṛdaya*, *Bharaṇī*, *Śatatabhiṣaj*, *Āśleṣā*, and *Revatī* mansions—these six mansions bring many obstacles. Furthermore, on days such as *Pūrvabhādrapadā*, *Uttarabhādrapadā*, and *Rohiṇī*, there is no harmony; no matters whatsoever should be undertaken.”
On a day of the lunar mansion Kṛttikā (Káng), those who wish to undertake a task should do so for a minor matter.
On the days of the four mansions Vṛṣabha (Dǐ), Āśleṣā (Wēi), Pūrvāṣāḍhā (Jǐng), and Rohiṇī (Kuǐ), one may act with full autonomy.

"When the constellation Jyeṣṭhā presides for six days, it determines and adjudicates the results of evil karma. If one falls ill on this day, one should offer parched non-glutinous rice flowers as a sacrifice to the Sun Deity; recovery will be attained on the eighth day."

For those born on this day or who conceive on this day, it is auspicious to engage in agricultural work, as they shall attain great wealth and abound in livestock such as elephants, horses, and sheep; however, on the day of the *Bhava* asterism, nothing is favorable for any undertaking.
On the days of the lunar mansions Wei (柳) and Fang (房), the performance of various undertakings will mostly result in waste and dissipation.
On the day of Di (氐), it is auspicious to engage in all manner of activities; they will proceed according to one's wishes with ease and mastery.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Ārdrā, Pūrvaphalgunī, and Svāti, it is auspicious to undertake all matters; whatever one seeks shall accord with one's wishes.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Hasta, Jyeṣṭhā, and Rohiṇī, it is auspicious to travel far; one’s journey will be secure and one’s endeavors will meet with harmony.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Dou (Dipper), Yi (Wing), and Kui (Quail), it is auspicious to form friendships and seek spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
On the four mansions of Kang (Neck), Bi (Net), Zi (Mouth), and Xu (Emptiness), these days create various obstacles for those born under the well (*jing*) mansion.

"When the lunar mansion Mṛgaśiras presides over the seven-day period, one can become gentle and unbreakable in the wholesome Dharma; if one falls ill on that day, one should offer yellow honey to Jupiter, and within five days, one will recover."

One born on this day observes the precepts and delights in virtuous deeds; they shall attain high official rank as a national teacher or a prime minister, constantly instructing kings in the governance of the world through righteous laws. However, regarding marriage, it is particularly difficult for them to find harmony; only after diligent efforts through the mediation of others will they achieve success.
For those born on these days, it is auspicious to conceive on the days of the lunar mansions Śravaṇā, Ārdrā, Śatabhīṣaj, Rohiṇī, and Āśleṣā.
The three lunar mansions of Pūrvaphalgunī, Viśākhā, and Anurādhā constitute obstacles for them.
On days of the Heart (Hṛdayā), Kṛttikā, or Rohiṇī constellations, undertakings will not succeed and one shall lose wealth.
On days of the Tail (Mūla) constellation, undertakings will succeed, and on days of the Room (Mṛgaśiras) constellation, there will likewise be much benefit.
The lunar mansions Bi (Jyeṣṭhā) and Liù (Anurādhā)—on the days of these two mansions, undertakings will not be successful.
On the day of Zhāng (Śravaṇā), traveling far away will be peaceful and secure.
The mansions Lóu (Aśvinī) and Jī (Pūrvaphalgunī) will act as obstacles.
The lunar mansions of Jyeṣṭhā, Vṛṣabha, and Mṛgaśiras: undertaking tasks on the days of these three mansions will result in harmony and the certain attainment of excellent companions.
The mansions of Rohiṇī, Śravaṇa, Maghā, and Śatabhiṣaj are suitable for forming friendships and associating with virtuous spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
Regarding the lunar mansions of Kṛttikā and Ārdrā: on the days of these two mansions, whatever one seeks will yield much benefit.
"When the eighth day of the mansion of Śravaṇā presides, all manner of evil deeds can be performed; within the world, one is like King Yama. On this day, those who are ill cannot be cured.

Those born on this day are by nature prone to anger and lack compassion; they commit many transgressions and are hated and envied by others. They are capable of destroying wholesome dharmas and always take pleasure in hunting."
The constellations Bi (Bharaṇī) and Niu (Kṛttikā)—on the days of these two constellations, entering the womb is auspicious.
The constellations Zhen (Anurādhā) and Mao (Mṛgaśiras)—for those entering the womb on these days, it is inauspicious.

The constellations Zi (Śravaṇā), Xu (Śatabhiṣaj), Kang (Rohiṇī), and Zhang (Pūrvabhādrapadā)—on the days of these four constellations, one should not undertake any affairs, as there will be much waste and dissipation.
On the days of the lunar mansions Jishi (Jyeṣṭhā), Louxiu (Rohiṇī), and Fangxiu (Anurādhā), it is auspicious to perform various undertakings, which will achieve excellent success.
On the day of Xinxiu (Śravaṇā), Qixingxiu (Aśvinī), and Weixiu (Ārdrā), traveling far away will be peaceful and secure.
On the days of the lunar mansions of Yi (Jyeṣṭhā), Dou (Uttarabhadrapadā), and Nü (Rohiṇī), it is appropriate to cultivate study and achieve mastery in the arts.
On the days of the five lunar mansions of Jiao (Aśvinī), Dou (Uttarabhadrapadā), Wei (Śatabhiṣaj), Wei (Mūla), and Bi (Pūrvaphalgunī), it is appropriate to form friendships.
Regarding the lunar mansions of Di (氐), Shen (參), Jing (井), and Shi (室)—on these four days, it is likewise appropriate to form bonds with spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).

"The seven stars and nine days exercise their influence; toward all sentient beings they are mild and gentle. On those days, if one who is ill offers a sacrifice to their ancestors with sesame oil and *śāli* rice, they will recover on the eighth day.

Those born on these days are intelligent and possessed of merit, and always perform virtuous deeds; however, such people are by nature somewhat prone to false speech. If they would protect themselves, they should be careful to avoid lying; the undertakings of such a person will be successful."
Those who conceive on the days of the Heart (Hṛdayā), Sun (Sūrya), or Base (Jyeṣṭhā) lunar mansions will be impoverished and possess few material goods.
Those who conceive on the days of the Three Stars (Pūrva-phalgunī), Peril (Ārdrā), or Net (Pūrvā-bhādrapadā) lunar mansions will meet with misfortune and constantly engage in evil deeds.
If one conceives on the days of the lunar mansions Jyeṣṭhā and Rohiṇī, one will be poor and inclined toward evil deeds.
If one conceives on the days of the three lunar mansions Śatabhīṣaj, Ārdrā, and Dhanisthā, one will act with autonomy and obtain the property of others.
On the days of the lunar mansions Lou (Lubitha), Zhang (Jyeshthā), and Ji (Pūrvaphalgunī), those who wish to undertake tasks will encounter many obstacles.
On the days of the four mansions Zhen (Chitrā), Niu (Vr̥ṣabha), Mao (Rohiṇī), and Di (Mṛgaśiras), travel and arrival are peaceful, and undertakings will be harmonious.
The lunar mansions Xū (虛) and Zǐ (觜)—on the days of these two mansions, there will be obstacles.

"When the mansion Zhāng (張) presides over the day on the tenth, it performs gentle deeds and brings peace to the world; those who are ill on that day should offer *bimba* fruit and fresh ghee to the deity, and they will recover within seven days."

Those born on this day are by nature fond of fragrant scents, garments, and necklaces; they crave sensual pleasures and have a penchant for wine, and thus must exercise self-restraint and vigilance when among the multitude.
The lunar mansions Lou (Lubetha) and Jing (Jyeṣṭhā)—on the days of these two mansions, conception is most inauspicious.
The mansions Xu (Anurādhā), Kang (Ardra), and Zi (Mūla)—conception on the days of these three mansions is also inauspicious and unsuitable for undertaking any affairs.
The days of the three lunar mansions—Pleiades (Mao), the Rear Cart (Zhen), and Ox (Niu)—are also characterized by many obstacles.
On the day of the Net (Zhang) mansion, one attains mastery.
On the days of the Stomach (Wei) and the Dipper (Dou) mansions, those who seek something will not obtain it as they wish.
On the day of the lunar mansion Di (Jyeṣṭhā), those who have conceived can eliminate obstacles.
On the days of the four lunar mansions—Kang (Ārdrā), Can (Aśvinī), Bi (Pūrvaphalgunī), and Nü (Anurādhā)—traveling afar will be peaceful and secure.
On the days of the lunar mansions Anurādhā, Śravaṇā, Ārdrā, Hṛdaya, Kṛttikā, and Abhijit, one who wishes to form a spiritual bond will encounter obstacles and fail to achieve it.

"When the constellation *Śraviṣṭhā* governs on the eleventh day, it performs two kinds of activities throughout the four continents: namely, deceitful crookedness and gentle flexibility. If one falls ill on this day, one should cook black or blue beans to offer as a sacrifice to the deities;

recovery will occur on the tenth day. Those born on this day are suitable for various endeavors, yet their nature is foolish; they are stingy, greedy, and miserly, unable to rejoice in giving. They may also fast for five, six, or even seven days. They are not loved by worldly people; one must be diligent in guarding against enemies and should avoid engaging in strife."
Those who enter the womb on the day of the lunar mansion Wei (胃) will mostly commit various evils.
On the days of the four mansions Wei (危), Shen (參), Di (氐), and Fang (房), both good and evil deeds may be performed.
On the day of the lunar mansion Fang (房), there is neither good nor evil.
On the days of the lunar mansions Bi (辟) and Gui (鬼), those who conceive on these two days will find it difficult to avoid losing their wealth and goods.

On the days of the three mansions Wei (胃), Lou (婁), and Dou (斗), those who conceive on these three days will have their undertakings harmoniously fulfilled. On the days of the three mansions Zhen (軫), Niu (牛), and Mao (昴), undertakings will likewise be brought to successful completion.
If one undertakes a task on the days of the lunar mansions Xū (虛), Zǐ (觜), or Kàng (亢), these three will succeed; by the power of these three mansions, one may travel far with safety and ease.
On the days of the mansions Jǐng (井), Shì (室), and Wěi (尾), there is neither good nor evil.

On the days of the lunar mansions Lou (Lubdhaka), Qi-xing (Saptarṣi), Kui (Kṛttikā), Liu (Anurādhā), and Xin (Hṛdaya), matters concerning the formation of spiritual friendships and marriage shall all achieve harmony.

"When the mansion Zhen (Jyeṣṭhā) presides over the day for twelve days, it acts as an evil sovereign, swift as the wind. If one falls ill on such a day, one should offer curd to the deity; the illness will be cured within five days.

Those born on this day will possess great wealth and abundance, being capable of using the five weapons—the sword, the spear, the bow and arrow, the battle discus, and the lasso—and they may become great thieves who harm sentient beings."

If one who cultivates goodness can also maintain the precepts and joyfully practice giving, performing all manner of meritorious deeds, then within seven paces of that person's path, even a snake will not dare to advance.
On the day of its entry into the womb, one becomes a leader among a host of thieves, yet is also able to maintain the precepts and take delight in the giving of alms.
On the day of the lunar mansion Mūla, the one who has entered the womb will encounter no obstacles wherever they may be; when entering battle to fight, they shall be victorious over their enemies.
On the days of the two lunar mansions, Well (Jing) and Room (Shi), those who have conceived should always engage in activities from birth until death.

On the days of the three mansions—Ox (Niu), Neck (Kang), and Void (Xu)—those who have conceived should engage in activities, with the sole exception that on the day of Ox (Niu), it is not suitable to do so.
Furthermore, on the days of the four lunar mansions—Jiao (亢), Xu (虛), Nü (女), and Zui (觜)—undertaking tasks will bring benefit and grant mastery.
On the days of the three mansions—Jiang (亢), Bi (畢), and Wei (危)—traveling to distant places will be peaceful and secure.

On the days of the lunar mansions Di (Jyeṣṭhā), Shen (Śravaṇā), Fang (Rohiṇī), and Bi (Pūrvaphalgunī), one may perform various activities to gain human vitality and strength; furthermore, it is auspicious for taking a wife, forming alliances with friends, and cultivating virtuous spiritual companions.

On the days of the six lunar mansions—Ji (Pūrvaphalgunī), Qīxīng (Uttarāṣāḍhā), Lóu (Pūrvabhādrapadā), Dòu (Śravaṇā), Zhāng (Śraviṣṭhā), and Wèi (Dhaniṣṭhā)—any undertaking performed will yield benefits as described above.
"When the thirteenth day of the Viśākhā lunar mansion is presiding, it is characterized by evil and rapidity.

If one falls ill on this day, one should remove the husks from mung beans (*mudga*), grind them raw, and offer them as a sacrifice to the deity; within six days, the illness will be cured. Those born under this asterism are capable of engaging in jesting, music, song, dance, and performance, and they are also able to practice renunciation and giving."
Furthermore, those who possess much lustful desire and likewise delight in those with knowledge should enter the womb on a day corresponding to the *Bharaṇī* lunar mansion;
those who enter the womb on days such as *Aśvinī*, *Śravaṇā*, or *Kṛttikā* will generally commit many evil deeds.
On days such as those of the lunar mansions Bi (Jyeṣṭhā), Fang (Vidhi), and Gui (Mūla), whatever tasks a person undertakes will all be auspicious and free from obstacles.
On days such as those of the lunar mansions Wei (Pūrvabhādrapadā), Di (Mṛgaśirā), and Can (Āśleṣā), if one engages in worldly affairs, one shall likewise attain mastery.
Traveling on days when the lunar mansions of Beizhu (Aśvinī), Jiangzhu (Ārdrā), Xuzhu (Śravaṇā), and Weizhu (Anurādhā) are prominent ensures safety and peace.
On days when Beizhu and Liuzhu (Śravaṇā) are prominent, those engaged in business affairs will gain the power of their associates.

The Heart (Jyeṣṭhā), Aquarius (Aśvinī), Dipper (Uttarabhadrapadā), Pleiades (Kṛttikā), Wing (Śravaṇā), Ox (Rohiṇī), and Banner (Pūrvaphalgunī) constellations—on the days of these seven constellations, it is auspicious to perform matters such as forming friendships and marriages.

"When the lunar mansion *Jyeṣṭhā* governs on the fourteenth day, it can cause various evil deeds to be committed in the world; its nature is swift and its actions are sharp and effective. If one contracts a disease on this day, it will be extremely severe and difficult to cure; by offering flowers and honey to the deities, one may finally recover on the twenty-fifth day."

Those born on this day are skilled at calculation and possess great wealth and abundance; however, they are by nature stingy and greedy, unable to give with joy, and are frequently prone to anger, making their minds difficult to manage.
If one sees a solitary bull or a yellow-bellied monkey, one must exercise self-protection.
If a person enters the womb on the day of either the lunar mansion *Jyeṣṭhā* or *Mūla*, it will result in evil and unwholesome consequences.
On the days of the lunar mansions Zhang (Jyeṣṭhā), Wei (Anurādhā), Liu (Śravaṇā), and Xin (Hṛdayā), those who wish to undertake an enterprise will encounter neither good nor evil results.
On the days of the lunar mansions Shi (Dhaniṣṭhā), Wei (Mūla), and Jing (Pūrvāṣāḍhā), those who wish to perform an undertaking will frequently encounter obstacles.
On the days of the three lunar mansions—Jyeṣṭhā, Ārdrā, and Śravaṇā—those who undertake projects will obtain the assistance of others.
On the days of the three lunar mansions—Rohiṇī, Anurādhā, and Saptarṣi (Uttara-bhādrapadā)—long journeys will be safe and secure.
The lunar mansions Fang (房), Gui (鬼), and Bi (辟) are suitable for forming friendships and marrying a wife on their respective days.
The seven mansions—Zhen (軫), Nü (女), Bi (畢), Mao (昴), Niú (牛), Yì (翼), and Gāng (亢)—are suitable only for travel and coming and going; other activities should not be undertaken on these days.

"When the fifteenth day of the Di (Jyeṣṭhā) lunar mansion is in operation, one can cause oneself to be feared and respected by all evil people; if one falls ill on that day, one should offer flowers to the deity, and only after the fifteenth day has passed will one recover."

Those born on this day possess majestic authority and are immensely wealthy; yet they are by nature stingy and greedy, and lust after the wives of others. You must discipline yourself and refrain from such conduct.
That person’s entry into the womb should take place under the constellation Param; for the undertaking of various activities, it should take place under the constellation Wei.
If on the days of the constellations Qixing, Lou, or Ji, one undertakes affairs, they will succeed regardless of whether they are good or evil.
If one undertakes construction on the day of the lunar mansion Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, or Śatabhīṣaj, the undertaking will be unfavorable and encounter many obstacles.
On the days of Ārdrā, Punarvasu, and Mṛgaśiras, these three days bring benefit.
On the day of the lunar mansion *Śravaṇā*, traveling far away is peaceful and secure.
On the days of the three mansions *Citrā*, *Kṛttikā*, and *Anurādhā*, those who wish to undertake an enterprise will obtain the assistance of others.
On the days of the three mansions *Svātī*, *Ārdrā*, and *Vaiśākha*, it is appropriate for matters such as forming friendships and taking a wife.

“The lunar mansion Bharaṇī governs on the first day of the white fortnight; it can accomplish swift matters in the world. On this day, if one is ill, one should prepare a meal of green beans to offer to the deities, and recovery will occur within ten days. Those born on this day face the perils of falling from cliffs or being harmed by weapons; regarding these two matters, they must protect themselves. They are well-suited for occupations such as managing livelihoods or trade, and they are gentle, refined, delight in the Dharma, and have faith in merit.”
When that person enters the womb, it is auspicious on days under the lunar mansions (nakṣatras) of Jing (井) and Zhang (張).
On days under the mansions of Dou (斗), Wei (胃), and others, one may undertake any undertaking without concern for its being good or evil.
If one undertakes work on the days of the three lunar mansions Zhèn, Bì, and Nǚ, it will be inauspicious;
if one undertakes work on the days of the three lunar mansions Xīn, Liù, and Kuí, it will be auspicious.
The lunar mansions of Śravaṇā, Bharaṇī, Āśleṣā, and Abhijit—on these four days, one’s undertakings will be secure and one shall attain mastery.
The lunar mansions of Pūrvaphalgunī and Rohiṇī—on these two days, traveling afar will be secure and one shall gain the power of knowledge.
The lunar mansions of Xū (虛), Mǎo (昴), Zhāng (張), and Yì (翼) are favorable for undertaking tasks and acquiring the property of others.

The six mansions of Jī (箕), Zǐ (觜), Jué (角), Xū (虛), Kàng (亢), and Shēn (參)—on the days of these six mansions, it is auspicious to establish close friendships with teachers and friends of all ranks, as well as to take a wife.

"When the Heart Star (Hṛdayā) exercises its influence for two days, it favors the commission of evil deeds; if one falls ill on such a day, one should offer an oblation of non-glutinous rice, barley, and yellow rock honey to Śakra Devendra. After thirteen days have passed, the illness will be cured."
Those born on this day are by nature prone to anger and lack a heart of compassion; even if they uphold the precepts, they will eventually break them.

If one sees others practicing pure conduct, one must exercise self-restraint and vigilance in such matters, and one must also protect oneself from the place of childbirth. It is auspicious for those whose *citta-nakṣatra* (mental asterism) entered the womb on this day.
The three lunar mansions of Jiao (Jyeṣṭhā), Xu (Mūla), and Zi (Pūrvāṣāḍhā)—on the days of these three, entering the womb is inauspicious.
The three lunar mansions of Mao (Maghā), Niú (Vṛṣabha), and Yi (Śravaṇā)—on the days of these three, it is appropriate to perform all activities.
On the day of Bi (Abhijit), if one undertakes any activity, there will be many obstacles.
On the days of the three lunar mansions—Dipper (Ji), Ladle (Qi), and Net (Lou)—one attains mastery and gains great benefit.
On the six lunar mansions—Tail (Wei), Willow (Liu), Quail (Kui), Danger (Wei), Pivot (Zhen), and Net (Bi)—one relies on the power of others.
On the days of the three lunar mansions Wei (胃), Zhang (張), and Dou (斗), it is auspicious for long journeys; travel on the roads will be peaceful and secure.
On the days of the six lunar mansions Shi (室), Kang (亢), Wei (危), Jing (井), Di (氐), and Shen (參), it is auspicious for forming friendships and taking a wife.

"When the constellation Mūla presides over the three days, it is capable of performing both firm and gentle tasks. If one falls ill on such a day, one should take the scent of various fruits, roots, and flowers to offer as a sacrifice to the deity; recovery will occur within thirty days."

Those born on this day will be greatly wealthy with abundant riches and much grain and wheat; such people possess the marks of those with divine virtue. However, they must exercise caution regarding their place of birth, and they are also prone to being trampled by mares; when at the place of mares, they must likewise provide for themselves.

For those who enter the womb on the day of the lunar mansion Mūla, as well as the days of the lunar mansions Anurādhā, Viśākhā, Ārdrā, and Aśleṣā—on these four lunar mansions, one should perform evil deeds.
On the days of the lunar mansions Zhèn (Jyeṣṭhā), Fáng (Rohiṇī), Bì (Pūrvaphalgunī), and Kuí (Aśvinī), one must not undertake various kinds of activities.
On the day of the mansion Wēi (Śatabhiṣaj), evil deeds may be performed.
On the days of the three lunar mansions—Dōu (Fighting), Yì (Wings), and Wèi (Stomach)—if one intends to perform evil deeds, there will be no benefit and much affliction.
On the days of the three lunar mansions—Jī (Winnowing Basket), Qīxīng (Seven Stars), and Lóu (Hare)—one attains mastery and achieves benefit.
On the days of the three lunar mansions—Jyeṣṭhā, Śravaṇā, and Mūla—one obtains the power of others and attains mastery.
On the days of the three lunar mansions—Pūrvā-phalgunī, Rohiṇī, and Śravaṇā—one travels and arrives in safety and peace.

On the days of the lunar mansions Śravaṇā, Āśleṣā, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, Mṛgaśirā, Kṛttikā, and Rohiṇī, it is auspicious to form friendships; matters such as those between close relatives and friends, as well as marriages and betrothals, will all be favorable.

"When the four days of the lunar mansion *Ji* (Pūrvā-phalgunī) govern the day, one who falls ill on such a day should offer a gruel of hemp and *ni-ku-ta* seeds as a sacrifice to the Water Deity; on the eighth day—according to the Dan edition, it says 'on that day'—the illness will be cured."

Those born on this day are well-suited for the occupations of plowing fields and navigating ships; by nature they are diligent and practice the ten virtuous deeds. Possessing great learning and wisdom, they enjoy high renown, abundant wealth, and vast riches, and they always associate with wise people.
On the days of the Seven Stars (Ursa Major) mansion and the Lou (Revatī) mansion, it is appropriate to perform various activities.
On the days of the three mansions of Jiao (Aśvinī), Zi (Jyeṣṭhā), and Xu (Śravaṇa), the undertaking of various matters results in neither good nor evil.
On the days of the lunar mansions Di (Jyeṣṇā) and Shi (Śatabhiṣaj), undertaking affairs is inauspicious.
On the day of Jing (Pūrvāṣāḍhā), those engaged in business will lose their former enterprises.
On the days of Yi (Śravaṇā), Mao (Mṛgaśirā), and Niu (Rohiṇī), those who wish to undertake affairs will achieve their goals as they desire and be able to obtain benefit.
If one undertakes tasks on days corresponding to the lunar mansions Zhang (張), Wei (胃), or Dou (斗), one will obtain the assistance of others and achieve benefit.
If one wishes to undertake tasks on days corresponding to the mansions Shen (參), Kang (亢), or Wei (危), one will likewise obtain the assistance of others.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Jyeṣṭhā, Bharaṇī, and Rohiṇī, if one intends to travel on a long journey, the road will be peaceful and secure.
On days of the five mansions—Śravaṇā, Āśleṣā, Śravaṇā, Kṛttikā, and Abhijit—it is appropriate for matters such as forming friendships or taking a wife.
"When the lunar mansion Dou (Dhruva) presides over affairs for five days, one should perform acts of gentleness.
If one falls ill on that day, one should parch the flowers of non-glutinous rice and mix them with honey to offer as a sacrifice to the various deities; within seven days, the illness will be cured."

Those born on these days are wise people; they have few ailments, possess great wealth, and have many friends and acquaintances. Such individuals are best conceived during the lunar mansion Zhang (Jyeṣṭhā).

If conception occurs on the days of the lunar mansions Wei (Mūla), Shen (Pūrva-phalgunī), or Kang (Vaiśravaṇa), the outcome will be neutral, with neither good nor evil; whatever undertakings one wishes to pursue will all be successfully accomplished.
The asterisms Bi (Aśvinī), Fang (Rohiṇī), Gui (Mūla), and Wei (Pūrvabhādrapadā)—on the days of these four asterisms, undertaking tasks is inauspicious.
The asterisms Bi (Uttarabhadrapadā), Nü (Śravaṇā), and Zhen (Anurādhā)—on the days of these three asterisms, those who seek mastery will encounter many obstacles.

On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Pleiades (Kṛttikā), Ox (Vṛṣabha), and Wing (Pūrvaphalgunī), those who wish to undertake an enterprise will achieve their goals with ease and as they desire.
On days of the Base (Jyeṣṭhā), Well (Pūrvāṣāḍhā), and Room (Uttarabhādrapadā) mansions, it is likewise appropriate to perform tasks, for they possess the power of merit.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Jiao (角), Zi (觜), and Xu (虛), those traveling on distant journeys will find their paths peaceful and secure.
On days corresponding to the six mansions of Kui (奎), Liu (柳), Fang (房), Lou (婁), Qi-xing (七星), and Xin (心), it is auspicious for matters such as forming friendships and arranging marriages.

"When the Ox Mansion (Go) governs for six days, those born on this day are by nature firm and resolute, their hearts free from fear; they are fierce and powerful, surpassing others in ability, capable of conquering kingdoms, facing no strong adversaries, and possessing great wealth and abundance."
If one enters the womb under the constellation *Śraviṣṭhā*, none of the other stars shall act as obstacles; they will all become auspicious friends.

"When the constellation *Anurādhā* exercises its influence for seven days, if one falls ill on such a day, it will persist for twelve months; only by offering rock honey and flowers to the mountain deity can one be cured."

Those born on this day will meet companions when traveling afar; it is auspicious for them to engage in livelihoods and perform gentle deeds. Such persons possess wisdom, suffer little from illness, and will constantly receive offerings from kings of the world.
For those who enter the womb on the day of the lunar mansion Jyeṣṭhā (軫宿), their lives will be even and devoid of both good and evil.
The lunar mansions of Ārdrā (鬼宿) and Viśākhā (房宿)—on these two days—one encounters obstacles.
The lunar mansions of Śravaṇā (七星宿), Hṛdaya (心宿), Anurādhā (女宿), and Pūrvā-phalgunī (畢宿)—on these four days—it is auspicious to undertake various undertakings.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Kṛttikā, Ārdrā, and Aśvinī, undertaking activities is inappropriate.
However, on days of Śravaṇā and Mūla, one attains harmony, success as desired, and mastery.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Śravaṇā, Puṣya, and Viśākhā, one may travel far with safety and attain mastery.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Bharaṇī, Rohiṇī, and Śravaṇā, those who wish to undertake enterprises will obtain the assistance of others and meet with virtuous friends.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Pleiades (Mṛgaśiras), the Net (Jyeṣṭhā), and the Wing (Śatabhiṣaj), it is auspicious to form friendships.

"When the eighth day of the mansion of Emptiness (Śravaṇā) is presiding, one who falls ill on that day will recover only after a year; one should prepare four kinds of soups made from mung beans, black beans, red beans, and adzuki beans, and offer fragrant flowers as a sacrifice to the deity."

Those born on this day are by nature prone to anger and greed; they are poor and lack clothing and food, and they likewise suffer from a deficiency in sensual pleasures. In their dealings with relatives, they are constantly beset by much fear.
If one conceives on the day of the lunar mansion Jyeṣṭhā, it is auspicious.
If one conceives on the days of the lunar mansions Śravaṇā, Bharaṇī, or Puṣyā, it is unfavorable and there will be many obstacles.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Bharaṇī, Śravaṇā, and Rohiṇī, those who enter the womb will experience a life that is neutral, devoid of both good and evil.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Ārdrā, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, and Uttarabhādrapadā, conception occurs under unfavorable conditions, resulting in separation and lack of harmony.
On the days of the constellations Kṛttikā, Ārdrā, and Aśleṣā, undertakings will yield benefit and achieve harmony.
On the day of the constellation Mṛgaśiras, anyone wishing to undertake a task may do so with complete success.
The lunar mansions of Ārdrā, Svātī, and Bharaṇī—on these three days, it is auspicious for traveling on distant roads with safety and ease.
On the days of Rohiṇī, Śravaṇa, and Hṛdaya (Jyeṣṭhā), those who undertake affairs will obtain virtuous friends and excellent companions.
On the days of the lunar mansions of Yi (Feather), Ji (Winnowing Basket), and Mao (Swift), it is also appropriate to bind together various kinsmen and friends.
On the days of the two mansions of Bi (Net) and Niu (Ox), it is likewise appropriate to bind together great and virtuous friends.

"When the constellation Wei (危) presides for nine days, its nature is gentle and supple. If one falls ill on this day, one should offer curdled milk, fresh milk, and rice gruel to the Water Deity; within seven days, the illness will be cured."

Those born on this day are by nature prone to anger and resentment; they are fierce, robust, and courageous, yet face perils from water. When approaching bodies of water, they must exercise great caution and vigilance.
For those who enter the womb on the day of the constellation Kṛttikā (Kàng), it is auspicious.
On the days of the lunar mansions Lou (Lubdhaka), Qi-xing (Śravaṇā), and Xin (Hṛdaya), those who undertake tasks will experience neutrality, with neither good nor evil results.
On the days of the three mansions Dou (Dhaniṣṭhā), Mao (Mṛgaśīrṣa), and Yi (Pūrvaphalgunī), those who undertake tasks will meet with misfortune.
On the days of the lunar mansions of Bì (Fen), Guǐ (Mṛgaśirā), Wěi (Jyeṣṭhā), and Cān (Aśleṣā), undertaking tasks will also be unfavorable and one’s wishes will not be fulfilled.
On the days of the lunar mansions of Shì (Śravaṇā), Jǐng (Pūrvāṣāḍhā), and Dǐ (Vṛṣabha), undertaking tasks will be harmonious and one will attain peace and security.
On days corresponding to the constellations of the Seven Stars (Ursa Major), Room (Jyeshthā), Willow (Śravaṇa), and Quail (Kṛttikā), long journeys will be auspicious and secure.

On days corresponding to the constellations of Canopy (Pūrvaphalgunī), Winnowing Basket (Anurādhā), and Stomach (Punarvasu), those who wish to undertake tasks will obtain the assistance of excellent companions.
On the days of the six lunar mansions—Jiao (角), Nü (女), Zi (觜), Zhen (軫), Bi (畢), and Niú (牛)—it is auspicious to form virtuous friendships and to take a wife.

"Regarding the day when the lunar mansion Śravaṇā presides for ten days, its nature is swift and rapid; if one falls ill on this day, one should offer various flowers as a sacrifice to the deity, and recovery will occur within thirty days."

Those born on this day are deceitful and treacherous, acting as thieves; they are foolish and speak falsehoods, harming sentient beings, and their minds constantly commit evil without fearing their parents. Whether in disputes, strife, or as bandits, they will meet with calamity in such circumstances. Such a person must enter the womb under the lunar mansion of Jyeṣṭhā.
If one undertakes a task on the days of the lunar mansions Jyeṣṭhā, Anurādhā, or Śravaṇā, there will be no obstacles and it may be done anywhere.
However, if one undertakes any business on the days of the three mansions—Pūrvābhādrapadā, Svātī, or Rohiṇī—all such endeavors will be unfavorable.
On the day of the Well (Jing) lunar mansion, undertaking affairs will be auspicious.
On the days of the Room (Fang), Willow (Liu), and Quail (Kui) lunar mansions, those who initiate undertakings will encounter many obstacles and fail to obtain benefit.
On the days of the lunar mansions Ārdrā, Svātī, and Bharaṇī, it is auspicious to undertake enterprises for the sake of gaining profit.
On the days of the lunar mansions Rohiṇī, Śravaṇa, and Hṛdaya (Jyeṣṭhā), traveling afar will be peaceful and secure.

On days corresponding to the lunar mansions Pleiades (Kṛttikā), Dipper (Ursa Major), and Winnowing Basket (Pūrvaphalgunī), those who undertake tasks will obtain the assistance of excellent companions.
On days corresponding to the mansions Void (Śravaṇā), Horns (Viśākhā), and Horns (Ārdrā), it is appropriate to establish small-scale acquaintances through essential means.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Xū (虛), Shēn (參), and Kàng (亢), it is appropriate to form essential bonds with great spiritual friends.
"When the mansion of Pì (辟) presides on the eleventh day, if one falls ill on that day, one should offer flowers and deer jerky to the Fire God; after seven days, one will recover."

One born on this day possesses wisdom and delights in the Dharma of the sages; they master various arts and are capable in all things, and they also fully understand singing, dancing, and performance. Furthermore, they preside over great wealth, possessing much gold, silver, grain, and silk. If one is to enter the womb, it is appropriate to do so on the day of the Tail (Mūla) lunar mansion.
On the days of the lunar mansions Bi (Pleiades) and Dou (Dipper), when performing various activities, the results are neutral, being neither good nor evil.
On the days of the three mansions Zi (Orion’s Head), Nü (Virgo), and Gui (Ghost), undertakings will achieve success.
The seven stars of the Heart (Hrdaya) mansion and these three mansions bring many obstacles to undertakings.
On the days of the Willow (Jyestha) and the Room (Vishakha) mansions, those who wish to undertake tasks will achieve harmony and their wishes as desired.
On days of the constellations Zhèn (Jyeṣṭhā), Niú (Vṛṣabha), and Bì (Pūrvabhādrapadā), undertaking tasks will proceed as desired, provided one encounters a capable companion.
On days of the constellations Zhāng (Śravaṇā), Wèi (Anurādhā), and Jī (Svātī), travel and movement will be peaceful and secure.
On the days of the lunar mansions Kṛttikā, Śravaṇa, and Aśvinī, it is appropriate to form minor associations.
On the days of the lunar mansions Puṣya, Viśākhā, and Ārdrā, it is most auspicious to form close friendships.
"If one falls ill on a day when the lunar mansion Wei (Qu) governs for twelve days, it is appropriate to offer incense and flowers to the deities; after twenty days have passed, one will recover."

One born on this day performs gentle deeds and possesses great power; they are respected by others, though they must guard themselves against dangers in the dark. They will be immensely wealthy with gold, silver, grain, and silk in unlimited measure; their business ventures will be profitable, and they will acquire the property of others.
That person enters the womb on days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Heart (Hṛdayā), Tail (Jyeṣṭhā), Net (Pūrvabhādrapadā), and Ox (Rohiṇī); on these days, one also accumulates much wealth.
On the two lunar mansions of Neck (Ārdrā) and Void (Śravaṇā), for those who undertake tasks, the outcome is neutral, being neither good nor evil.
On the day of the lunar mansion *Aśvinī*, one should not undertake any activities.
On the days of the four mansions—*Anurādhā*, *Śravaṇā*, *Dhaniṣṭhā*, and *Mṛgaśirā*—traveling and coming are peaceful and secure.
If one undertakes a task on the days of the lunar mansions of Virgo (Nü), Hyades (Bi), or the Horns (Jiǎo), one will obtain an excellent companion.
If one wishes to undertake a task on the days of the Pleiades (Jī), the Net (Zhāng), or the Stomach (Wèi) mansions, there will be no obstacles and one will gain the assistance of others.
On the days of the lunar mansions Lou (Pleiades), Xin (Heart), and Wei (Tail), one should seek to form friendships for the sake of mutual benefit.
On the days of the lunar mansions Jing (Well), Di (Base), and Wei (Danger), it is appropriate to seek to form minor friendships.
On the days of the lunar mansions Mūla, Śravaṇā, and Uttarabhādrapadā, it is appropriate to formally establish great friendships.

"If one falls ill on the thirteenth day when the mansion Rohiṇī is presiding over the day, one should offer an oblation of barley gruel to the deity; only after twenty-five days will the illness be cured."

Those born on this day are by nature quick-tempered and impetuous; they should always protect sentient beings and refrain from harming living creatures. When passing through passes or fords, they must exercise self-restraint and caution. They should become physicians who are skilled in understanding prescriptions and medicines and capable of curing various ailments; they will also be proficient in the arts of song and dance.
If one enters the womb on a day corresponding to the Heart (Hṛdayā) lunar mansion, there will be no obstacles.

If one undertakes any activity on days corresponding to these seven lunar mansions—Jyeṣṭhā, Mūla, Strī (Anurādhā), Śravaṇa, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, Rohiṇī, and Bharaṇī—it will result in neutrality, being neither good nor evil.
On the days of these lunar mansions, one must strictly refrain from buying or selling, traveling, or shaving the head; nor should one go to places where fighting occurs.

On the days of the three mansions—Jyeṣṭhā, Ārdrā, and Śravaṇā—it is appropriate to avenge enemies and engage in combat to achieve victory; it is also suitable for undertaking light, profitable, and gentle tasks, which will be successfully accomplished.
On the days of the seven lunar mansions, undertakings are firm and also bring benefit.
On the days of the mansions Zhang (Jyeṣṭhā), Ji (Anurādhā), and Wei (Mūla), one who wishes to travel far will find safety and peace.
On the days of the lunar mansions Bi, Zhen, and Bi, it is appropriate to perform beneficial activities and likewise to employ esoteric speech.
On the days of the lunar mansions Shen, Xu, and Kang, one should perform malevolent deeds.
On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Ārdrā, Svātī, and Uttarabhādrapadā, it is appropriate to seek out and form bonds with minor acquaintances.

On days corresponding to the lunar mansions of Anurādhā, Viśākhā, and Pūrvaphalgunī, it is appropriate to seek out and form bonds with major acquaintances; furthermore, for the sake of gaining the protection and affection of the masses, one should construct beds and carriages, or purchase oxen and horses.

"When the lunar mansion Āśleṣā (Wei) exercises its influence for fourteen days, the auspicious and inauspicious events, the performance of good and evil deeds, illnesses, and other matters pertaining to human life are as explained above.
When the moon has completed its circuit through the lunar mansions in the void and begins again from Kṛttikā (Mao), it is therefore called a 'day'."
When the moon is full in the sky for thirty days and nights, it is also called a "full moon.
When the eighth month is full, it begins with the lunar mansion Mūla and ends with Pūrvaṣāḍhā;
such is that month. There are fifteen periods of night and fifteen periods of day, and at midday, the shadow of the sun is six footprints long.
The lunar mansion Lou (Revatī) travels at night; Fang (Aśvinī) is situated before the sun, and the planet Mars follows the sun on its day.
This is the time of the eighth month, when the deity Scorpion presides; Mūla is the governing karma, as has already been explained above.

Within this waxing moon, on the fifteenth day next, the Pleiades (Kṛttikā) again presides; when the moon conjoins with the Pleiades, it is the full moon of the eighth month, and the conjunction of the Pleiades and the moon lasts for one full day and night.
Subsequently, it moves again to conjoin with the lunar mansion Pi (Pūrvabhādrapadā); on the first day of the ninth month, Pi presides.

"In the dark fortnight of the ninth month: on the first day, it is in conjunction with the asterism Bi (Pisces); on the second day, with Zi (Aquila); on the third day, with Shen (Hydra); on the fourth day, with Jing (Sagittarius); on the fifth day, with Gui (Corvus); on the sixth day, with Liu (Virgo); on the seventh day, with Xing (Lyra); on the eighth day, with Zhang (Delphini); on the ninth day, with Yi (Sculptor); on the tenth day, with Zhen (Norma); on the eleventh day, with Jiao (Taurus); on the twelfth day, with Kang (Geminorum); on the thirteenth day, with Di (Cancer); on the fourteenth day, with Fang (Cancri); and on the fifteenth day, it is in conjunction with Xin (Heart)—thus the dark fortnight is full."

"In the waxing moon, on the first day it is in conjunction with the Tail (Mṛgaśiras); on the second day, with the Winnowing Basket (Pūrvaphalgunī); on the third day, with the Dipper (Uttaraphalgunī); on the fourth day, with the Ox (Hasta); on the fifth day, with the Woman (Citrā); on the sixth day, with the Void (Svātī); on the seventh day, with the Perilous (Viśākhā); on the eighth day, with the Room (Anurādhā); on the ninth day, with the Opening (Jyeṣṭhā); on the tenth day, with the Aries (Mūla); on the eleventh day, with the Lou (Pūrvāṣāḍhā); on the twelfth day, with the Stomach (Uttarāṣāḍhā); on the thirteenth day, with the Pleiades (Abhijit); on the fourteenth day, with the Net (Śravaṇā); and on the fifteenth day, with the Beak (Dhaniṣṭhā)—this is the fullness of the waxing moon."

In the ninth month, the moon is full in conjunction with the *Ji* (Mṛgaśiras) lunar mansion; the day consists of fourteen *muhūrta*s and the night sixteen *muhūrta*s. At midday, the shadow of the sun measures eight footprints in length. The sun travels along the southern path (*dakṣiṇāyana*), while the *Mao* (Pleiades) mansion moves through the night and the *Wei* (Tail) mansion is positioned before the sun.
In the ninth month, Jupiter governs the season; it is revered by all the heavens, and matters of both gain and loss all depend upon it.
During this ninth month, the deity of Archery presides.

"In the tenth month, during the dark fortnight: on the first day it is in conjunction with the constellation Shen (參); on the second day, with Jing (井); on the third day, with Gui (鬼); on the fourth day, with Liu (柳); on the fifth day, with Xing (星); on the sixth day, with Zhang (張); on the seventh day, with Yi (翼); on the eighth day, with Zhen (軫); on the ninth day, with Jue (角); on the tenth day, with Kang (亢); on the eleventh day, with Di (氐); on the twelfth day, with Fang (房); on the thirteenth day, with Xin (心); on the fourteenth day, with Wei (尾); and on the fifteenth day, it is in conjunction with Ji (箕). This is the full moon of the dark fortnight."

"In the waxing moon, on the first day it is in conjunction with the Dipper (Dō), on the second with the Ox (Gyu), on the third with the Maiden (Nyō) and Emptiness (Ko), on the fourth with the Danger (Ki), on the fifth with the Chamber (Shitsu), on the sixth with the Opening (Hei), on the seventh with the Aries (Kei), on the eighth with the Goat (Rō), on the ninth with the Stomach (I), on the tenth with the Pleiades (Myō), on the eleventh with the Net (Pitsu), on the twelfth with the Beak (Shi), on the thirteenth with the Scorpion (San), on the fourteenth with the Well (Sei), and on the fifteenth with the Ghost (Ki); this is the fullness of the waxing moon."

"In the tenth month, when the moon is full in conjunction with the lunar mansion of Gui (Ghost), the day consists of thirteen periods and the night of seventeen periods; at midday, the shadow of the sun is ten footprints long; the lunar mansion of Zi travels by night, and the lunar mansion of Nü (Virgo) stands before the sun."
At this time, the planet Mercury (Kṛttikā) presides over the affairs. This is the month of the tenth lunar month, when the deity Makara presides over that month.

"In the dark fortnight of the eleventh month: on the first day, it is in conjunction with the constellation Willow (Jyeṣṭhā); on the second day, with the Seven Stars (Ursa Major); on the third day, with the Net (Pūrvaphalgunī); on the fourth day, with the Wings (Pūrvāṣāḍhā); on the fifth day, with the Pivot (Anurādhā); on the sixth day, with the Horns (Aśvinī); on the seventh day, with the Neck (Bharaṇī); on the eighth day, with the Base (Kṛttikā); on the ninth day, with the Chamber (Rohiṇī); on the tenth day, with the Heart (Mṛgaśiras); on the eleventh day, with the Tail (Ārdrā); on the twelfth day, with the Winnowing Basket (Punarvasu); on the thirteenth day, with the Dipper (Puṣya); on the fourteenth day, with the Ox (Maghā); and on the fifteenth day, with the Woman (Pūrvaphalgunī). This constitutes the fullness of the dark fortnight."

"In the waxing moon, on the first day it is in conjunction with Xū (虛), on the second day with Wēi (危), on the third day with Shì (室), on the fourth day with Pì (辟), on the fifth day with Kuí (奎), on the sixth day with Lóu (婁), on the seventh day with Wèi (胃), on the eighth day with Miǎo (昴), on the ninth day with Bì (畢), on the tenth day with Zī (觜), on the eleventh day with Shēn (參), on the twelfth day with Jǐng (井), on the thirteenth day with Guǐ (鬼), on the fourteenth day with Liǔ (柳), and on the fifteenth day it is in conjunction with Qīxīng (七星); this is the fullness of the waxing moon."

"In the eleventh month, when the moon is full in conjunction with the Seven Stars (Ursa Major), the day consists of twelve *muhūrta* and the night eighteen; at midday, the sun's shadow measures twelve footprints. The lunar mansion Mṛgaśiras (Ghost) moves through the night, while Ārdrā (Danger) stands before the sun, turning toward the south; the planet Mercury (Chenxing) exercises its influence."

This is the eleventh month; the deity of the water vessel presides over this month. "In the dark fortnight of the twelfth month: on the first day, it is in conjunction with the *Jyeṣṭhā* mansion; on the second day, with *Nakṣatra*;

on the third day, with *Svāti*; on the fourth day, with *Viśākhā*; on the fifth day, with *Ārdrā*; on the sixth day, with *Punarvasu*; on the seventh day, with *Puṣya*; on the eighth day, with *Aśleṣā*; on the ninth day, with *Maghā*; on the tenth day, with *Pūrva-phalgunī*; on the eleventh day, with *Uttara-phalgunī*; on the twelfth day, with *Hasta*; on the thirteenth day, with *Citrā*; on the fourteenth day, with *Svāti*; and on the fifteenth day, it is in conjunction with *Viśākhā*. Thus the dark fortnight is complete."

"In the waxing moon: on the first day it is in conjunction with the mansion Śravaṇā; on the second day, with Aśvinī; on the third day, with Bharaṇī; on the fourth day, with Kṛttikā; on the fifth day, with Rohiṇī; on the sixth day, with Mṛgaśiras; on the seventh day, with Ārdrā; on the eighth day, with Punarvasu; on the ninth day, with Puṣya; on the tenth day, with Āśleṣā; on the eleventh day, with Maghā; on the twelfth day, with Pūrvaphalgunī; on the thirteenth day, with Uttaraphalgunī; on the fourteenth day, with Hastā; and on the fifteenth day, with Citrā—this is the fullness of the waxing moon."

"In the twelfth month, when the moon is full in conjunction with the lunar mansion Yi (Yi-xiu), the day lasts for thirteen *kāla* and the night for seventeen *kāla*. The sun moves closer to the north, and at midday, the shadow measures twelve footprints. This is the time when the Seven Stars travel through the heavens and the celestial master Jupiter (*Sāvarṇi*) presides over affairs. This is the twelfth month, and the deity Tianyu (Heavenly Fish) presides over this month."

"In the dark fortnight of the first month, on the first day it is in conjunction with the asterism Zhèn; on the second day, with Jiǎo; on the third day, with Kāng; on the fourth day, with Dǐ; on the fifth day, with Fáng; on the sixth day, with Xīn; on the seventh day, with Wěi; on the eighth day, with Jī; on the ninth day, with Dǒu; on the tenth day, with Niú; on the eleventh day, with Nǚ; on the twelfth day, with Xū; on the thirteenth day, with Wēi; on the fourteenth day, with Shì; and on the fifteenth day, it is in conjunction with Pì. This is the completion of the dark fortnight."

"In the bright fortnight, on the first day it is in conjunction with Kui; on the second day, with Lou; on the third day, with Wei; on the fourth day, with Mao; on the fifth day, with Bi; on the sixth day, with Zi; on the seventh day, with Shen; on the eighth day, with Jing; on the ninth day, with Gui; on the tenth day, with Liu; on the eleventh day, with Qi-xing; on the twelfth day, with Zhang; on the thirteenth day, with Yi; on the fourteenth day, with Zhen; and on the fifteenth day, it is in conjunction with Jiao—this is the full moon of the bright fortnight."

"In the first month, the moon reaches completion in conjunction with the lunar mansion Jie (Jyeṣṭhā). Daytime lasts fourteen *kāla* and nighttime lasts sixteen *kāla*. The sun moves closer to the north; at midday, the shadow of the sun measures eight footprints. The mansion Zhang (Śravaṇā) traverses the night, while Lou (Pūrvaphalgunī) stands before the sun. The planet Mars (*Aṅgāraka*) is fierce, violent, and swift, presiding over this period. This is the time of the first month, when the deity Te-yang (Meṣa, the Ram) presides over that month."
