One does not grasp the present or future worlds; one does not grasp the wholesome or unwholesome; one does not grasp the outflowing (*sāsrava*) or the non-outflowing (*anāsrava*). One does not grasp the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, or the unsurpassed Mahāyāna. One does not grasp the three realms, nor the three vehicles; one does not grasp existence, nor non-existence; one does not grasp that which is non-existent and beyond verbal expression. Thus, one attains the Samādhi of Unconditioned Compassion, which is not the stage of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
By means of this samādhi, these people are able to see the entrance to the Śūraṅgama Samādhi gate and shall, in due order, attain the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
"O virtuous ones!

This is called the purity and equality of the vessel for supramundane wisdom; it is not the definitive purity and equality [of nirvana], but rather the equality of wisdom sought through the application of skillful means. "O noble ones!
In that regard, what is this "abiding in the supramundane vessel of all dharmas, the prajñā that is the purity and equality of the entire dharma-realm"?
O noble ones! The entire dharma-realm is not seen by the fleshly eye, nor is it seen by the divine eye; it is associated with the noble Dharma-eye of wisdom.

With the noble eye of wisdom, one observes that all dharma-realms neither increase nor decrease; one does not see any dharmas flourishing or declining, nor does one see proximity or distance, nor any location to which they go, nor does one see arising or ceasing.
When this person thus perceives all phenomena as pure and equal, they no longer perceive any sentient being as having substantial reality.
If they enter into the non-apprehensibility of sentient beings, they then attain entry into the non-apprehensibility of all phenomena.

Why is this? There are no dharmas apart from sentient beings, and there are no sentient beings apart from all dharmas. The essential nature of sentient beings is the essential nature of all dharmas; the essential nature of all dharmas is the essential nature of sentient beings. The essential nature of all dharmas is the essential nature of the self; the essential nature of the self is the essential nature of all dharmas. The essential nature of all dharmas is the essential nature of the Buddha-dharma; the essential nature of the Buddha-dharma is the essential nature of the realm of non-self; the essential nature of the realm of non-self is the essential nature of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); and the essential nature of the limit of reality is the essential nature of suchness (*tathatā*).
Thus one knows all phenomena. O worthy ones!
This is called abiding in the purity and equality of the vessel of supramundane wisdom regarding all dharma-spheres, which is the vessel for all dharmas and the supramundane wisdom-vessel.
"O virtuous ones! What therein is the purity and equality of all supramundane vessels of the Dharma?

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva thus abides in prajñā and enters meditative concentration (dhyāna), they do not perceive any dharma that can be apprehended; they abide in meditative concentration without abandoning it, dwelling in meditative concentration without abiding in, without extinguishing, and without cognizing any objective realm of dharmas."
This person does not abide in meditative concentration by means of the body-meditation, nor do they abide in meditative concentration by means of the mind-meditation.

When this person abides in such meditation, they enter the reality-limit (*tathatā-bhūtakoṭi*) and the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*); they are able to enter all dharmas without grasping or attachment, surpassing all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. This person, abiding in such meditation and meditative concentration, is an undetermined bodhisattva who is able to sever all afflictions, views, and the higher fetters of affliction.

"If, furthermore, a bodhisattva is able to abide in such dhyāna, they will be able to enter into all dharmas; upon entering these dharmas, they can know the various wholesome and unwholesome desires of sentient beings and bring them to maturity."

This person does not perceive sentient beings; they do not perceive a self, a person, a life-span, a soul, a collection of aggregates, a being, a nourisher, an agent, one who causes to act, an originator, one who causes to originate, an experiencer, or one who causes to experience.
When this person further enters the *tathatā* dharma-realm, they see all sentient beings with perverted afflictions; because of these perversions, they undergo various kinds of suffering.
In this way, such a person enters the subtle reality-limit (tathatā-bhūtakoṭi) of the dharma-realm; as a bodhisattva, they bring sentient beings to maturity while perceiving no sentient beings.

Because sentient beings are not real; because sentient beings are devoid of "sentient being-ness"; because sentient beings are without self; because sentient beings are detached; because sentient beings lack intrinsic nature; because sentient beings are ineffable; because sentient beings are empty; because sentient beings are signless; because sentient beings are wishless; because sentient beings are without activity; because sentient beings are of the nature of suchness; because sentient beings are unarisen; because sentient beings are unceasing; because sentient beings are pure—while maturing sentient beings in this way, one likewise does not perceive a self, nor even a recipient, yet one does not destroy the task at hand.

“The intrinsic nature and characteristics of these dharmas are the ineffable dharma-realm; it cannot be expressed by any speech or writing, it cannot be demonstrated, and it is non-existent. Yet, out of great compassion, this bodhisattva speaks of all dharmas within that which is ineffable.”

"This is with outflows, this is without outflows; this is mundane, this is supramundane; this is blameworthy, this is blameless; this is conditioned, this is unconditioned; this is with affliction, this is without affliction; this should be practiced, this should be abandoned; this is the dharma of ordinary persons, this is the dharma of those in training, this is the dharma of those beyond training; this is the dharma of pratyekabuddhas, this is the dharma of bodhisattvas, this is the dharma of the Buddhas."

"O noble ones! This undetermined bodhisattva, thus abiding in the supramundane prajñā that is the vessel for all dharmas, enters into the pure equality of all dharma-realms and expounds the Dharma through discernment; yet, regarding the Dharma thus expounded, the bodhisattva perceives no signs therein."
"O virtuous ones!
It is like a magician who, throughout the realm of space, conjures various forms and various flowers; though no such thing has ever been made before, he is able to manifest its creation."

If a Buddha did not appear in the world, could such wondrous meanings, phrases, and flavors emerge from within those flowers, entering the gateways of the Dharma and manifesting the sounds of the Dharma?
Would it not be difficult to perform such a feat?
At that time, the assembly of all devas, humans, ghosts, and spirits spoke thus:
"O Virtuous Blessed One! This matter is difficult."
"O Virtuous Sugata! This is the first difficulty.
The Buddha said:
"O noble ones! This is exceedingly difficult;

this is the most difficult of all difficulties. For a bodhisattva who has not yet reached certainty, regarding these phenomena that are non-appropriated—phenomena such as these which are formless, invisible, non-literal, and beyond verbal expression—to be able to eliminate the afflictions of other sentient beings and bring them to maturity, while he himself has not yet known, realized, well-cultivated, mastered, or reached the further shore of these [phenomena], is indeed most difficult."
Those sentient beings, who have not yet realized such a profound and ineffable Dharma, do not slander it upon hearing it; this is the first difficult turning.

Those sentient beings are able to shatter all trees of affliction; they abide with a mind of pliancy and a mind of purposeful action, maintaining toward all sentient beings a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of compassion, a mind of non-harming, a mind of pity, a mind of solidarity, and a mind of equality.

Because those sentient beings possess supple minds, they dry up the ocean of existence, cross the ocean of afflictions, and swiftly enter the city of fearlessness; yet, regarding such ineffable realization that they have not themselves attained, they do not slander it upon hearing it. This is even more difficult than the previously mentioned supreme difficulty.
"Why do you evil-minded spirits and ghosts not restrain your own minds?
Why do you not cultivate a gentle heart toward all sentient beings, nor contemplate the terrors of future lives?
O virtuous ones!..."

If there are Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who abide in the Samādhi of the Purity and Equality of All World-Transcending Dharma-Vessels, they are able to cause all sentient beings to guard their six sense-faculties and each remain within their own respective domains; how much more so would they be able to obstruct and ward off you evil-minded ghosts and spirits!
These virtuous beings have all attained this Dharma; abiding in a mind of great loving-kindness and great compassion, they do not afflict others.
Why is this? Because, through the power of the skillful means of cultivating great loving-kindness and great compassion, they do not afflict others.

Once these bodhisattvas have entered such profound dharmas, they are able to cast sentient beings into the realm of empty space so that for many billions of nayutas of kalpas they do not see one another; how much less would they be unable to subdue you evil ghosts and spirits!
Furthermore, they are able to cast all sentient beings into the midst of the great darkness between worlds, and can even cause all sentient beings to subsist solely on wind, water, earth, and stone.

Because these bodhisattvas abide in this profound, supramundane, dharma-vessel-like, pure, and equanimous samādhi, they are able to cause all sentient beings to go without food for many billions of kalpas; how much more so could they not restrain you evil ghosts and spirits who consume the vital essence, blood, and flesh of other sentient beings!
Why have I abandoned you? These bodhisattvas, through the power of their great loving-kindness, great compassion, and skillful means, have abandoned you.

Among all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in these four continents who dwell in this profound, supramundane vessel-purifying and equalizing samādhi, there are those named Bodhisattva Sovereign of the Multitude, Bodhisattva Sovereign of Loving-kindness, Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī-voice, Bodhisattva Sovereign of Lightning, Bodhisattva Sovereign of the Sun, Bodhisattva Sovereign of the Moon, Bodhisattva Sovereign of the Earth, Bodhisattva Sovereign of Perception, Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, and Bodhisattva Sovereign of Water; such as these eighteen thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas reside within these four continents.
“Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in these ten kinds of foremost, most profound, supramundane, all-vessel-purifying equanimity. What are the ten?

That is to say: the equality of sentient beings, the equality of phenomena, the equality of purity, the equality of generosity, the equality of ethical discipline, the equality of patience, the equality of diligence, the equality of meditative concentration, the equality of wisdom, and the equality of the purity of all phenomena.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who abide in these ten kinds of foremost, most profound, supramundane, and all-vessel-purifying samādhis of equality are each individually able to subdue you evil spirits and ghosts, as previously described.
Why do they let you go? These bodhisattvas let you go because they have cultivated the power of skillful means through great loving-kindness and great compassion;
how much more so the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavat!

"O noble ones! Even if all sentient beings were to abide in these ten kinds of supramundane, profound, and pure equality of all dharma-vessels as previously described, a single moment of wisdom of a Tathāgata would surpass them all."
How much more so does the Tathāgata, at all times, protect you with a heart of great compassion, neither giving rise to anger nor abandoning you.
At all times the Tathāgata feels pity for you, desiring to bring you benefit and peace.

"You all are thus devoid of shame and remorse, disregarding the terrors of future lives; you harbor toward all sentient beings a lack of compassion, a lack of gentleness, an evil mind, a mind of enmity, a lack of loving-kindness, and a lack of pity. You should not commit such unrighteous acts."
Wishing to clarify this meaning once more, he spoke these verses:
"The Great Hero, seeing such a gathering of spirits without exception,
immediately raised his right arm and proclaimed these words:"
The appearance of a Buddha in the world is extremely rare; the Dharma and the Saṅgha are likewise rare.
Pure faith among sentient beings is rare, and freedom from all calamities is also rare.
Compassion for sentient beings is rare; contentment is the foremost rarity.
To hear the True Dharma is difficult; to be able to practice it is the foremost difficulty.
To know that these difficulties are equal brings constant happiness in the world.
These ten points of equality—the wise should understand them swiftly.
First, regarding the equality of sentient beings: abandon all evil karma and perform all virtuous karma;
by doing so, one will long enjoy supreme happiness.
Regarding the equality of the practice of the Dharma: all dharmas are equal.
The Buddhas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and ordinary beings are all suchness (tathatā).
This pure equality is attained among those people;
having distanced themselves from grasping at objects, they likewise do not destroy the self.
Practice generosity with equanimity and joy; do not harm other sentient beings;
do not seize the means of their livelihood; and do not destroy flowers or fruits.
There is not a single sentient being who has not been my father or mother.
All sentient beings have once been my close acquaintances;
I shall not cause even a single being further distress.
May untimely winds and all violent rains cease.
Abundant and joyful affairs nourish all kinsmen and acquaintances;
the vital essence of sentient beings increases, remaining forever undiminished.
One does not exhale breath upon the bodies of others, nor does one look with eyes of anger or malice.
I do not rob others of their vital energy, but fulfill all their happiness.
My heart benefits all beings; I do not harbor anger toward those who fail me.
To sever all afflictions, I seek the teachings of the Buddhas.
The wise constantly guard the ten paths of wholesome action;
they always rejoice in the world and shall later attain the vision of Nirvana.
They do not rely on the aggregates to maintain their precepts, nor do they rely on the elements or the sense bases.
The precepts that extinguish the branches of existence, The craving for existence that is extinguished,
And the relinquishing of manifold perceptions— These can quell anger and rage.
When words and letters are thus joined, The wise one is free from conceptual discrimination.
Because it is empty like space, it is free from all conceptualization;
one who practices patience in this way is a wise person free from conceptualization.
It is like the moon in the sky, surrounded by a multitude of stars.
One who practices patience in this way is manifest among the assembly in peace and security.
Just as moonlight illuminates the *maṇi* gem, causing the waters of the ocean to swell to fullness,
so too does patience illuminate the demons of an evil mind, enabling them to attain pure faith.
Having distanced themselves from all evils and cultivated the practices of enlightenment,
those sentient beings, in due order, will be able to fulfill the ocean-like qualities of all Buddhas.
In the past, when I was a rishi, I cultivated patience within the forest.
Though my body was dismembered limb by limb, I did not give rise to a heart of anger.
When I became a rabbit for the sake of a seer, I threw myself into the fire;
because I practiced patience, the fire was transformed into a lotus pond.
By the power of that patience, I have brought many sentient beings to maturity;
yet among the Arhats today, none possess such patience.
The wise always exert themselves, cultivating practice for the sake of merit and wisdom.
The ocean of wisdom becomes full and complete, and one attains the ocean of all Buddhas.
By practicing dhyāna and prajñā, one is freed from all afflictions;
no longer discriminating within the three realms, one abides in suchness.
The wise one cultivates the wisdom of dhyāna, Transcending the world to abide in the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi).
Untainted by any phenomena, They are free from all conceptual discrimination.
Not discriminating among phenomena, They do not perceive the existence of sentient beings.
All phenomena have but a single characteristic; thus one attains the vision of the Buddha’s realm.
The immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas dwells securely in this dharmatā;
they do not afflict you, for they abide in noble prajñā.
The Tathāgata has been patient with you and has not caused you distress;
yet you are devoid of shame and have abandoned all sense of modesty.
These sentient beings who commit evil are of a base nature and exceedingly stubborn.
Beholding the Buddha’s great valor, all have attained a supple mind.
Each of you should restrain your own evil thoughts;
you shall, in due order, swiftly realize Great Nirvana.
If you are gentle and pliant, you shall be able to leave behind all evil karma;
for the sake of protecting this Dharma, I entrust it to you.
Those śrāvakas whom I have taught, endowed with wisdom and great renown—
Out of compassion for you all, he causes you to obtain merit and wisdom;
you shall receive the benefit of food and drink, be honored by the devas,
attain an excellent dwelling place, and gain an increase in lifespan.
"If one hears the words of the Guide and is able to practice according to what was taught, one will always receive the reward of supreme bliss within the worlds of humans and devas.

At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching the Dharma among that assembly of evil spirits and ghosts, there were among them certain evil spirits who had previously established firm faith in the Buddha-Dharma; however, at a later time, they associated with evil friends and perceived the faults of others. Due to these causes and conditions, they were reborn as evil spirits. Among those ninety-two nayutas of hundreds of thousands of evil spirits, there were those who attained the fruit of *srotāpanna*.
Billions of nayutas of kotis of evil spirits who had previously practiced the Mahāyāna attained the patience of conformity (*anulomikī-kṣānti*);
immeasurable asaṃkhyeyas of evil spirits attained a supple mind, and having attained it, they further resolved their minds toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, among that assembly of ghosts and spirits, there was a rākṣasa king named Ox-King-Eye, who, together with ten thousand rākṣasa kings, joined his palms toward the Buddha, paid homage with single-minded devotion, and spoke these words:
"O Virtuous Blessed One!
"Because we were driven by the latent tendency of anger, we have long endured unpleasant fruits within this world.
Now, by receiving the Buddha’s spiritual power, we are able to recollect our own past lives during this Bhadrakalpa."

"In the Dharma of the Tathāgata Krakucchanda, we once went forth as monastics; we recited and upheld eighty thousand collections of Mahāyāna teachings and eighty thousand collections of Śrāvaka teachings, and we made the vow for Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

"At that time, we gave rise to a mind of anger toward those bhikṣus who dwelt in the forest according to the Dharma; because of this karmic obstruction, at the end of our lives there, we were born in hell, where we were burned and boiled for a long time until our mindfulness was utterly lost. At the end of our lives there, we were born among these evil rākṣasas who feed on the flesh and blood of others."

It is precisely because we collectively committed evil karma at the time we formerly left the household life that we have now received these bodies of evil rākṣasas; for the sake of food and drink, we sever the lives of immeasurable billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of beings.
"Therefore, we now, in the presence of the Buddha, repent of all our evil karmas and shall never commit them again.
Thus they spoke three times, until they reached a state of firm resolve to practice the precepts and discipline.
"We only pray that the World-Honored One will grant us the prediction of our attainment of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Buddha said, "O virtuous ones!"
I do not see any other single dharma that distances one from the bodhicitta more than the arising of an evil mind toward a forest-dwelling bhikṣu. O noble ones!
"In a future age, during this Bhadrakalpa, there will be a final Tathāgata named Rocana; that Buddha shall bestow upon you all the prediction of supreme enlightenment.
Then those ten thousand rākṣasa kings shed tears and said:

"We would rather dwell in hell than, having taken human form, give rise to an evil thought for even a single moment toward an araṇya bhikṣu, for such a person can sever all roots of goodness—how much more so if one repeatedly gives rise to evil thoughts!"

At that time, there were also various evil spirits and ghosts who revered and had faith in the Triple Gem; dwelling in a mind of gentleness and contemplating the terrors of future lives, they all spoke with one voice, saying:
"O Great Virtuous Bhagavān!
From this day forward, we shall cease all evil and repent for all past unwholesome karma.

From now on, we shall subsist on flowers, incense, fruits, water, air, the Dharma, and joy; we shall no longer afflict others. For the sake of ensuring that the Buddha’s teachings remain long in the world, we shall uphold and protect the Buddha’s entrustment, and we shall provide superior protection for the World-Honored One’s śrāvaka disciples who dwell in araṇya hermitages.
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent! O virtuous man!"
You should thus properly receive my entrustment; I now further entrust you all to every bodhisattva and every śrāvaka of the Bhadrakalpa.

Out of compassion for you all, he practices what is wholesome and aids the Path day and night; he shares his own merits with you, invokes your names, and offers prayers on your behalf. By this means, your vital energy, great strength, majestic virtue, and powerful efficacy, as well as your close kinsmen and retinues, shall all increase.

Because they thus protect and uphold my Dharma in various ways, they also well protect the bhikṣus dwelling in araṇya who follow either the Mahāyāna or the Hīnayāna; in this manner, their vital energy increases, as does that of their retinues.

"In this way, indeed, you have made a supreme offering to the Buddhas of the three periods of time; by these roots of goodness, you shall be able to abandon the evil realms and attain both worldly happiness and the bliss of nirvāṇa."

Chapter Nine: The Protection and Sustenance by the Various Heavenly Kings. *Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra*, Candragarbha-parivarta, Part Twelve. Chapter Nine: The Protection and Sustenance by the Various Heavenly Kings. At that time, for the sake of revealing the world, the World-Honored One addressed Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, saying:
"Who is able to provide protection, sustenance, and nourishment for these four continents?"
Then Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, spoke these words:
"O Virtuous Blessed One!
The King of the Tuṣita Heaven, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Tuṣita devaputras, protects, sustains, and nurtures Uttarakuru."
The King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sons of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods, protects, sustains, and nurtures Pūrvavideha in the east.
The King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sons of the Nirmāṇarati gods, protects, sustains, and nurtures Jambudvīpa in the south.
The Suyāma Heavenly King, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Suyāma devaputras, protects, sustains, and nurtures Aparagoyānī.
"O Bhagavat of Great Virtue!
The Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of yakṣas, protects, sustains, and nurtures Uttarakuru in the north.
The Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of gandharvas, protects, sustains, and nurtures Pūrvavideha in the east.
The Heavenly King Virūḍhaka, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kumbhāṇḍas, protects, sustains, and nurtures Jambudvīpa in the south.
The Heavenly King Virūpākṣa, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nāgas, protects, sustains, and nurtures Aparagoyānī in the west.
“O Great Virtuous Blessed One!
Seven lunar mansions of celestial seers, three planets, and three celestial maidens protect, sustain, and nourish Uttarakuru.
As for those seven lunar mansions of celestial seers, they are: Śravaṇā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣaj, Pūrvabhādrapadā, Uttarabhādrapadā, Revatī, and Aśvinī.”
The three planets are Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars.
The three celestial maidens are Kumbhāṇḍī, Menā, and Miśrā.
O Virtuous Bhagavān!
Among those seven celestial mansions of the heavenly immortals, the three mansions of Xū, Wéi, and Shì constitute the domain of the planet Saturn (Tiānjīng), and Jūnpán is their lunar station (chén).
The two mansions of Pì and Kuí constitute the domain of the planet Jupiter (Suìxīng), and Mínnà is their lunar station.
The two lunar mansions of Lou (Liu) and Wei (Wei) are the terrestrial domain of Mars, and Mi-sha is their *chen* (constellation). O Virtuous Bhagavān!
Thus, these seven lunar mansions of the celestial seers, the three luminaries, and the three celestial maidens protect and nourish Uttarakuru in the north.
“O Great Virtuous Blessed One!
Seven lunar mansions of celestial seers, three planets, and three celestial maidens protect and nurture Pūrvavideha in the east.
As for those seven lunar mansions of celestial seers, they are Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśiras, Ārdrā, Punarvasu, Puṣya, and Āśleṣā.”
The three luminaries are Venus, Jupiter, and the Moon.
The three celestial maidens are Viśākhā, Maitrāyaṇī, and Karkoṭakī.
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!
Among those seven lunar mansions of the celestial seers, the two mansions of Mṛgaśiras and Kṛttikā are the domain of Venus; Viśākhā is its *nakṣatra*."
The three lunar mansions of Jyeṣṭhā, Āśleṣā, and Pūrva-phalgunī constitute the domain of Jupiter; Mithuna is its *nakṣatra*.
The two lunar mansions of Ārdrā and Uttaraphalgunī constitute the domain of the Moon; Karkaṭaka is its *nakṣatra*.
"O Bhagavān of Great Virtue!
In this way, the seven lunar mansions of the celestial seers, the three luminaries, and the three celestial maidens protect and nurture Pūrvavideha in the east.
O Bhagavān of Great Virtue!"
The seven celestial mansions of the heavenly immortals, the three luminaries, and the three celestial maidens protect and nourish Jambudvīpa in the south.
As for those seven celestial mansions of the heavenly immortals, they are: Xing (Jyesthā), Zhang (Anurādhā), Yi (Śravaṇā), Zhen (Dhaniṣṭhā), Jiao (Aśvinī), Kang (Bharaṇī), and Di (Kṛttikā).
The three planets are the Sun, Venus, and Jupiter.
The three celestial maidens are Śikhā, Kanyā, and Daurī.
O Virtuous Blessed One!
Among those seven celestial mansions of the heavenly immortals, Xing (Jyeṣṭhā), Zhang (Mūla), and Yi (Pūrvāṣāḍhā) are the domains of the Sun, and Shēhē (Śravaṇā) is their lunar station (*nakṣatra*).
Zhěn (Uttarāṣāḍhā) and Jiao (Abhijit) are the two mansions that are the domains of Saturn (*Tīkṣṇa*), and Jiāruò (Śatabhiṣaj) is their lunar station.
The two lunar mansions of Kṛttikā and Rohiṇī are the domain of Venus, and Dōula is their constellation.
O Virtuous Blessed One!
Thus, these seven lunar mansions of the celestial sages, the three luminaries, and the three celestial maidens protect and nurture Jambudvīpa in the south.
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!
Those celestial seers, the seven lunar mansions, the three luminaries, and the three celestial maidens protect and nurture Aparagoyānī.
As for those celestial seers and seven lunar mansions, they are Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśiras, Ārdrā, Punarvasu, Puṣya, and Āśleṣā."
The three planets are Mars (Hinghuo), Jupiter (Suixing), and Saturn (Zhensheng).
The three celestial maidens are Viriñcika, Dhanuṣā, and Makarā.
"O Virtuous Blessed One!
Among those seven lunar mansions of the celestial seers, the two mansions of Bharaṇī and Kṛttikā are the domain of the planet Mars (Maṅgala), and its *nakṣatra* is Viśākhā."
The three lunar mansions of Pūrvāṣāḍhā, Uttarāṣāḍhā, and Śravaṇā constitute the domain of Jupiter; Dhanu is its *nakṣatra*.
The two lunar mansions of Rohiṇī and Mṛgaśirā constitute the domain of Saturn; Makara is its *nakṣatra*.
"O Bhagavat, Mahābhāga!
In this way, the seven lunar mansions of the celestial seers, the three luminaries, and the three celestial maidens protect and nurture Aparagoyānī.
O Bhagavat, Mahābhāga!"
Among these four continents, Jambudvīpa in the south is the most excellent.

Why is this? Because the people of Jambudvīpa are courageous, robust, wise, and endowed with pure conduct (*brahmacarya*); it is here that the Buddha, the Blessed One (*bhagavān*), appears in the world. For this reason, the Four Great Heavenly Kings provide protection, support, and nourishment here with redoubled intensity.
In this Jambudvīpa there are sixteen great nations:

namely, the kingdoms of Aṅga-Magadha, Vaṅga-Magadha, Aparānta, and Ceti. These four great nations are surrounded by and protected, nurtured, and sustained by the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa together with his hosts of yakṣas.
The four great kingdoms of Kāśī, Kośala, Vatsa, and Malla are protected, guarded, and nurtured by the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who is surrounded by a host of gandharvas.

The kingdoms of Kaurava, Vatsa, Pañcāla, and Sūna—these four great kingdoms—are surrounded by and protected by the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka together with his host of kumbhāṇḍas, who nurture and sustain them.
The four great kingdoms of Aśvaka, Suma, Surāṣṭra, and Kamboja are surrounded by and protected and nurtured by the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa together with his host of nāgas.
“O Great Virtuous Blessed One!
In the past, because the celestial seers protected and nurtured these four continents, they likewise distributed and established them in this very manner.”

Thereafter, throughout their respective lands, cities, towns, villages, stūpas, monasteries, gardens, groves, beneath trees, in cemeteries, mountain valleys, wildernesses, rivers, springs, ponds, marshes, and even upon jewel islands in the ocean or at celestial shrines—therein dwell various beings born from eggs, from wombs, from moisture, or by transformation, such as nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, bhūtas, and kaṭapūtanas; they are born therein and continue to reside in those places, remaining unattached and not subject to the instructions of others.

Therefore, we pray that the Buddha will have those spirits and deities distributed and stationed throughout all the lands of this Jambudvīpa for the sake of providing protection and for the sake of guarding all sentient beings; we here express our desire to rejoice in this.
The Buddha said: "So it is, Great Brahmā!
It is just as you have said."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke in verse:
"To manifest to the world, the Guide questioned Brahmā:
'Within these four continents, who protects and nurtures them?'"
Thus the Teacher of Gods and Brahmā, with the various celestial kings at their head—
the Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, Paranirmita-vaśavartin, and Suyāma— heavenly beings—
are able to protect, uphold, and nurture [him].
In this same way, the Four Heavenly Kings and their retinues are likewise able to protect and sustain these four continents.
The twenty-eight lunar mansions, the twelve earthly branches,
and the twelve celestial maidens also protect and sustain the four continents.
Wherever they may be born— whether as nāgas, ghosts, rākṣasas,
or others who do not accept the teachings of others— may they instead act as protectors therein.
May the Buddha cause the various classes of devas and other celestial beings to be distributed accordingly.
Out of compassion for sentient beings, you shall blaze brightly the lamp of the True Dharma.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Candragarbha, saying: “O Knower of Purity!”
At the beginning of this Bhadrakalpa, when the human lifespan was forty thousand years, the Buddha Krakucchanda appeared in the world.

For immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings, that Buddha turned back the wheel of birth and death and turned the wheel of the True Dharma, leading them away from the evil realms and establishing them in the good realms and the fruit of liberation.

That Buddha entrusted these four great continents to the Great Brahmā King, Lord of the Sahā World, as well as to the Kings of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin, Nirmāṇarati, Tuṣita, and Suyāma heavens, for the sake of protection and sustenance, out of compassion for sentient beings, so that the lineage of the Triple Gem would not be severed, but would instead flourish and blaze forth; so that the vital essence of the earth, the vital essence of sentient beings, and the vital essence of the True Dharma might long endure and increase; and so that all sentient beings might find rest from the three evil realms and proceed toward the three good realms. Thus, he entrusted the four continents to the Great Brahmā and the various heavenly kings.

In this manner, as the kalpas gradually come to an end, all devas and humans perish; all wholesome karma and pure dharmas are utterly extinguished, while great evils increase and sentient beings are submerged in the afflictions.
"When the human lifespan was thirty thousand years, the Buddha Kanakamuni appeared in the world.

That Buddha entrusted these four great continents to the Lord of the Sahā World, the Great Brahmā King, the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, and even to the Four Great Kings and their retinues, so that they might protect, sustain, and nurture them; and so that all sentient beings might find rest from the three evil paths and proceed toward the three good paths, he entrusted these four continents to the Great Brahmā and the various heavenly kings."

In this manner, as the kalpas successively come to an end, all devas and humans perish, and the white dharmas also vanish, while great evils increase and sentient beings are submerged in the afflictions.
When the human lifespan is twenty thousand years, the Tathāgata Kāśyapa appears in the world.

That Buddha entrusted these four great continents to the Great Brahmā King, Lord of the Sahā World; to the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven; to the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven; to the King of the Tuṣita Heaven; to the King of the Suyāma Heaven; to Kauśika Śakra; and to the Four Heavenly Kings, along with their retinues, for the purpose of protecting, upholding, and nurturing them, and even to cause all sentient beings to rest from the three evil paths and proceed toward the three good paths.

That Kāśyapa Buddha entrusted these four continents to the Great Brahmās, the Four Heavenly Kings, and others, as well as to the assembly of celestial beings, the seven luminaries, the twelve celestial maidens, and the twenty-eight lunar mansions, so that they might protect and nurture them.

"O Knower of Purity! In this sequence, we have now reached this age of strife—a degenerate eon, a degeneration of afflictions, a degeneration of sentient beings, and a degeneration of great evil afflictions—where the lifespan of humans is one hundred years, all wholesome dharmas (*śukladharma*) have vanished, and all manner of evils obscure the world."

Just as the water of the ocean has the single taste of great saltiness, so too the flavor of the great afflictions pervades the world; they gather in evil factions, holding skulls in their hands with blood smeared upon their palms, mutually slaying one another.

Thus, among such evil sentient beings, I have now appeared in the world; having attained perfect enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree, I accepted the food offered by the merchants Trapusa and Bhallika.

For their sake, and because the devas, nāgas, gandharvas, kumbhāṇḍas, yakṣas, and others of this Jambudvīpa protect and nurture them, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas from every buddha-field throughout the ten directions, without exception, have gathered here in this great assembly.

Even unto this Sahā Buddha-field, wherein there are ten billion suns and moons, ten billion sets of four continents, ten billion great oceans, ten billion Cakravāḍa and Mahācakravāḍa mountains, ten billion Sumeru mountains, ten billion cities of the four Asura kings, ten billion Great Kings of the Four Quarters, ten billion Trāyastriṃśa heavens, and so on, up to ten billion spheres of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
In this manner, I have briefly enumerated the Buddha-fields of Sahā; it is in these places that I perform the work of a Buddha.

Furthermore, all the Brahma kings and their retinues throughout the Sahā Buddha-field, as well as the Māra kings, the kings of Paranirmita-vaśavartin, the kings of Nirmāṇarati, the kings of Tuṣita, the kings of Suyāma, the kings of Śakra, the four Great Kings, the Asura kings, the Nāga kings, the Yakṣa kings, the Rākṣasa kings, the Gandharva kings, the Kiṃnara kings, the Garuḍa kings, the Mahoraga kings, the Kumbhāṇḍa kings, the Preta kings, the Piśāca kings, the Pūtana kings, and the Kaṭapūtana kings—all brought their retinues to this great assembly for the sake of hearing the Dharma.
Even unto this Sahā Buddha-field, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and all the śrāvakas without exception have gathered here for the sake of hearing the Dharma.
I now manifest the profound Buddha-dharma for this assembled great multitude.
Furthermore, for the sake of protecting the world, I shall distribute and station these spirits and deities gathered here in Jambudvīpa to guard, uphold, and nurture it.
At that time, the World-Honored One again asked Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World:
"To whom did the Buddhas of the past entrust these four great continents, charging them with protection, guardianship, and nourishment?"
Then Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, said:

"The Buddhas of the past entrusted these four continents to me and to Kauśika, charging us with their protection; yet I failed in this, for I did not proclaim my own name nor that of Śakra, but instead spoke only of other heavenly kings, the lunar mansions, and the planets as providing protection and nourishment."
At that time, Mahābrahmā, the lord of the Sahā world, and Kauśika Śakra prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and spoke these words: “O Virtuous Bhagavān!
"O Great Virtuous Sugata!
I now offer my apologies. Like a small child, foolish and lacking wisdom, I did not state my own name before the Tathāgata.
O Great Virtuous Bhagavat!"
I only pray that you will grant me forgiveness,
O Great Virtuous Sugata! I only pray that you will grant me forgiveness!
I also pray that this great assembly will grant me their forgiveness.
For the sake of protecting and nurturing those within my domain—where I possess mastery over speech and commands—I act even unto leading all sentient beings toward the wholesome paths.
"We have already received instructions from the Buddha Krakucchanda, even to the point of causing the lineage of the Triple Gem to blaze forth.

At the abodes of the Buddhas Kanakamuni and Kāśyapa, we received instructions in the same manner, diligently causing the lineage of the Triple Gem to blaze forth. Because the vital essence of the earth, the vital essence of sentient beings, and the vital essence of the cream of the flavor of the True Dharma were made to abide long and increase, we are now likewise receiving these instructions upon our heads from the World-Honored One."

Within their own domains, where they possess mastery over speech and instruction, they cease all conflict and famine; furthermore, they act with diligent effort to protect and uphold [the Dharma] so that the lineage of the Triple Gem is never severed, so that the three types of vital essence may long endure and increase, so as to obstruct sentient beings of evil conduct and nurture those who practice the Dharma, so as to cause sentient beings to rest from the three evil destinies and proceed toward the three good destinies, and so that the Buddha-Dharma may abide for a long time.
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent! O Sublime Being!"
"You should act in this manner.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the ten billion Great Brahma Kings, saying:
"All those who practice the Dharma, abide in the Dharma, accord with the Dharma, and renounce evil—I now entrust them all entirely into your hands."

O virtuous ones! Within each of the realms of the ten billion four-continent worlds, where you have attained mastery over speech and commands, there are sentient beings who are wicked, cruel, and coarse, who harm others, lack compassion, and disregard the terrors of future lives; they provoke the minds of kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, and even provoke the minds of animals.

In this way, from creating the conditions for killing up to creating the conditions for wrong views, you should restrain anyone who—according to their actions—causes untimely wind and rain, or brings about the diminution of the vital essence of the earth, the vital essence of sentient beings, and the vital essence of the True Dharma, thereby causing them to abide in wholesome dharmas.

“If there are sentient beings who wish to attain goodness, who wish to attain the Dharma, who wish to cross to the other shore of birth and death; those who practice the *dānapāramitā* up to those who practice the *prajñāpāramitā*; all sentient beings who practice the Dharma and abide in the Dharma, as well as those who manage affairs for the sake of practicing the Dharma—you all should protect, support, and nurture them.”

If there are sentient beings who receive, uphold, read, recite, and explain for others various sūtras and śāstras on liberation, you should provide those sentient beings with the skillful means of mindfulness and retention to attain firm strength, so that they may enter the wisdom of not forgetting what they have heard and believe in the characteristics of all dharmas, thereby causing them to leave birth and death and cultivate the samādhi of the eightfold noble path in accordance with its roots.

If there are sentient beings within your sphere who dwell in the sequential skillful means of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā* regarding the Dharma, who are in accord with various *samādhis*, and who diligently seek to cultivate the three types of enlightenment, you should protect, sustain, and receive them; you should zealously provide for their needs through giving so that they do not suffer from lack.
If there are sentient beings who give them food and drink, clothing, bedding, or medicinal decoctions for the sake of their illnesses, you should cause those donors to increase in five benefits.
What are the five?
First, the increase of lifespan;
second, the increase of talent; [and so forth].
Third, the increase of joy;
fourth, the increase of wholesome conduct;
fifth, the increase of wisdom.
"You have obtained benefit and peace for a long night.
By this cause and condition, you shall be able to fulfill the six pāramitās and before long attain all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā)."
At that time, the Great Brahma King, Lord of the Sahā World, together with ten billion Brahma Kings, all spoke these words: "So it is, so it is."
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!

Within our respective domains, there are those who are wicked, cruel, and coarse, who afflict others, lack a heart of compassion, and disregard the terrors of future lives; we shall restrain them and cause these patrons to increase their fivefold merit."
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent! It should be so."
At that time, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all the great śrāvakas, all the devas and nāgas, and even all humans and non-humans, praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"O Great Heroic Warriors!
By acting thus, you shall cause the Dharma to endure for a long time, enabling all sentient beings to leave the evil realms and swiftly proceed toward the good realms.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke these verses:
I said to Candragarbha: "The Buddha Kṛkin entrusted [this task] to you;
for the sake of obstructing all evils throughout the four continents, including the Brahma world, you shall cause the Eye of the True Dharma to blaze forth."
Abandoning all evil deeds, they protect and uphold those who practice the Dharma;
they do not sever the lineage of the Triple Gem and increase the three vital essences;
they bring rest to all evil realms and cause beings to turn toward the various wholesome paths.
Kanakamuni, in turn, entrusted [the teaching] to the Great Brahmā King,
the gods of Paranirmita-vaśavartin and Nirmāṇarati, down to the Four Heavenly Kings.
Subsequently, Kāśyapa Buddha likewise entrusted it to the Brahmā King.
The four heavens, such as Nirmāṇarati, Śakra, and the World-Protecting Kings,
as well as the celestial sages of the past— for the sake of all the worlds—
have established the various lunar mansions and planets, commanding them to guard, sustain, and nourish [all beings].
When the age of defilement and evil arrives, and the pure dharmas have utterly perished,
I alone shall awaken to the Unsurpassed and establish and protect the people.
Now, before this great assembly, they repeatedly trouble and disturb me.
"You should set aside the preaching of the Dharma and entrust me with its protection.
Bodhisattvas from the ten directions have all gathered here;
the Heavenly Kings have also come to this Sahā Buddha-field."
I asked the Great Brahmā King: "Who was it that protected and upheld [this] in the past?
Śakra and the Great Brahmā Devas pointed toward other heavenly kings.
Then Śakra and Brahmā apologized to the Teacher, saying:
In the realms over which we rule, we obstruct all evil,
cause the seeds of the Triple Gem to flourish, and increase the three vital essences.
We block the factions of all evil associates and protect the assemblies of virtuous friends.
The Mahāsannipāta Sūtra, Scroll 51; The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra, Scroll 52.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Northern Qi Dynasty.
Chapter Ten: All Māras Attain Reverent Faith; Section Twelve: The Moon-Treasury. Chapter Ten: All Māras Attain Reverent Faith.
At that time, within the assembly, there was a Māra-king named Jupiter (Vṛhaspati). He immediately rose, joined his palms, and addressed the host of Māras in verse, saying:
"This seer Gautama now wishes to deceive and overstep me."
Distributed throughout the four continents, all the various spirits and deities,
together with the four heavenly kings, were all commanded to provide protection;
yet, excluding us, they did not grant us our share.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another Māra named Nārāyaṇacandra, who raised his hand, pointed toward the Māra Pāpīyan, and spoke these verses:
"Because of this Pāpīyan, He will not share [the merit] with us;
Such an evil person as this Will destroy our assembly."
At that time, within the assembly, there was another Māra named Rudrapiśāca, who spoke in verse:
"We shall now join together To cast far away Māra Pāpīyān;
Such a corrupt Pāpīyān, With his base and most evil dharma."
Since time immemorial, we have never before seen or heard of this;
we now all entreat the Great Master, the Sage Gautama—
the true and precious mass of the Dharma— to cause it to blaze forth and endure for a long time.
"We shall protect and uphold it, nurturing it so that it may flourish.

At that time, having seen and heard the various Māras form a single faction and deliberate together, Māra Pāpīyān felt ashamed and abashed; he rose from his seat, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and spoke this verse:
"Of all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout all the worlds..."
Forever free from false speech, you are the most honored and peerless one.
Having now offered my repentance and apology to all the Honored Teachers, I have gained deep reverence and faith; I shall henceforth take refuge with single-minded resolve.
“World-Honored One, for what reason do you still regard him with such loathing and contempt?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Candragarbha, speaking in verse:
“O pure gentleman who has attained full understanding, such is this Māra Pāpīyān.”
Now, although they have indeed created all manner of obstacles against me, none are able to exhaustively recount their faults.
They sincerely repent before me; this is not out of a deceitful or crooked intent.
With profound reverence and faith in the Triple Gem, he honors them as never before.
Therefore, I now bestow upon this Māra Pāpīyas the prophecy of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and true wisdom.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Candragarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

The minds of ordinary beings are frivolous, hesitant, and unstable; they do not abide in the ultimate within the Three Vehicles, and they cannot reach certainty regarding good or evil. Their aspirations are likewise unsettled, and because they are unsettled, they encounter spiritual friends and thereby give rise to pure faith."

By means of the causal condition of faith, one is able to generate superior vows through all the wholesome deeds performed by body, speech, and mind; through the causal conditions of that virtuous mind and superior vow, one attains the most excellent and wondrous fruits of retribution according to whatever is desired.
“O Great Virtuous Blessed One!

It is like a herd of cows that eat various kinds of grass, whether fresh or withered, and drink various kinds of water, whether clear or turbid; yet when they are milked, they yield pure milk. From that pure milk comes fragrant and flavorful curd; from the fragrant and flavorful curd comes fresh butter; and from the fresh butter comes the superior ghee, the ripened fruit of excellence.”
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!
In this way, an ordinary person whose wholesome mind continues in succession can give rise to pure faith; through the causal conditions of that faith, they subsequently give rise to a superior vow;
through such a sequence, they attain the great and wondrous fruit."
"So it is, World-Honored One!
It is likewise for those who have set out in the Mahāyāna: until they have attained the patience of compliance (kṣānti-anulomika), their minds remain constantly hesitant, wavering, and unstable."

Having attained the patient acceptance that accords with reality (anulomikī-kṣānti), one cultivates the six pāramitās within the Mahāyāna; with a mind free from weariness, one progressively advances until finally attaining the status of a sovereign Dharma King by natural law.
“O Great Virtuous Blessed One!

It is like when excrement and filth are scattered in a wild field, and various seeds are sown therein and irrigated with water; through the assistance of human effort, the causes and conditions being fully complete, the flowers, leaves, and fruits of those seeds reach full maturity.”
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!

If an ordinary person, with a mind of hesitation, practices the six pāramitās within the Mahāyāna, training sequentially until they attain the patience of compliance (anulomikī-kṣānti), they will before long fulfill the six pāramitās and achieve perfect awakening in unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment."

Thus, although Pāpīyān has in the past committed various evils, his afflictions have been blazing, and through his various mental activities and the unwholesome deeds of body, speech, and mind, he ought to undergo the retribution of suffering.
Now, having attained deep reverence and faith in the presence of the Buddha, they have sincerely repented and resolved their minds upon unexcelled bodhi.
Having thus resolved their minds, they immediately receive the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and shall successively attain the state of the Unexcelled Dharma King.
“O Great Virtuous Blessed One!

It is like a caravan leader who, though he had not previously seen the ocean or the island of jewels, prepared his provisions and did not lose his way; together with the merchants, through diligent application of effort, he gradually crossed to the other shore of the great ocean and reached that various island of mani-jewels.”
"O Virtuous Bhagavān!

If this Pāpīyān can sincerely confess and repent for all his evil karma, and with all his roots of goodness wholeheartedly dedicate them toward unsurpassed bodhi, exerting great courage and vigor, then he will be able to swiftly fulfill the six pāramitās, cross the great ocean of birth and death within the three realms of existence, bring all boundless merits to complete perfection, and reach the precious island of all-encompassing wisdom—a place that cannot be reached by those of the two vehicles."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Candragarbha, saying: “O Purified One! It is so, it is so.”

As you have said, this Māra Pāpīyān has now, before me, confessed and repented for all the evil karma he committed in the past; having attained purity, he has resolved to attain unsurpassed bodhicitta.
Therefore, I now bestow upon this Pāpīyān the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; in a future age, he shall attain the state of the Unsurpassed Dharma King.
At that time, there were also ten billion māras who all rose from their seats simultaneously, joined their palms toward the Buddha, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

We, too, shall rouse great valor to protect and nurture the True Dharma of the Buddha, causing the seeds of the Triple Gem to flourish and endure long in the world, so that the vital essence of the earth, the vital essence of sentient beings, and the vital essence of the Dharma may all increase.

If there are disciples of the World-Honored One who abide in the Dharma, accord with the Dharma, and practice in accordance with the three types of action, we shall all protect, sustain, and nourish them, ensuring that they lack nothing whatsoever that they may require.
Furthermore, there are disciples of the World-Honored One who possess no accumulations;
they are free from the turbidity and confusion of afflictions and from strife and contention, do not engage in mutual litigation, and seek neither fame nor profit.

They feel shame and abashment toward all unwholesome dharmas, do not associate with the fourfold assembly or their kinsmen and friends, and having abandoned the villages, dwell alone in secluded forests.
To those who dwell in accordance with all wholesome dharmas with firm and courageous resolve, as if their very heads were on fire,
we shall together protect, support, and nurture them, ensuring they lack nothing whatsoever that is required.
We shall completely ward off all evil beings and [protect against] all strife and famine in every place.
I shall provide protection against epidemics, hostile enemies from other regions, untimely winds and rains, freezing cold,
scorching heat, mosquitoes, gadflies, snakes, scorpions, and various other insects and beasts; I shall cause them to attain reverence and faith.
He shall cause the kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and even animals to likewise revere and have faith in the Buddha’s True Dharma;

he shall also cause all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, garuḍas, kumbhāṇḍas, pretas, piśācas, pūtanas, and kaṭapūtanas to likewise revere and have faith in the Buddha’s True Dharma.

Furthermore, may all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, garuḍas, kumbhāṇḍas, pretas, piśācas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, and so forth, be endowed with vital energy, possess abundant physical strength and vigor, and be fully satisfied with excellent fragrances and delicious flavors, lacking nothing.

May all the grasses, trees, roots, stems, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits upon the earth flourish; may the five grains and cultivated crops grow lush and lustrous; and may all clothing likewise be abundant. May the soil be fertile and entirely delightful. May monasteries, gardens, groves, rivers, springs, ponds, wells, palaces, houses, mountains, marshes, forests, and wilds all be made complete. May all sentient beings find joy in their hearts and physical ease in those dwelling places, free from weariness.

Furthermore, World-Honored One, if among the śrāvaka disciples there should be those who accumulate [defilements], who are distracted by afflictions, indolent, lazy, or who act contrary to the Dharma, I shall abandon them and no longer protect or sustain them; instead, I shall remain established in my own cultivation, nurturing myself. Now, I shall never intentionally speak falsehoods or commit defiled offenses before the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent! You who have mastery over all desires!"
"You should thus cause my Dharma to blaze brightly, even unto the point of bestowing peace and happiness upon all sentient beings.
O worthy ones!
I now entrust the Dharma-eye once more to all the kings of men throughout Jambudvīpa."

If my disciples within my Dharma harbor craving and accumulation, engage in the strife of afflictions, become defiled by worldly associations, and form intimate ties with friends while greedily seeking fame and profit; if they act contrary to the True Dharma in body, speech, and mind, causing devas and humans to lose their respect and faith, delighting in committing various evils and dwelling in unwholesome paths;

then, for the sake of ensuring that the Buddha-Dharma may endure for a long time and so that devas and humans may regain their respect and faith, you must cause the kings of Jambudvīpa and others to rule according to the Dharma.

At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed ten billion Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas, ten billion Nirmāṇarati devas, ten billion Tuṣita devas, ten billion Suyāma devas, and ten billion Śakra-devānām-indras, saying: "O worthy ones!
"I have taught the Dharma and Vinaya; I entrust them to you all. You should protect and uphold them, establishing and nurturing them as previously described.
Having spoken these words, the five heavenly kings addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If there are disciples of the World-Honored One who dwell in accordance with the Dharma, conform to the Dharma, and practice with their three karmas in harmony, we shall all together protect, support, and nurture them, providing whatever they require so that they lack for nothing.
Furthermore, World-Honored One, if a śrāvaka disciple of yours possesses no accumulations, you should protect, support, and nurture them as previously described;

however, if a śrāvaka disciple of yours dwells in accumulation and even acts in ways that are inconsistent with the Dharma through the three karmas, you should likewise abandon them and no longer provide support, remaining instead in the cultivation of yourself.
"I shall never, for the sake of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, intentionally utter false speech or commit a defiled offense.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent!"
"O Wondrous Being!
You should act in this way so that my Buddha-dharma may blaze forth and endure for a long time, granting peace, stability, and happiness to all sentient beings.
At that time, the entire great assembly who had gathered—the devas, humans, gandharvas, and others—also praised those five heavenly kings, saying:
“Excellent, excellent! O Sublime Being!
We have never before heard of such protection and nurturing, whereby the True Dharma of all Buddhas shall long abide in the world, gods and humans shall flourish, and the evil realms shall diminish.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke these verses:
"In this Sahā world, when the Bhadrakalpa first began,
Tathāgata Krakucchanda had already entrusted [this matter] to the four heavenly kings."
Śakra and Brahmā, the King of Devas, protect and sustain them,
causing the seeds of the Triple Gem to flourish and the three vital essences to increase.
Kanakamuni likewise entrusted the four continents [to their care].
The Brahmā and Śakra kings, and all the celestial lords, shall protect and nurture [him].
Kāśyapa is likewise; having entrusted the four continents to Brahmā, Śakra, and the world-protecting kings, they shall guard those who practice the Dharma.
The multitude of sages of the past, as well as the celestial beings and the various constellations and planetary deities,
were likewise entrusted with the task of disseminating [this teaching].
Having appeared in this world of five turbidities, I have subdued all Māras and adversaries.
He convened a great assembly and manifested the Buddha’s true Dharma.
All the devas made their request that it be distributed throughout the four continents.
At that time, I questioned Brahmā: "Who was formerly entrusted with this charge?"
Neither Brahmā nor Śakra, Lord of the Devas, spoke of themselves;
having surveyed all the devas, they then offered repentance and thanks to the Buddha.
All the hosts of devas together addressed the Buddha, saying:
In all the realms over which we rule, we shall protect and uphold the True Dharma,
cause the seeds of the Triple Gem to flourish, and increase the three vital essences;
we shall bring to rest all plagues and epidemics, as well as famine and strife.
The Tathāgatas of the past Instructed me to establish [this teaching];
Now the Honored Teacher, the Guide, Also commands that it be protected and upheld.
The World-Honored One further addressed The billions of Brahmā devas:
Ten billion Śakras, Lords of Devas, and ten billion Caturmahārājas:
each of you, within your respective four continents,
wherever you exercise sovereignty, shall restrain and ward off evil beings.
Not allowing the mind to be disturbed or turbid, dwelling securely in a wholesome state,
those who practice the True Dharma should be endowed with mindfulness.
If there are any śrāvakas who diligently seek nirvāṇa, [they should likewise be so].
Whatever they may require, all shall be provided for them;
furthermore, the donor shall likewise increase in five meritorious qualities:
long life as their reward, peace and happiness, diligence, and wisdom.
They are able to swiftly fulfill the six perfections and realize great bodhi.
Thus, hundreds of thousands of billions of devas and Great Brahma Kings all addressed the Buddha together, saying:
Protecting all śrāvakas, Shielding against evil beings,
Abiding securely in the Buddha’s true Dharma, And causing the seeds of the Triple Gem to flourish,
They cause the three kinds of essential flavor and vigor To increase in every way.
The billions of māra hosts all simultaneously felt shame and remorse;
they too rose from their seats, joined their palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We have all resolved to protect and uphold the Buddha’s true Dharma."
Kindling the seeds of the Triple Gem, increasing the three vital essences,
and establishing all sentient beings so that they may dwell in the wholesome paths—
for the sake of all sentient beings, he brings all evils to rest.
Protecting the World-Honored One and the śrāvakas who practice the Dharma,
upholding the Buddha’s true and wondrous Dharma, may their three karmas always be in accord with it;
with all necessary provisions, nourish and support them so that they lack for nothing.
If there are any śrāvakas who possess nothing accumulated,
who remain far removed from strife and dispute, who feel shame regarding fame and profit,
and who are firm and diligent in their vigor— like one whose head is on fire— then they shall attain the goal.
He is able to cause immeasurable multitudes To dwell securely in the True Dharma.
All places of evil Are made entirely delightful;
The seeds produced from the earth, Fruits, medicinal herbs, and all crops—
May they all flourish, endowed with moisture, fragrance, and flavor.
If there are any śrāvakas who greedily seek accumulation,
who are full of anger, envy, and litigation, and who pursue profit without shame—
"If there are such as these, we shall abandon them.
Regarding the Buddhas of the three periods of time, I shall never commit a lie.
The Guide further addressed them:
“You hosts of Māras, you kings who protect the nations, and you obstructors of evil beings. Chapter Eleven:

The Protection by the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra The Twelfth Part of the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*, the "Moon Store" Section: Chapter Eleven, "The Protection by the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra. At that time, within the four continents of this world-system, the Sun Devaputra and the Moon Devaputra addressed the Devaputra Swift and Firm, saying:

“The World-Honored One is currently holding a great assembly on Mount Khadiraka, the dwelling place of the sages and seers. For the sake of causing the Buddha-dharma to endure for a long time, for the sake of ensuring that the lineage of the Triple Gem continues without interruption, for the sake of preventing the three kinds of vital essence from diminishing, for the sake of inspiring reverence and faith in wicked sentient beings, for the sake of bringing rest to the three evil realms, and for the sake of increasing the three good realms, you should go quickly to that great assembly and declare your desire to rejoice in it. I and my retinue shall protect, uphold, and nurture the Buddha’s True Dharma.”
Then the devaputra Drutagati-dṛḍha went to where the Buddha was.
Having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Sun Deva and the Moon Deva, from afar, prostrated at the Buddha's feet and spoke thus:
"Since we were traveling swiftly by means of our celestial chariots, we were unable to go to that place of the great assembly."

I and my retinue express our desire to rejoice; we shall protect and uphold the Buddha’s true Dharma, establishing and nurturing it so that the seeds of the Triple Gem may flourish. We shall also cause the five planets and the twenty-eight lunar mansions to move in their proper courses, causing the three types of vital essence to increase, and we shall obstruct all unwholesome beings so that the assembly of those with wholesome dharmas may become abundant and full, such that the wholesome qualities of humans and devas are perfectly complete.
The Buddha said: "Sons of Heaven, the Sun and the Moon!
Since you protect, uphold, and nurture my Dharma, may you enjoy long life free from all decline and affliction."

At that time, there were also ten billion kings of the Dhṛtarāṣṭra heaven, ten billion kings of the Virūḍhaka heaven, ten billion kings of the Virūpākṣa heaven, and ten billion kings of the Vaiśravaṇa heaven. They all rose from their seats simultaneously along with their retinues, adjusted their robes, joined their palms in reverent salutation, and spoke these words:
"O Great Virtuous Bhagavān!

Each of us, within our respective realms, shall diligently protect, uphold, and nurture the Buddha-dharma, causing the seed of the Triple Gem to flourish and endure for a long time, and ensuring that the three kinds of vital essence all increase. Furthermore, regarding those disciples of the World-Honored One’s śrāvakas who dwell in accordance with the three kinds of wholesome karma, we shall diligently protect, sustain, and nourish them, so that their minds remain untainted, free from all distraction, and they may proceed toward the gate of Nirvāṇa.

For as long as time may last, we shall constantly shield all sentient beings with evil minds, causing the assembly of those who practice wholesome dharmas to abide for a long time and to increase; we shall cause all strife, pestilence, famine, untimely winds and rains, frost and cold, poisonous heat, bitter and pungent sensations, harsh textures, lack of flavor, dryness, and all foul, impure, and unpleasant evils to completely cease.

Why is this? Because the disciples of the World-Honored One do not accumulate [worldly things], but constantly cultivate a mind of loving-kindness, abiding in accordance with virtue and free from all distraction.
The Buddha said: “Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!”
"You should thus diligently protect, uphold, receive, and nurture the Dharma-eye of the Buddhas that I have cultivated.
The entire great assembly also praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Joyful Excellence, saying:
"O Worthy Man! Within this Jambudvīpa of the four continents, you should protect and sustain the fourth division in the eastern quarter."
Why is this? Because this Jambudvīpa is the place where all Buddhas arise; therefore, you should provide the most supreme protection and support for it.

All Buddhas of the past have already instructed you to protect, support, and nurture it; all Buddhas of the future shall do likewise. Furthermore, you, your sons, the hosts of gandharvas, the yakṣas, and all your retinues should be made to respect, believe in, protect, support, and nurture it.

"You have ninety-one sons who delight in various activities; some travel throughout the ten directions riding elephants, others riding horses, others riding camels, others riding bulls, others riding black goats, others riding white sheep, others riding dragons, others riding birds, others riding men, others riding women, and others riding boys or girls as they travel throughout the ten directions. You, too, should cause them to give rise to respectful faith, and you shall together with them protect the fourth eastern quarter of Jambudvīpa."

“Furthermore, there are gandharva ministers and generals of great power: first named Pañcika, next Pāñcāla, next Laṅkāra, next Śāṇḍa, next Khimavaddha, next Citrasena, next Nata-rāja, next Dhyāniliśava, next Śivaka, next Mucilinda, next Viśvamitra, and next Cūḍapanthaka, and so forth. All of these are your ministers and generals of great power; you should also cause them to give rise to respectful faith, and together with them, you shall protect the fourth part of Jambudvīpa in the eastern direction.”
Furthermore, there were four mahā-cakravartin generals of great power, each with a vast host of soldiers:
the first was named Priyadīrghakarṇa;
the second was named Priyadīrghanāsa.
The third is named Supūrṇa; the fourth is named Khadiravaṭī.
These Cāraṇas are all your powerful army generals; you should also cause them to give rise to respectful faith, and together with them, you shall protect the fourth eastern quarter of Jambudvīpa.
"Furthermore, there are three brothers who are Gandharva generals of great power; they constantly lead their troops and possess great influence. They all receive your commands:
the first is named Rati, the second is named Rāga, and the third is named Gīta."

Furthermore, there were eleven gandharva brothers: the first was named Vṛika, the second Pāṇṭi, the third Lambukaśita, the fourth Karada, the fifth Kruñcasvara, the sixth Yaśaśrī, the seventh Yaśapanta, the eighth Yaśodharā, the ninth Mārapandu, the tenth Māramanda, and the eleventh Mathumanta.
Furthermore, there were three gandharva brothers:
the first was named Śrīmandu; the second was named Dhṛtimanta; [and the third was named...].
The third is Puṣpamāndhātṛ.
Furthermore, there were thirty-three gandharvas: the first was named Satyamāndhātṛ, the second Yaśomāndhātṛ, the third Dānamāndhātṛ, the fourth Nandika, and the fifth...
Utpala, next named Padma, next named Candana, next named Candana,
next named Dūrumārasa, next named Pañcāla, next named Kucirasupāra, next named Jambhula, next named Pañcaśīrṣaka, next named Sā...
Vani, next named Surasa, next named Marāvi, next named Vardhana,
next named Kāmaśrīṭa, next named Nirgrantha, next named Nirgranthaka, next named Bhadrapura, next named Yaśodharā, and next named Viśva.
Bamitiduo; next, named Shiqianduo; next, named Tiangu; next, named Madouluo; next, named Zhiduolisi na; next, named Nadawang;
next, named Chananalisha po; next, named Shipoka; next, named Muzhenlinduo; next, named Bi...
Śubhamitra, next is named Cūḍanirghoṣa. These Gandharvas possess many hosts and great power;
you should also cause them to give rise to respectful faith, and together with them, you shall protect the fourth part of Jambudvīpa in the eastern direction.

"Furthermore, there are sixteen celestial deities of great power who are endowed with supernatural faculties (*abhijñā*). Their names are: first, Most Victorious; second, Superior Victory; third, Accomplished Meaning; fourth, Unconquerable by Others; fifth, Supreme Joy; sixth, Joyful Army; seventh, Delight in Joy; eighth, Increasing Joy; ninth, Abundant Wealth; tenth, Greatly Abundant Wealth; eleventh, Endowed with Hair; twelfth, Ten Hairs; thirteenth, Abundant Hair; fourteenth, *Utpala*; fifteenth, *Padmaka*; and sixteenth, *Śyāma*. These sixteen celestial kings possess great majesty and power; you should also cause them to give rise to reverent faith, and together with them, you shall protect the fourth eastern quarter of Jambudvīpa."

“In the eastern direction there is a place named Cāpala, where the Buddhas of the past once resided, and which is also the place where arhats and other noble sages attained the fruits of realization. It is the dwelling place upon which devas, humans, and others rely when they resolve to practice; you should protect the fourth division of Jambudvīpa in the eastern direction with the power of great diligence.”

“In the east there is a mountain named Avata, and next to it one named Riṣivabha; these were also the original sites where the Buddhas and sages of the past practiced their cultivation. By relying on these places, devas and humans alike attained the vision of the Noble Truths. Therefore, you all should, with the power of great diligence, protect the fourth division of Jambudvīpa in the east.”

“In the eastern direction, there are furthermore three luminaries, seven lunar mansions, and three celestial maidens; you should command them to traverse the world throughout its days and nights, and together with them, protect the fourth part of Jambudvīpa in the east.”

"Furthermore, in the eastern direction, there are devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, pretas, piśācas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, and others who dwell in your eastern quarter without a specific affiliation; I shall later distribute them and establish them in various lands so that they may protect and sustain you."
At that time, the Deva-king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Joyful Excellence, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One! It is so, it is so.”

"O Great Virtuous Blessed One, the Buddhas of the past entrusted us with the task of establishing, protecting, and nurturing [this realm], and they also instructed us to protect the eastern continent of Pūrvavideha; this is now no different from the instruction given to us by the World-Honored One today."

With a profound mind, I shall reverently receive and uphold the Buddha’s True Dharma; I shall protect and maintain the fourth quarter of the eastern region of Jambudvīpa, and I shall likewise cause my various palaces and retinues, both great and small, to provide protection and maintenance, causing all beings in the three evil realms to find rest and ensuring that the three good paths flourish everywhere.

At that time, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Delightful Victory, together with his ministers and assistants, the kṣatriyas, men and women, and boys and girls, all rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Buddha, prostrated themselves at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!

We have now conceived deep faith in the World-Honored One, our Teacher; we have attained a sense of respect, veneration, and admiration such as we have never known before. We have likewise conceived deep faith in the Dharma Jewel and the Sangha Jewel; we have attained a sense of respect, veneration, and admiration such as we have never known before.

"O Great Virtuous Blessed One! From this day forth, we shall diligently protect and sustain the fourth eastern quarter of Jambudvīpa. For all the World-Honored One’s śrāvaka disciples—whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—as well as other sentient beings who abide in accordance with the three wholesome karmas; those who reverently believe in the Triple Gem, making offerings and gifts and listening to and receiving the Dharma; those who resolve their minds toward the Buddha’s True Dharma, practicing it and abiding in accordance with the observance of the precepts; and those who diligently make offerings to the Saṃgha—we shall constantly protect, sustain, and nurture them."

Furthermore, if there are other sentient beings who dwell in araṇyas, as well as disciples of the Buddha who abide in and accord with the Dharma, whose resolve is as firm as the horn of a rhinoceros, and who dwell alone without companions in secluded forests—we shall provide them with all their necessities, making offerings, supporting, protecting, and nurturing them.

Furthermore, if there are any other sentient beings who see those dwelling in association with that secluded grove and are able to diligently provide them with their necessities, we shall likewise protect and nurture them, ensuring that all their needs are met to their satisfaction; we shall also grant them long life free from decline and disease, sovereign wealth, peace and happiness, and the widespread distribution of their good reputation.
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!

We shall perform such deeds as these to protect, uphold, and nurture the True Dharma of the Buddha; we shall cause all strife, pestilence, famine, scarcity, and unseasonable winds and rains to cease entirely. Furthermore, we shall cause all flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, the five grains, and other things to flourish, ripen, become succulent and soft, and to abound with excellent fragrance, exquisite flavor, and wondrous color."

Furthermore, it causes the essence of the earth, the essence of sentient beings, and the essence of the Dharma—the cream of the cream—to flourish and increase. Because such refined essences thus grow, the three evil realms are stilled and the paths of the virtuous become full; the Buddha-dharma abides for a long time, blazing brightly throughout the world.
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent! O sublime man!"
