If you all diligently perform such deeds as these—to protect, uphold, and nurture [the teachings] so that my Dharma-eye may long endure and blaze forth, and so that the well-expounded Dharma and Vinaya may give rise to faith and understanding—then you will have fully made offerings to all Buddhas of the three periods of time.

You shall then attain an increase in lifespan, an increase in the Dharma, an increase in retinue, an increase in reputation, an increase in physical strength and vitality, an increase in virtuous friends, an increase in dwellings, an increase in faith, an increase in ethical discipline, an increase in learning, an increase in diligence, an increase in mindfulness, and an increase in wisdom. Because such matters as these increase, you will be able to swiftly fulfill the six pāramitās and achieve the state of the unsurpassed, self-arisen Dharma King, just as I am now.
At that time, the entire great assembly that had gathered—the devas, humans, gandharvas, and others—all praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! O Wondrous Man!"
"You should thus diligently protect and uphold the true Dharma of all Buddhas, causing it to endure for a long time, blazing forth in the world so that it shall never be severed.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke in verse:
"The two with supernatural powers in the world, The sun and moon, have sent an envoy to come; The Buddha has dispatched me to you, To inform you of the Tathāgata’s passing."
Swift-moving and firm, the devaputra Tianzi, together with the great assembly,
now desires this true Dharma of the Buddha; we shall protect it,
causing the seeds of the Triple Gem to flourish, so that the stars may move in their proper courses.
Increasing the three vital essences, Shielding against evil beings,
The assembly of the Dharma increases, And all good paths are filled to overflowing.
Ten billion Dhṛtarāṣṭras, Virūḍhaka, and Virūpākṣa—
Ten billion Vaiśravaṇas all addressed the Buddha together:
"Within our respective realms, we shall each diligently provide protection and support,
even for those bhikṣus who have few desires and refrain from amassing possessions."
"We shall restrain all evils, and the community of Dharma-friends shall increase;
may strife, disease, and famine—all such evils—be brought to rest.
The Guide, the Buddha, spoke these words:
The Tathāgatas of the past have already instructed you to establish yourself and protect the fourth eastern quarter of Jambudvīpa; you,
along with your army and retinue, shall likewise cause the Eye of Dharma to increase.
Dhṛtarāṣṭra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"My army is a host of great power; may the Eye of Dharma cause it to blaze forth, eliminating all unwholesome dharmas and shielding against evil sentient beings."
They constantly protect all the śrāvakas who possess no accumulations.
All the gandharvas arise and likewise address the Buddha, saying:
"The śrāvakas have no accumulations; we shall ensure they never lack food or drink."
We shall uphold the Dharma for those who dwell within the realm of the Dharma;
we shall nurture those donors and likewise protect them.
We shall shield them from evil beings and cause the assembly of Dharma friends to flourish.
The three kinds of vital essence increase, And all wholesome paths are filled to capacity.

Chapter Twelve: The Chapter on the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka The Great Collection Sūtra, Moon Store Section, Chapter Twelve: The Chapter on the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka At that time, the Buddha addressed the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka, the Flower-Spark, saying:
“O Wondrous Being!
"This fourth division in the southern quarter of Jambudvīpa within these four continents, you should protect and uphold. Why is this?
Because this Jambudvīpa is the place where all Buddhas arise; therefore, you should protect and uphold it most preeminently."

The Buddhas of the past have already instructed you to protect, uphold, and nurture [this teaching]; the Buddhas of the future shall do likewise; and I command that you, along with your children, all your retinues, ministers, military generals, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, all provide protection and support.

"You have ninety-one sons who delight in various activities; some travel through the ten directions riding elephants, and others even travel through the ten directions riding young boys or girls. You should also cause them to give rise to reverent faith, so that together they may protect the fourth part of Jambudvīpa in the southern direction."

Furthermore, there are Kumbhāṇḍa ministers who possess numerous troops and great power: the first is named Varuṇaka, the second Aṭavaka, the third Bhaṭaka, the fourth Sūciloma, the fifth Asimukha, the sixth Daṇḍasiti, the seventh Madhura, the eighth Daṇḍanimi, the ninth Tiriṭivaka, the tenth Candana, the eleventh Karakanda, the twelfth Sūmukha, and the thirteenth Dhatimukha.
Furthermore, there were four kṣatrapas:
the first was named Vajracakra;
the second was named Vajrajvāla.
The third was named Arrow-Hair;
the fourth was named Wind-King.
They all possessed great armies of powerful forces.
Furthermore, there were nine brothers who were powerful kumbhāṇḍa generals:
the first was named Dandika;
the second was named Upadandika; [and so on for the remaining seven].
Third, Kakasa; fourth, Paśi; fifth, Mahāpaśiva.
Sixth, named Great Belly;
seventh, named Elephant Hand;
eighth, named Ten Hands.
The ninth is named Fire-Hand.
Furthermore, there are three kumbhāṇḍa brothers:
the first is named Earth-Walker;
The second is named Mountain-Walker;
the third is named Left-Walker.
Furthermore, there are three brothers who are kumbhāṇḍas:
The first is named Black;
the second is named Crimson Eyes;
the third is named Cloud Color.
Furthermore, there were four brothers who were kumbhāṇḍas:
the first was named Vimala;
the second was named Nirvraṇa.
The third is named Cloud Heaven;
the fourth is named Great Power.

Furthermore, there were twenty-six *kumbhāṇḍas*: the first was named Long Ears; the next, Long Breasts; the next, Solitary Elephant; the next, Braided Hair; the next, Ten Mortars; the next, Ten Eyes; the next, Solitary Tree; the next, Delight in Desire; the next, Great Desire; the next, Carpenter; the next, Fond of Sons; the next, Three *Kumbhāṇḍa* Sons; the next, All Alleys; the next, Variegated Colors; the next, Painted Eyes; the next, Full Vase; the next, Vase-Eyes; the next, Free from Illness; the next, *Cūccha*; the next, Yellow Hair; the next, Many *Cañca*; the next, *Cañca-Cañca*; the next, Thread; the next, Flesh-Eater; the next, Horse-Water; and the last, Bone-Marrow Eater.

These Kumbhāṇḍas are powerful military generals with great might and vast armies; you should also cause them to give rise to reverent faith, so that together they may protect the fourth division of the southern region of Jambudvīpa.

Furthermore, there were sixteen celestial kings: the first was named Jālinī, the second Jālamukha, the third Puṇḍarīka, the fourth Suprabha, the fifth Tejorāśi, the sixth Ekānta, the seventh Bahvantaka, the eighth Citra, the ninth Candrādhipati, the tenth Viśvabhadra, the eleventh Rātri, the twelfth Abhibhū, the thirteenth Anabhibhū, the fourteenth Duṣki, the fifteenth Vasuki, and the sixteenth Aparājita.

These sixteen celestial kings and their divine generals possess vast armies and great power; you should also cause them to give rise to reverence and faith, so that together they may protect the fourth division of Jambudvīpa in the southern quarter.
“In the south there is a stūpa named Suvihita; there, in the past, various Buddhas, sages, and noble ones once dwelt and perceived the Four Noble Truths.
In the south there is a mountain named Sudarśana; there too, in the past, various Buddhas and assemblies of noble ones dwelt and perceived the Four Noble Truths.”

Furthermore, in the southern quarter there are three luminaries, seven lunar mansions, and three celestial maidens; you also should cause them to act rightly in the world, together protecting the fourth division of Jambudvīpa in the south.

"Furthermore, in the southern direction, there are devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, kumbhāṇḍas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, pretas, piśācas, pūtanas, and kaṭapūtanas who dwell in your southern quarter and have no other affiliation. I shall later distribute and establish them according to their respective lands, and cause you all to protect and nurture them."
At that time, the celestial king Vaiśravaṇa, Flower-Fire, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One! It is so, it is so.”
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!

The Buddhas of the past have already entrusted me with the command to establish [this teaching], and the devas and ṛṣis of the past also instructed me to establish and protect the fourth southern division of Jambudvīpa; now the World-Honored One likewise instructs me to establish it."

I shall receive this upon my head and uphold, protect, and nurture it; I, along with my retinue, ministers, and military generals, shall likewise uphold, protect, and nurture the Buddha-dharma, until even the three evil realms are entirely brought to rest and the three good paths are increased and filled to overflowing.

At that time, the celestial king Vaiśravaṇa, together with his retinue—the kṣatrapas, ministers, assistants, kumbhāṇḍas, generals, men and women, and boys and girls—all rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Buddha, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!

We have now attained a profound faith, reverence, and veneration for the World-Honored One, our Teacher, such as we have never before experienced; likewise, we have attained a profound faith, reverence, and veneration for the Jewel of the Dharma and the Jewel of the Sangha, such as we have never before experienced.
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!

From this day forth, we shall diligently nurture and protect the fourth division of Jambudvīpa in the southern quarter, until the Buddha’s True Dharma remains long and flourishes, the evil paths are stilled, and the good paths are filled."
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent! O Sublime Being!"
Thereupon, the entire assembly that had gathered—the devas, humans, gandharvas, and all others—unanimously praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke these verses:
The Buddha told Virūḍhaka, the minister Kumbhāṇḍa:
"In the past, the Buddhas instructed you to protect the southern quarter;
the celestial seers of antiquity likewise taught you to establish yourself there."
The companions of the blazing True Dharma shall obstruct the evil sentient beings.
The Guide now tells you: "Cause my Dharma to blaze forth;
receive this entrustment from me, the Right Dharma Eye of the Tathāgata."
The seeds of the Triple Gem blaze brightly; the three kinds of vital essence increase.
Food, drink, various flavors, and medicines are abundant and delightful.
The bhikṣus who dwell in the Dharma possess nothing whatsoever in accumulation.
One should protect and nurture [the recipient], ensuring they lack for nothing;
one should also protect the donor, so that these five matters— wealth, life, happiness, prosperity, and wisdom—
are constantly benefited and all cause them to increase.

"May all the lunar mansions, constellations, years, and four seasons be correctly practiced, causing the three evil realms to be exhausted and the paths of goodness to be filled to overflowing. Chapter 13:

The Chapter on the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa The Great Collection Sūtra, Section on the Moon Treasury, Part 12: The Chapter on the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa, Chapter 13 At that time, the Buddha addressed the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa, Candanapuṣpa, saying:
“O Sublime Being! You should protect and uphold the fourth western division of Jambudvīpa within this world-system of four continents. Why is this?
This Jambudvīpa is the place where all Buddhas arise; therefore, you should protect and uphold it with the highest devotion.
All Buddhas of the past have already instructed you to protect and nurture it, and all Buddhas of the future shall do likewise, as will your son, your ministers, and your retinue.
"You have ninety-one sons who delight in various practices as described above.
Furthermore, there are various nāgas, ministers, and military hosts of great power:
one is named Siṃha;..."
The second was named Siṃhakeśa; the third, Īśvara;
and the fourth, Piṅgala.
The fifth is named Yellow Weasel;
the sixth is named Red-Eyed;
the seventh is named Gaudama.
The eighth is named Mountain-Water.
Furthermore, there are four more *kṣatriyas*:
the first is named Aṅgū;... [and so on].
The second name is Māṅgū;
the third name is Lambakaccha; the fourth name is Śākha.
"Furthermore, there are various nāga generals who possess great power and constantly lead their armies;
the first is named Nanda, the second Upananda, the third Suprabha,
the fourth Anavatapta, the fifth Vāsuki, the sixth Suvyūha, and the seventh Devadatta."
Next is named Takṣaka; next is named Varuṇa; next is named Vāsava; next is named Aruṇa;
next is named Hūluda; next is named Bhṛṅgāra; next is named Saṃjñāra; next is named Guṇa; next is named Suguna; next is named Pūrṇaguṇa; next...
The first is named False Practice (Mṛṣācāra); next is named Pārśa; next is named Mahāpārśa;
next is named Dhyāna; next is named Gṛhapati; next is named Sāgara; next is named Jambūpati;
next is named Śyāmala; next is named Subāhu; next is named Sumana; and next is named Sūryaprabha.
Next is named Candraprabha; next is named Candranetra; next is named Candana; next is named Subhadra;
next is named Sunetra; next is named Citra; next is named Varṇadatta; next is named Añji;
next is named Mukhaliṇda; next is named Lambula; next is named Kanaka.
Next is named Hastikarṇa; next is named Pañcika; next is named Śaṅkha; next is named Elāpattra; next is named Apalāla; next is named Nalada;
next is named Upala; next is named Śrīka; next is named Āmradeva; next is named Bāhula.
Next is named Mithilā; next is named Campā; next is named Gautamī; next is named Pañcālī;
next is named Kāliṅgī; next is named Vatsapalī; next is named Vimalā;
next is named Parvatā; next is named Gaṅgā; next is named Sindhu; next...
The one named Vakṣa, the next named Sitaśva, and these sixty-one nāgas such as these are all your powerful army generals.

Furthermore, among the sixteen celestial deities of the western quarter, there are also hosts of beings with great power: the first is named Śaśapāti, the next Śiśapāti, the next Yaśodharā, the next Yaśavati, the next Ugrasena, the next Prathamasādhu, the next Sujñāna, the next Susamudgata, the next Chanda, the next Vichanda, the next Vimala, the next Virūḍhaka, the next Goṣṭha, the next Campaka, the next Uruvilvā, and the last Kakkhaṭaśila.

"Furthermore, there is a stūpa in the western direction named Utter Rain; there is a mountain named Fragrant Wind; there is a mountain named Multicolored Tiered Pavilion; and furthermore, in the western direction, there are three luminaries, seven lunar mansions, and three celestial maidens, all of whom practice correctly to protect the fourth division of Jambudvīpa in the west."

"O all you devas, nāgas, ghosts, and even kaṭapūtanas who dwell in the western quarter and have no other affiliation, I shall later distribute and establish you according to their respective lands, and likewise cause you to protect and nurture [those regions]."
At that time, the celestial king Vairocana-candana-puṣpa spoke these words:
"O Great Virtuous Bhagavān!

In the past, the Buddhas of the past already instructed me in this way to settle, protect, and nurture the fourth western division of this Jambudvīpa; it is no different from what the World-Honored One has now instructed me to do."

"I now, before the Buddha, receive this solemn instruction to protect and uphold the True Dharma of all Buddhas of the Western Quarter, and even to cause the auspicious paths to be filled to overflowing.
At that time, Virūpākṣa again spoke in verse before the Buddha:
"King Virūpākṣa, together with his dragon ministers, speaks thus:"
The Buddhas and celestial seers of the past have commanded me to protect the western quarter,
together with the hosts of nāga armies, to obstruct evil beings,
strife, and various pestilences; you should cause these to cease.
It increases the three vital essences and protects my Dharma-eye.
Those bhikṣus who abide in the Dharma, possessing few desires and no accumulations,
protect and uphold it, thereby increasing their lifespan, as well as their physical beauty, strength, and ease of appearance.
Thus the Teacher of Gods and Humans has now spoken all this to me;
with deep faith in the Buddha’s injunction, I now receive it upon my head,
protecting and upholding the seeds of the Triple Gem and causing the Eye of the True Dharma to blaze brightly.
We shall protect and uphold all those śrāvakas who abide in the Dharma;
together with the hosts of nāga armies, we shall eliminate all unwholesome dharmas,
obstruct evil beings, and cause them all to cease.
Abounding in flowers, fruits, and medicinal herbs, and endowed with all flavors and rich moisture,
may it cause all Kṣatriya kings to reverently believe in the Buddha’s True Dharma;
as well as the Vaiśyas and Śūdras, and the multitudes of nāgas, devas, and yakṣas.
I cause them to attain faith, To deeply revere what the Buddha has taught.
They dwell in protection within secluded forests, With few desires and no accumulation.
They correctly practice regarding the lunar mansions and planets, The constellations, the years, and the four seasons.
"May the three evil realms be exhausted, and may the paths of the virtuous be filled to overflowing.

Chapter 14: The Chapter on the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa The Great Collection Sūtra, Section on the Moon Treasury, Part Twelve, Chapter Fourteen: The Chapter on the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa At that time, the Buddha addressed the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa of Kauśāmbī, saying:
"O Wondrous Being!"
"Of these four continents, you should protect and uphold the fourth division in the northern region of Jambudvīpa. Why is this?
Because this Jambudvīpa is the place where all Buddhas arise; therefore, you should protect and uphold it most preeminently."

The Buddhas of the past have already instructed you to protect and nurture [this teaching]; the Buddhas of the future shall do likewise, as will your sons, ministers, retinues, yakṣas, and piśācas, all of whom shall provide protection.

"You have ninety-one sons who delight in various activities; some travel throughout the ten directions riding elephants, others riding horses, others riding camels, others riding bulls, others riding rams, others riding white sheep, others riding dragons, others riding birds, others riding men, others riding women, and others riding boys or girls as they travel through the ten directions. You, too, should cause them to give rise to reverent faith and together protect the fourth northern quarter of Jambudvīpa."

"Furthermore, there are yakṣa ministers and generals of great power, whose names are: first, Aroga; second, Śrī; third, Kṣema; fourth, Siddhārtha; fifth, Aparājita; sixth, Pūrṇamanoratha; seventh, Subhikṣa; eighth, Nandana; ninth, Vāri-kṣaya-dhvaja; tenth, Narmuṣadha; eleventh, Vidyunmālī; twelfth, Jvālāmukha; thirteenth, Vārinetra; fourteenth, Ugra; fifteenth, Sukarṇa; sixteenth, Parigraha. These yakṣas are your ministers and generals of great power; you should cause them to conceive respectful faith and together protect the fourth quarter of Jambudvīpa in the north."
"Furthermore, there are four mahā-cāturantā kings:
the first is named Dīrghākṣa;
the second is named Dīrghamukha."
The third is named Kumbhāsana;
the fourth is named Puṣpadanda.
These Cāṭas are all your powerful military generals; you should also cause them to develop respectful faith and together protect the fourth quarter of Jambudvīpa in the north.
Furthermore, there are yakṣa generals of great power who constantly lead their troops:
the first is named Indra, the second Soma, the third Varuṇa, the fourth Vāsava,
the fifth Brahmapati, the sixth Īśāna, the seventh Jayakāma, and the eighth Candra.
Dāna, next named Nirgrantha, next named Nirgranthaka, next named Bhañji, next named Maṇicāra, next named Panira, next named Upacāka,
next named Sthāgiri, next named Himavanta, next named Sattha, and so forth.
The first is named Paramatana; the second is named Khandaka; the third is named Kamatavi;
the fourth is named Pūrṇa; the fifth is named Khadali; the sixth is named Gopāli; the seventh is named Jihmaji;
the eighth is named Aṭṭhaka; the ninth is named Aṭṭhabhagu; the tenth is named Nanda.
Rādhi; next, named Nārāyaṇa; next, named Dhyānariṣava; next, named Citrakā; next, named Citrasena; next, named Śyāmali; next, named Nairgrantha;
next, named Dīrghamukha; next, named Maṇḍaka; next, named Māṇava.
Next is named Śikhin; next is named Vairocana; next is named Nāgavinīta;
next is named Vemacitra; next is named Dvārapāla; next is named Tamana; next is named Mohana;
next is named Manohara; next is named Putramba; next is named Kaṭaṃkaṭa; next...
Named Pātra-ghaṭa, next named Candraprabha, next named Avatasa, next named Samudra,
and next named Go-rakṣa— these fifty yakṣa generals are all members of your powerful host who receive your commands;
you should also cause them to give rise to reverent faith.
Together they protect the fourth division of the northern region of Jambudvīpa.

"Furthermore, there are sixteen celestial kings of the gods: the first is named Eḍa, the second Vīḍa, the third Naḍa, the fourth Devapadmaka, the fifth Padmavati, the sixth Kṛtāñjali, the seventh Mahāsena, the eighth Akhida, the ninth Khidasaya, the tenth Virūḍhaka, the eleventh Utpala, the twelfth Candra, the thirteenth Candraka, the fourteenth Varuṇa, and the fifteenth Sarpadi. These sixteen celestial kings of the gods also possess great power and vast armies; you should likewise cause them to give rise to reverent faith, so that they may together protect the fourth quarter of Jambudvīpa in the north."
“In the north there is a stūpa named Śikhara, where the Buddhas of the past, as well as sages and noble saints, dwelt and perceived the Four Noble Truths.
In the north there is a mountain called Śiṅku, the abode of the Sun and Moon Devas, and the dwelling place of powerful spirits and deities of renown.”
"By means of their great power of diligence, you shall together protect the fourth division of the northern region of Jambudvīpa.

Furthermore, there are three luminaries, seven lunar mansions, and three celestial maidens in the north; you should also cause them to act rightly in the world, so that they may together protect the fourth division of the northern region of Jambudvīpa."

All the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, pretas, piśācas, pūtanas, and kaṭapūtanas who dwell in the northern direction and have no other affiliation—afterward, I shall distribute and establish them according to their respective lands, and I shall likewise cause you to protect and nurture them.
At that time, the World-Protecting Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, son of Kubera, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One! It is so, it is so."
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!

In the past, the Buddhas of the past already instructed me to provide protection, establish, and nurture this northern fourth part of Jambudvīpa. I now likewise deeply receive the Buddha’s teaching to protect the Dharma of all Buddhas in the northern region of Jambudvīpa."

At that time, the son of King Kubera Vaiśravaṇa, the minister Kṣatara, and all the yakṣa generals, the sixteen celestial deities, their entire retinues—men and women, boys and girls—all rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Buddha, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“O Great Virtuous Bhagavān!

I and my retinue have now, before the Buddha, given rise to deep faith, reverence, and veneration such as we have never experienced before; likewise, we have given rise to deep faith, reverence, and veneration toward the Jewel of the Dharma and the Jewel of the Sangha, such as we have never experienced before.
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!

From this day forward, with sincere and earnest hearts, for the sake of subduing all sentient beings who harbor evil intentions, we shall diligently protect and uphold this northern fourth part of Jambudvīpa. Together with the chief Vaiśravaṇa King, we shall now likewise protect and uphold the Buddhadharma in this northern region of Jambudvīpa."
At that time, the Vaiśravaṇa King Kuvīra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

If the disciples of the Buddha—whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—who accord their three karmas with the Buddha’s True Dharma, who listen to the Dharma with single-minded devotion and practice according to the teachings, and who study and uphold the precepts; or if other sentient beings who have gained reverent faith in the Triple Gem, who make offerings to the Buddha, bestow gifts upon the Saṃgha, and diligently cultivate meritorious deeds—I, together with my retinue, shall all with one mind receive the Buddha’s entrustment to provide for them, protect them, and nurture them."

If a disciple of the Buddha dwells in accordance with the dharma of the araṇya, practices diligently in conformity with the dharma, and lives alone without a companion in the secluded forest like the horn of a rhinoceros, I shall protect, support, and nurture them all the more.

If there are sentient beings who, in those secluded forests, diligently practice and make offerings to the World-Honored One’s śrāvaka practitioners without lack of anything, I shall, through skillful means, protect, sustain, and nourish them, benefiting them in five ways.
What are the five? First, the increase of lifespan;
second, the increase of wealth; [and so forth].
Third, the increase of freedom from illness;
fourth, the increase of happiness;
fifth, the increase of renown.
Because I have thus protected, sustained, and brought them to fulfillment, the Three Jewels flourish and the lineage of the Buddhas endures for a long time.

“If there are sentient beings who, within their own domains, greedily seek and amass wealth without ever finding satisfaction; who do not contemplate the terrifying consequences of future lives; who are malicious, impetuous, and devoid of compassion; who provoke and harass Kṣatriyas with various weapons and engage in mutual combat; who butcher, disembowel, hack, pierce, hunt, and slaughter; who imprison, penalize, and exile; and who commit acts such as killing, stealing, and even holding wrong views—thereby creating evil conditions for Kṣatriyas, as well as for Brāhmaṇas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, men and women, boys and girls, and even down to animals, provoking mutual harassment and creating evil conditions that cause those beings to kill and harm one another and plunder in various ways, through the convergence of immeasurable causes and conditions of unwholesome conduct.”

I shall shield all evil sentient beings, causing them to abide in minds of loving-kindness, compassion, faith, morality, renunciation, learning, and wisdom; I shall cause them to leave unwholesome states and establish them in wholesome ones. I shall ward off all strife, pestilence, famine, untimely winds and rains, as well as harsh frost and hail. Furthermore, I shall shield against all wicked elephants, lions, tigers, wolves, vicious oxen, vicious horses, bears, brown bears, hawks, falcons, mosquitoes, gadflies, flies, and fleas. Moreover, I shall cause all flowers, leaves, fruits, medicinal herbs, and the five grains to flourish, and all fragrances, fine flavors, beautiful colors, and lustrous textures to be delightful and always abundant.
The vital essence of the earth, the vital essence of sentient beings, and the vital essence of the *sarpis* (clarified butter) of the Dharma—thus do these essences increase.

Whatever in the world is parched, coarse, rough, foul-colored, tasteless, malodorous, putrid, unpleasant, or useless—I cause all such things to vanish. In this way, the vital essence of the earth, the vital essence of sentient beings, and the vital essence of the *sarpis* of the Dharma increase and endure for a long time;

because the vital essence of the earth, the vital essence of sentient beings, and the vital essence of the *sarpis* of the Dharma increase and endure for a long time, the Buddha-dharma likewise increases and endures for a long time.

Because the Buddha-dharma increases and abides for a long time through this, the long night of birth-and-death and afflictions for all sentient beings comes to rest, and they are able to enter the city of great, fearless nirvana.

For this reason, together with my military generals, ministers, and retinue, I shall protect and uphold the fourth quarter of the northern region of Jambudvīpa, causing the Eye of the Buddha’s Dharma to abide long and blaze brightly. Furthermore, I shall ensure that the disciples of the World-Honored One remain without accumulation, dwelling in secluded forests like the rhinoceros horn—solitary and without companion—their three karmas in accord as if extinguishing a fire on their heads, never engaging in mutual derision, deception, or strife.

Toward all sentient beings, one gives rise to a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of compassion, a mind of pity, a mind of faith, a mind of ethical discipline, a mind of equanimity, a mind of diligence, a mind of mindfulness, a mind of concentration, and a mind of wisdom.

“O Great Virtuous Blessed One! In this way, we shall cause the Eye of the Buddha’s Dharma to abide long in the world; we shall cause the lineage of the Triple Gem to blaze forth and endure for a long time; we shall cause all things in the world that are unpleasant, painful, or distressing to be brought to rest; we shall restrain evil beings and establish wholesome dharmas; and we shall quiet the three evil destinies while increasing the three auspicious paths.”

Furthermore, if a disciple of the Blessed One abandons right mindfulness, abandons reflection, abandons right contemplation, and abandons recitation as well as teaching it to others; if they abandon the practices of the True Dharma and instead engage in managing household affairs and various means of livelihood, such as commerce, planting gardens and fruit trees, and maintaining slaves, elephants, horses, camels, donkeys, cattle, sheep, chickens, dogs, pigs, deer, hawks, falcons, and peacocks; if they diligently attend to all royal affairs, matters concerning cities, villages, and households; if they associate with the laity, acting as messengers and servants to deliver messages; and if they hoard wealth, food, drink, clothing, rice, millet, and silks.

Regarding the wealth and property of others, they likewise guard, hoard, and accumulate it; or else, through incantations or by means of painting and calligraphy, they teach others how to earn a living.
If such are they, we are unable to protect, maintain, or nurture them.
"I shall never, for the sake of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, deliberately utter false speech or commit a defiled offense.
The Buddha said: "Excellent, excellent!"
O Sublime Being!

If one diligently protects, upholds, nurtures, and causes the Dharma-eye cultivated by me over immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas—the well-expounded True Dharma, the Vinaya, and the Right Precepts—to endure for a long time, then that person is making offerings to all Buddhas of the three periods of time.

If you act in this way, you will obtain an increase in lifespan, an increase in wealth, an increase in strength, an increase in happiness, an increase in followers, an increase in retinue, an increase in palaces, an increase in faith, an increase in precepts, an increase in learning, an increase in diligence, an increase in relinquishment, an increase in mindfulness, and an increase in wisdom. By the power of these causes and conditions of increase, you will be able to swiftly fulfill the six pāramitās and attain equal and perfect enlightenment, just as I have now attained the state of the unsurpassed, self-arisen Dharma King.
I now further entrust the True Dharma of the Buddha to the great kings of Jambudvīpa, so that after my parinirvāṇa they may protect, uphold, and nurture it.

If there should be bhikṣus who, devoid of shame and remorse, defile my Dharma by privately establishing fields and estates, keeping slaves and even livestock, and engaging in various kinds of household livelihoods;

In this way, monks, the great kings throughout the realm of Jambudvīpa should restrain, rebuke, and banish those who have committed transgressions, causing them to leave behind their faults; they should protect, sustain, and nurture those who practice the True Dharma.
At that time, the entire great assembly who had gathered—the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, humans, and non-humans—all together praised him, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"O Sublime Being!
You must diligently protect and uphold [this] for the sake of ensuring that the Buddha-dharma remains long in the world.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke these verses:
The Buddha addressed Vaiśravaṇa and his thousand hosts of yakṣas:
"You all should together protect those bhikṣus who abide in the Dharma in the northern quarter,
as well as the śrāvakas possessed of a sense of shame."
Accept this entrustment from me and diligently protect and nurture it.
The Honored Teacher of the past commanded you to establish it;
uphold the Buddha’s True Dharma and ward off evil beings.
Increasing the three vital essences, Ceasing all strife and disputes,
And corresponding with the śrāvakas— One should also diligently protect them.
King Vaiśravaṇa said:
Accepting my offerings with the highest reverence, you diligently provide protection and nurture;
you cause the Eye of the True Dharma to blaze brightly, increase the three vital essences, and shield against evil beings; you strive to sever all strife and litigation.
Those śrāvakas who do not accumulate wealth, who have few desires and are content,
and who are able to abandon all evil deeds— I too shall diligently protect and uphold them.
If there are those who can make offerings to these practicing śrāvakas, [may they likewise be protected].
I shall increase five things to bring benefit to them:
oiliness, moisture, fragrance, delicious flavor, and an abundance of flowers, fruits, and various medicinal herbs;
so that they may enjoy these, I shall cause them all to be plentiful.
Because those three kinds of subtle flavors will increase,
we shall diligently protect and uphold them so that the Buddha-dharma may long remain ablaze.
I shall further cause the shameless kings to shave their heads.
Those kings should be restrained by him; the great assembly shall all offer praise.
Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra, Volume 52; Mahāvaipulya Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra, Volume 53.

At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Four Great Heavenly Kings,
speaking in verse: "The mountains that possess renown, Created by the Sovereign,
Extending as far as the two Kiṃśuka trees, The Gandhamādana and the Khadiraka."
Vāta, Agni, and Himavat, the abodes of the sun and moon—
these always protect and uphold the World-Honored One’s true and wondrous Dharma.
Pañcāla, Pañcālaka, Kṛṇi, and Gāndhāra.

the Earth Deity and the Great Earth Deity,
Kṛṣṇa and Mahākṛṣṇa, Rāhu and Vemacitrin, and Sūci and Pārata.

On Forbearance, Part One The Great Collection Sūtra, Section on the Moon Treasury, Chapter Twelve: Chapter Sixteen on Forbearance, Part One. At that time, there was an asura king named Agnijihva (Fire-Taste).
In that assembly, he rose from his seat, raised his hand to point toward Rāhu, the Asura King, and addressed four hundred billion Asura kings, saying:

"This Rāhu, the Asura King, is our revered teacher and elder. He is able to benefit all sentient beings through merit and wisdom; he is sovereign, courageous, and the most supreme among all the Asuras."

"King Rāhula and we ourselves have all been deceived and slighted by Gautama; because he wished to cause the Buddha-dharma to blaze forth, he entrusted it to other assemblies but did not grant it to us, thereby causing us to suffer great humiliation."
Next, there was another asura king named Tiṣya Vemacitra, who spoke these words:
"In the past, each of us within our own four continents was equal to Śakra Devānām Indra; now we are like jackals chasing after a lion."
"We would rather abandon this lowly place and return to our own country, its cities, towns, and palaces.
Furthermore, we would sooner die than endure such humiliation."
"This is a great enemy that causes us to experience immense sorrow and suffering.
Then Rāhu, the Asura King, spoke these words:
"It would be better for sentient beings to receive insults and humiliation from the most excellent of men than to receive praise from those who are base and lowly."
Why is this? Because it would cause many good people to hold him in contempt.

This Teacher of Gods and Humans is the most supreme and sovereign within the three realms; having reached the other shore, he perfectly knows the appropriate timing and acts according to what is required. Therefore, it is so.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Candragarbha joined his palms toward the Buddha, paid homage with single-minded devotion, and spoke these words:

“O Guide, you should observe this Rāhu, King of the Asuras, who possesses such steadfast wisdom and supreme wisdom; who dwells securely in firm faith, delights in goodness, and rejoices in forbearance; whose observance of the precepts is pure and who has deep faith in the Triple Gem—he will before long swiftly become an unsurpassed guide.”
"I only pray that the World-Honored One, for the sake of causing the Dharma to blaze forth, will grant this portion to Rāhula.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the four hundred billion asura kings, speaking in verse:
"You have previously possessed all virtues, And each has already dwelled in pure faith."
Thus have the Buddhas of the past entrusted the Dharma to you;
now I likewise entrust this Dharma entirely to you.
You should, by means of various skillful expedients, protect and uphold the eye of my Dharma.
By performing such merit as this, you shall fill the great ocean of wisdom;
each within your own sphere, protect my True Dharma.
Abiding in the Dharma with constant joy and patience, guard those who maintain the roots of concentration.
If you all act in this way, you shall all make offerings to the Buddhas of the three times;
you will constantly go to the happy realms, and with your lives, wisdom, and fruits fully perfected,
you shall escape all evil paths while wandering through the world.
"Those who seek supreme rewards should kindle the eye of my Dharma;
each within their own realm, they shall obstruct and restrain evil beings.
At that time, all the asuras rose, joined their palms, and spoke these words:
“We Asuras, each within our own realm, shall cease all evil and cause the Dharma of the World-Honored One to blaze forth.
Those who practice the gift of Dharma shall guard against what is unwholesome.”
"Increasing the three vital essences, one leaves evil and dwells in the good path.
At that time, the entire great assembly gathered there—gods, humans, gandharvas, and others—all together praised the asuras, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
At that time, the World-Honored One likewise praised those four billion asura kings and their retinues, saying these words:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"O noble sons! That you are able to act in this way is called making offerings to all Buddhas of the three periods of time; you should diligently protect, uphold, and nurture my Dharma.

Thus, the Buddha’s Dharma-eye shall blaze forth, and the lineage of the Triple Gem shall remain unbroken for a long time. For this reason, I now entrust you and your retinues to all the Buddhas of the ten directions who currently dwell in the world and have not yet entered parinirvāṇa, as well as to all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the Bhadrakalpa. May you always encounter those Asuras throughout your successive lives."

"When you attain perfect enlightenment and appear in the world during this Bhadrakalpa, he shall serve as your supreme donor; he will be foremost in upholding the true Dharma and maintaining the precepts, and he will attain dhyāna-samādhi and be fully endowed with the power of patience."
Thus, at the end of this Bhadrakalpa, a Tathāgata named Rocana, the Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, will appear in the world.

At that time, Rocana shall bestow upon them the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; they shall then swiftly fulfill the six pāramitās and, before long, become unsurpassed Dharma Kings, entering the great city of fearless Nirvāṇa.

Likewise, if there are sentient beings—whether in the present age or in future ages—who, within my Dharma, renounce the household life to practice the Way with their three karmas in accord; or who further permit others to renounce the household life to practice the Way; or who are able to diligently protect, sustain, and provide for my śrāvakas—monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—so that the lineage of the Triple Gem may not be severed; or who are able to cultivate the dāna-pāramitā up to the prajñā-pāramitā; or who construct stūpas, temples, and images, as well as repair those already existing; or who provide various kinds of gifts, offerings, and support to the Saṃgha of the four quarters, establishing monasteries and repairing them.

Furthermore, in those monasteries of the Saṃgha of the four quarters, they relinquish and bestow various kinds of clothing, bedding, utensils, and other necessities; as well as fields, houses, wealth, treasures, groves, gardens, male and female servants, attendants, and even domestic animals.

Furthermore, if one sees others who have abandoned and given away various goods being pursued and seized back, one should protect them by force; or again, if they give to me or my śrāvaka disciples all that is required—robes, food and drink, bedding, medicinal requisites for the sick, and so forth.

Among my śrāvaka disciples, there may be those who encounter suffering and distress due to various causes and conditions; whether by their own power or through the skillful means of others' power, I shall liberate them. I entrust all such sentient beings to all the Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions, as well as to all the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the Bhadrakalpa, so that they may be received and cared for, and born so as to meet with one another.

"If those Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa appear in the world, these sentient beings shall act as great donors to those Buddhas, be foremost in guarding the True Dharma and upholding the precepts, and attain meditative concentration and the perfection of the power of patience."

When such a Tathāgata appears in the world at the end of this Bhadrakalpa, that Buddha shall bestow upon them the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; they shall then swiftly fulfill the six pāramitās and, before long, become unsurpassed Dharma Kings, entering the great city of fearless Nirvāṇa.
At that time, there were again immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of sentient beings, their eyes filled with tears of sorrow, who gazed up at the Tathāgata and spoke thus:

“We now observe the liberation of the Greatly Compassionate World-Honored One, which has emerged from the prison of birth and death within all paths of the triple world; which has abandoned craving and thirst, departed from the eight worldly dharmas, and relinquished the afflictions of pride regarding ‘self’ and ‘mine’; which is free from all twelve links of existence (*dvādaśāṅga-pratītyasamutpāda*); and which knows all phenomena to be like empty space, abiding without inversion and constantly giving rise to great compassion for all sentient beings.”

Nevertheless, for the sake of sentient beings, all Tathāgatas provide protective sustenance so that this Dharma-eye and the lineage of the Triple Gem may long endure without extinction in this Sahā world.

The Tathāgata now further entrusts the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, garuḍas, mahoragas, kumbhāṇḍas, pretas, piśācas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, humans, non-humans, and others to all the Buddhas and bodhisattvas.

Those sentient beings, whether in the present or the future, should practice generosity, uphold the precepts, and cultivate meditative concentration and wisdom, diligently applying themselves to this Buddha-dharma. Entrusted to all Buddhas and Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, they do so in order to fulfill the six pāramitās and attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

If there are sentient beings who weary of suffering and seek happiness, there are none who, through skillful diligence in both the present and future lives, do not protect, uphold, and nurture the blazing Eye of Dharma, thereby succeeding to the lineage of the Triple Gem and attaining it.
The Buddha said: "So it is, so it is. It is just as you have said."

If there are those who, having grown weary of craving and suffering, seek happiness, they should protect and uphold the true Dharma of all Buddhas; from this, they shall obtain immeasurable rewards of merit.

If there are sentient beings who leave the household life for my sake, shaving their hair and beards and donning the saffron robes—even if they do not maintain the precepts—they have all already been marked with the seal of Nirvana.

Furthermore, if one who has left the household life does not uphold the precepts, there may be those who cause them distress, harassment, abuse, and revilement; who strike, bind, or cut them with their hands, knives, or staves; or who seize their robes and bowls, as well as various necessities for living. Such a person destroys the true *saṃbhogakāya* of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; they pluck out the eyes of all devas and humans. Because such a person seeks to cause the extinction of the seeds of the True Dharma and the Triple Gem belonging to all Buddhas, they cause devas and humans to fail to obtain benefit and fall into hell, thereby causing the three evil realms to increase and become full.
"Why is this? In the past, for the sake of all sentient beings, I cultivated the bodhisattva practices;
for the sake of this Dharma-eye, I gave rise to great compassion toward all sentient beings and gave my own blood, as vast as the great ocean, to those who begged for it."
His head was like Mount Vipula; his eyes and ears were likewise. He sacrificed a nose like a hundred thousand *turuṇa* mountains;
he sacrificed a tongue like ten *turuṇa* mountains; he sacrificed both hands and feet, each like Mount Vipula;
he sacrificed skin sufficient to cover one Jambudvīpa; and he also sacrificed immeasurable elephants and horses.
He gave chariots, oxen, slaves, servants, wives, and children, as well as his royal throne, to those who begged; furthermore,
he relinquished immeasurable kingdoms, cities, palaces, villages, houses, temples, gardens, groves,
clothing, bedding, mountains, marshes, and forests to those who begged.

“They upheld the prohibitive precepts in the presence of all Buddhas without any transgression; they made immeasurable offerings at the site of each Buddha; at the site of each Buddha, they received immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of Dharma-gates; and they upheld, recited, and protected these practices of the precepts, while skillfully cultivating samādhi, dhāraṇī, and patience.”

Furthermore, I have also made offerings to and honored immeasurable and boundless bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; I have made offerings to and honored immeasurable pratyekabuddhas; I have made offerings to the immeasurable śrāvaka assemblies of the Buddhas; I have made offerings to immeasurable śrāvakas who have attained the fruit; I have made offerings to immeasurable non-Buddhist sages; I have made offerings to immeasurable parents and teachers; I have made offerings to immeasurable beings afflicted by illness and suffering. Moreover, for immeasurable sentient beings oppressed by suffering who lacked protection, I have acted as their protector; for those without refuge, I have acted as their refuge; for those without a destination, I have acted as their destination, establishing them in peace and providing for them with offerings.

"I have, throughout immeasurable and vast eons, cultivated various ascetic practices and been fully endowed with the observance of precepts, dignified deportment, and the pure life (*brahmacarya*). O worthy ones!

Having thus, for those three great *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, out of compassion for all suffering sentient beings, I have given rise to a great, firm, and courageous mind and have long cultivated the practice for unsurpassed enlightenment."

Now, in this blind and dark world where there is no great teacher, at a time when the True Dharma is diminished, when extreme evil increases and pure dharmas are exhausted, among those sentient beings who commit the five deeds of immediate retribution, who slander the True Dharma, who revile the worthy and holy ones, who are associated with unwholesome roots, who are malicious, cruel, and harsh, devoid of shame and remorse, lacking compassion, and who do not contemplate the terrifying consequences of the future life—it is for the sake of such beings that I have resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

"Furthermore, may I rain down the great Dharma-rain upon all sentient beings abandoned in all pure Buddha-lands; may I cause those sentient beings to eliminate their vajra-like, firm afflictions, and may I lead them to non-retrogression from the enlightenment of the three vehicles according to their respective aspirations."

Furthermore, I vow to rescue and deliver sentient beings of the three evil realms, establishing them in the good paths and the bliss of nirvana; acting as the eye of the True Dharma for those beings, I shall provide protection so that it may long abide in the world, blazing brightly through the long night.

If those sentient beings go forth within my Dharma, shave their heads, and don the saffron robes, yet do not maintain the prohibitive precepts—if there are those who make offerings to such persons, these sentient beings will likewise obtain a great fruit; how much more so for those who have gone forth for my sake, maintain the precepts, and dwell in accordance with the Dharma? To make offerings to such as these results in an immeasurable, incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) mass of great merit!
How much more so, then, for those who can perform various kinds of offerings to my noble śrāvaka disciples—how could they not obtain an immeasurable, ineffable, and incalculable mass of great merit!
Therefore, among such sentient beings as these, I have now attained perfect enlightenment in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Out of great compassion, being the supreme among all the devas and humans in the world, I have established the assembly of all *śrāvakas* as the foremost field of merit—namely, those who have attained the stages of the eight great men (*mahāpuruṣa*).

For this reason, all sentient beings, in both the present and future worlds, should have deep faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. Those sentient beings shall receive supreme and wondrous karmic rewards among humans and devas, and before long they shall enter the City of Fearlessness. Likewise, even those who make offerings to a single person who has gone forth for my sake, or who has shaved their hair and beard and donned a fragment of the *kāṣāya* robe without having received the precepts—by making offerings to such a person, one also attains [the merit] up to and including entry into the City of Fearlessness.

For this reason, I have spoken thus: if there should be someone who has left the household life for my sake but does not uphold the prohibitions and precepts—shaving off their hair and beard and wearing a fragment of the kāṣāya—and if anyone were to afflict or harm such a person through unrighteous means, they would even destroy the dharma-body and reward-body of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and would even fill the three evil realms.

Therefore, I have told you this before: if there are those who love themselves and seek happiness while avoiding suffering, they should diligently protect, nurture, and kindle the Eye of the Dharma, ensuring that the Triple Gem is sustained and its lineage remains unbroken.
"By these causes and conditions, you shall from now on obtain immeasurable rewards of merit.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Candragarbha, together with eight thousand *koṭi-nayuta* hundreds of thousands of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Buddha, and with single-minded reverence, paid homage and spoke these words: "So it is, so it is."
"O Great Virtuous Bhagavān!

In my dwelling place, the world-system called Candravijaya, the Great Teacher Tathāgata Sūryacandraprabha frequently extols Śākyamuni Buddha of the Sahā world, saying: 'In the past, when he was a bodhisattva, he possessed great heroic power and cultivated all practices with extreme austerity and diligence. Thus, by virtue of his great compassion and the power of his great vows, this bodhisattva has now attained perfect awakening in the state of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* amidst those sentient beings in that five-fold defiled evil world who commit the immediate transgressions, slander the true Dharma, revile the noble ones, and are associated with unwholesome deeds.'"

"This Buddha preaches the Dharma for those sentient beings who harbor views of annihilationism or eternalism, who are malicious, coarse, and abrasive, who lack compassion, who have taken refuge in false paths, who seek out various teachers, and who fail to contemplate the terrifying consequences of future lives."

Nevertheless, there are sentient beings who diligently employ various means wishing to harm the Tathāgata Śākyamuni; they may offer him food mixed with poison, or seek to harm him through the means of swords, staves, wild elephants, lions, vicious oxen, or vicious dogs; some utter slanderous words, claiming he lacks the holy life (*brahmacarya*), or that he is not a man, or that he is a thief, or that he takes life—thus engaging in all manner of such slanders.
Furthermore, some defile him with dust and dirt; some, amidst the great assembly, revile him with coarse and fierce abuse and disparage him in various ways.

Some fill the Buddha’s dwelling with all manner of foul, impure things; some, upon seeing him, weep and feel displeasure; some, upon seeing him, close their eyes and cover their faces; some, upon seeing him, turn their backs and flee far away; and some, unwilling to see him, shut their doors and block their windows.

Yet that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, amidst all these evil sentient beings, is able to endure such immeasurable sufferings and miseries; furthermore, he neither feels anger nor resentment toward those evil beings. Moreover, without ceasing day or night, he constantly gives rise to great compassion for all those beings, following them everywhere at all times and in all places to transform them.

Just as a young cow that has recently given birth to a calf, before it has grown large, might suddenly lose it and its mother would then run about in search of it, so too is it with the Tathāgata Śākyamuni:

his mind is impartial toward all sentient beings, and out of great compassion, he pursues them, rescuing them from the three evil realms and establishing them in the good paths and the bliss of nirvāṇa.
"Thus, being fully endowed with such great compassion, this Śākyamuni Tathāgata now performs the Buddha-work in the Sahā world.

At that time, having heard these words, the entire great assembly was struck by such a rare and unprecedented occurrence; their hearts were filled with joy and they leaped for gladness. Before that Buddha, they spoke thus:
"O Great Virtuous Bhagavān!

We, too, shall likewise do so; with diligence and great heroic power, we shall practice the conduct of enlightenment for immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, practicing from the *dānapāramitā* up to the *prajñāpāramitā*. For the sake of maturing all sentient beings through such skillful means, we shall cultivate these practices just as the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, when he was a bodhisattva, long practiced the conduct of enlightenment, vowing to attain perfect awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) amidst the evil sentient beings of an impure world of five turbidities, and even to establish all sentient beings upon the various wholesome paths and in the bliss of nirvāṇa.

I, too, am likewise; I vow to attain perfect awakening in unsurpassed, complete, and perfect enlightenment within a five-turbid, impure buddha-field, and thus to bring to maturity those beings who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution, even those associated with all roots of unwholesomeness, establishing them in the good paths and the bliss of nirvāṇa.
"Those sentient beings immediately received the prediction of their future enlightenment from the Buddha Candrasūryaprabha, just as they had previously prayed.

At that time, there were further immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, who had come to this assembly from the ten directions in order to behold Śākyamuni Buddha, to make offerings to him, and to see the Great Assembly.
All those bodhisattvas spoke with one voice, saying: "Venerable Blessed One!
We, each in our own buddha-field, have likewise heard from our respective Tathāgatas such praise of the World-Honored One, just as it was spoken by the Bodhisattva Candragarbha."

In each of those [realms], there were likewise ten billion bodhisattvas who all made such great vows to perform buddha-work for the sake of maturing all sentient beings, just as the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Candragarbha has described.
At that time, all those who had come—the devas, nāgas, and even all the kaṭapūtanas, humans, non-humans, and so forth—joined their palms and spoke these words:
“We repent before the Greatly Compassionate Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.”

Whatever transgressions we have committed against the Buddha through body, speech, or mind, or whatever transgressions we have committed against the Dharma, the Saṅgha, or even a single disciple of the World-Honored One—we now sincerely repent before the Buddha. We vow never to commit them again and shall steadfastly uphold the prohibitive precepts.
We were ignorant, like small children, and unskilled in our conduct; we only pray that the World-Honored One, out of great compassion and deep pity, will accept our repentance.

Having received the entrustment to protect, uphold, and nurture the World-Honored One’s Eye of the Dharma, we shall employ various skillful means to cause it to blaze brightly, to protect and maintain the Three Jewels so they may endure long without extinction, and to increase the three kinds of vital energy while obstructing all evils.

Toward all the Buddha’s śrāvaka disciples, and even toward those who do not maintain the prohibitive precepts but have shaved their hair and beards and wear a fragment of the kāṣāya, one should regard them as teachers and elders, protecting, supporting, and nurturing them, providing them with all that is required so that they lack for nothing.

"Furthermore, if there should be any Kṣatriya kings who commit various unrighteous acts to harass and disturb the World-Honored One’s śrāvaka disciples—whether by reviling them with insults, striking or hacking them with blades and staves, or seizing their robes, alms bowls, and various requisites;

or if they create obstacles to the gifts and offerings provided by others—we shall cause natural and sudden enemies to arise from other regions against them, and we shall likewise cause military uprisings within their own territories, as well as pestilence, famine, untimely winds and rains, strife, litigation, slander, and derision. Furthermore, we shall cause those kings to lose their own kingdoms before long."

In this way, if any brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, śūdras, men or women, boys or girls, or others such as devas, nāgas, up to and including kaṭapūtanas, should cause disturbance to any of the Buddha’s śrāvaka disciples—whether by seizing their vital energy, exhaling breath upon their bodies, or even looking at them with an evil mind—we shall all together cause those devas, nāgas, up to and including kaṭapūtanas, to have impaired faculties, to become ugly, and to lose their proper abodes.
"By the power of my vow, I shall cause it to be thus:
that they may no longer dwell or eat together with us, nor may they share in our laughter and play; such shall be their banishment."
It is the same even for those who cause disturbance, down to those who have shaved their heads, donned the saffron robes, yet do not uphold the precepts.

Furthermore, O World-Honored One, if there are disciples of the Buddha who possess no accumulated possessions, who have a heart of compassion, and whose three karmas are in accord with the Dharma—if such persons come at this time, we shall be able to protect them, so that the World-Honored One’s Eye of the Dharma may blaze brightly and never perish.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised them, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! You noble and wondrous men!"

If you act in this way, you will be free from all faults in every deed you perform. Because you accept my entrustment to protect, uphold, and nurture the Dharma so that it may flourish, you shall thereby be making offerings to the Buddhas of the three periods of time.

If you diligently protect, uphold, and nurture my Dharma, causing it to blaze forth and ensuring that the lineage of the Triple Gem remains unbroken; and if there are those who have already gone forth for my sake, as well as all those who will go forth in the future, you should likewise protect, uphold, and nurture them—this is the cause for your own *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, the Asura King Rāhula, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of asuras, rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Buddha, and with single-minded reverence, paid homage and spoke these words:
"O Great Virtuous Bhagavān!

We, too, shall diligently protect, nurture, and cause the Buddha-dharma to blaze forth; so that the lineage of the Three Jewels shall not be severed; to subdue others; to cease and obstruct all evils; to cause the three vital essences to increase; furthermore, to guard, uphold, embrace, and nurture all the World-Honored One’s śrāvaka disciples and the True Dharma; to benefit all sentient beings; to block transgressions, crush wicked people, and subdue all enemies; to eliminate all malevolent ghosts and spirits, and to pacify all strife; to bring all crops to fruition; to cause wicked people to become virtuous friends; and to gather in all those who are scattered and distracted.
Furthermore, so that all desires may be fulfilled according to one's wishes, I shall proclaim a great dhāraṇī named "Lightning Flash and Contraction.
Having spoken these words, he then recited the mantra: *tadyathā*...
ravahe ravahe ravahe
Maṃśurā-hi, apaṃśurā-hi, brahmarā-hi.

Munivacanākarṣiṇī rājñe śaraṇe śikṣaṇe.

Candālanutaprabhākṣīra svāhā. "O Bhagavān of Great Virtue!
This *Vidyutprabha-saṃkoca* Great Dhāraṇī is capable of benefiting all sentient beings, even to the extent of fulfilling all their desires.

If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or other faithful sons and daughters of good family who dwell in accordance with the dharma of meditation; or those who manage monastic affairs, or practice in the forest hermitage (*araṇya*), or stay beneath trees, or in the open air—such persons as these, if they can receive, uphold, read, recite, and contemplate this *Vidyutprabha-saṃkoca* Great Dhāraṇī;

Should there be asuras, asura wives, asura fathers, asura mothers, and their sons and daughters; or asura attendants, retinues, men and women, and the servants of asuras who wish to come and cause harm by seeking an opportunity, none of them shall be able to gain even the slightest advantage over him.
"This Asura shall no longer be able to return to his own city; his head shall be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
At that time, the entire great assembly who had gathered there all exclaimed in praise:
"Excellent! Excellent!"

At that time, the Asura King Vemacitrin, together with hundreds of thousands of other asuras, rose from his seat, joined his palms toward the Buddha, paid homage with single-minded devotion, and spoke these words:
"O Bhagavān of Great Virtue!

We also, for the sake of protecting, upholding, and nurturing the Eye of the True Dharma taught by the World-Honored One, and even for the sake of increasing the three kinds of vital energy; furthermore, for the sake of protecting, receiving, nurturing, and supporting all the World-Honored One’s śrāvaka disciples; and again, for the sake of subduing all enemies so that all wicked people may develop faith and reverence, bringing rest to all diseases, taming those who are stubborn and strong, and converting wicked people into virtuous friends with excellent retinues; and so that all seeds may sprout without decay and all fruits, crops, and vegetation may ripen—we shall recite the Great Dhāraṇī named "The Lion’s Gait."
Having spoken these words, he then uttered this mantra:

Tadyathā: susārīye, varakhe khade, varakhe varakhe, amuni, amukhamunije ya-vi-jaye, aparite, yajīne, vahasrākṣe, khare anakhare, vijayemi śirakhare, munakara-sakhre, amitā, uccha-khre, avame sasnabhe, saṃkarasme, prarāsa-mudra-kṣe-ja-lū, śamana, kṣa-bhokṣe-saṃgha-kṣme, upaśāntā-hari. Svāhā. "O Virtuous Blessed One! "
This Great Dharani of the Lion’s Gait can subdue all enemies and even bring all crops to maturity.

If there be bhikṣus, or even virtuous women of pure faith, who are in accord with dhyāna and who, in an open space, uphold, recite, and disseminate this Great Dharani of the Lion’s Gait, then should any asuras or their servants come seeking to harm them or watch for an opportunity, they shall never be able to gain even a fraction of an advantage. Furthermore, these [asuras] shall not be able to return to the asura city; their heads shall be split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.
At that time, the entire assembly that had gathered also exclaimed in praise: "Excellent! Excellent!

Then, the Asura King Mucilinda, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of asuras, rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Buddha, paid homage with single-minded devotion, and spoke these words:
“O Bhagavān of Great Virtue!

For the sake of protecting, upholding, and nurturing the Eye of the True Dharma taught by the World-Honored One, and even for the sake of increasing the three kinds of vital essence, and furthermore for the sake of protecting, receiving, nurturing, and supporting all the Śrāvaka disciples of the World-Honored One, we shall proclaim a great dhāraṇī named ‘Subduing All Nāgas.’”
Having spoken these words, he then recited the mantra:
"Tadyathā: viliśca..."

Hana niya svāhā. "O Bhagavān, this Great Dhāraṇī for Subduing All Nāgas is capable of completely pacifying all diseases;

it can also coil up, strike, and bind all malevolent spirits so that they cannot cause harm. It can stop untimely evil winds, torrential rains, and all noxious poisonous vapors. It can also subdue the many evil nāgas who kill with a glance, severing their attachments to desire. It can inflict burning affliction upon the bodies of the nāgas, as well as upon their dwellings; it afflicts their minds, afflicts their karma, and afflicts all their means of livelihood."
"O Great Virtuous Blessed One!
If there are bhikṣus, or even virtuous women of pure faith, who are in accord with dhyāna and who receive, uphold, recite, and disseminate this great dhāraṇī for subduing all nāgas in an open space;

and if there should be nāgas, nāga wives, nāga fathers, nāga mothers, nāga sons or daughters, nāga attendants, male or female servants, or nāga henchmen who wish to come and cause harm by seeking an opportunity—none of them shall be able to gain even a fraction of an advantage against them. Instead, they shall themselves incur the affliction of feverish torment, and their heads shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an āmalaka tree."

At that time, all the nāgas from the four continents who were present in the assembly became enraged; they terrified the asura city that had arrived, causing all the asuras to be struck with such alarm and fear that they could find no peace of mind.
At that time, the Naga King Sagara rose from his seat, joined his palms in homage toward the great nagas, and spoke these verses:
"If one beholds the Great Sage, That person shall eliminate anger;
Being free from anger is itself to be a sage— One should therefore cease all resentment and affliction."
Patience is the supreme in the world; through patience one attains worldly happiness.
Patience puts an end to all enmity; through patience one proceeds toward the city of peace.
The immeasurable asuras have been our constant enemies.
One should simply practice self-restraint; this is what the Buddha has always taught.
Through anger one goes to the evil realms; anger only increases further anger.
Because of anger one abandons friends; through anger one does not attain liberation.
We were in the realm of animals due to our evil precepts and anger;
had we been able to eliminate anger and pride, we would have been born among humans.
Now that we have obtained human bodies, we have taken refuge in the Buddha and gone forth as monastics.
"By practicing the conduct of liberation, you shall become a great guide.
At that time, after Sagara, the Dragon King, had spoken thus, all the dragons attained patience; their countenances were serene and joyful as they each sat in their original places.

At that time, the asura king Vajravairocana, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of asuras, rose from his seat, joined his palms toward the Buddha, paid homage with single-minded devotion, and spoke these words:
"O Bhagavat of Great Virtue!

We, too, for the sake of protecting, upholding, and nurturing the True Dharma of the World-Honored One so that the lineage of the Triple Gem shall not be severed; for the sake of diligently subduing all evil deeds of others and causing all wicked people to cease their ways so that the three vital essences may increase; and furthermore, for the sake of rescuing, protecting, gathering, and nurturing all the Śrāvaka disciples of the World-Honored One, we shall proclaim this Great Dhāraṇī named "The Cessation of All Illnesses."
Having spoken these words, he then uttered this mantra:

*tadyathā | moṅgama | maṅgama | abhiṅgama | śarabhaṅgama | sitabhaviṣyagaṅgama | vaśyabhiṣyagaṅgama | yoni-bhiṣyagaṅgama | aśani-bhiṣyagaṅgama | vāha-bhiṣyagaṅgama | caṭakara-viravapari-saṇḍira-vihaṅgama | sāgara-śarakuṭu-śarakuṭu-viśekuṭu-sarvaloka-indriya-kuṭu | simiriti | vipraṅgaśekuṭu | svāhā.* "O Bhagavat, O Great Virtuous One!"

This Great Dhāraṇī for Resting All Illnesses can eliminate all suffering from disease, pacify all poisons, harms, and calamitous hailstones, and can also subdue all malevolent nāgas, causing them to serve the World-Honored One and his śrāvaka disciples with whatever is required, just like servants.

At that time, all the assembled hosts of nāgas and great nāga kings became filled with rage and indignation. They immediately raised a great cloud in the sky above the asuras, intending to sound great drums and hurl down massive boulders. They rained down iron nooses, long spears, swords, and staves, as well as various forms such as those with sword-faces, iron mouths, sharp-toothed mouths, bamboo mouths, and jar mouths—all intended to harm the asuras—but they were unable to do so.
