"You all should together protect the kingdom of Bharuṇḍa.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Devadaha to the divine son Siṃhadanta with his retinue of five thousand, the gandharva Sadāmanda with his retinue of five hundred, the kinnara Munisvara with his retinue of one hundred, the yakṣas Maṇibhadra and Pūrṇabhadra each with their retinues of two thousand five hundred, the asura Ayomukha with his retinue of five hundred, the kumbhāṇḍa Āpāntara with his retinue of one hundred, and the goddesses Śaśini and Pañcikā each with their retinues of one thousand:
"All of you together shall protect the kingdom of Devadaha."
When the Buddha and the great assembly had all praised him, saying, "Excellent!

Excellent!", the World-Honored One then entrusted the kingdom of Campā to the Devaputra Gandhamegha and his retinue of one thousand celestial seers; to the Gandharva Guṇamālī and his retinue of two hundred; to the Kiṃnara Śaṅkhapāla and his retinue of one hundred; to the Yakṣa Dṛḍharoman and his retinue of five thousand; to the Asura Kanakā and her retinue of one hundred; and to the Kumbhāṇḍas Suprabha and Upaprabha, each with a retinue of fifty thousand; and to the goddess Daśamukhī and her retinue of five hundred.
“You all should together protect the kingdom of Campā.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Setavyā to the divine son Raktamegha with his retinue of one thousand; the gandharva Jambhala with his retinue of five hundred; the kinnara Maṇicūḍa with his retinue of one hundred; the yakṣa Durjaya with his retinue of one thousand; the asura Nidaghu with his retinue of five hundred; the kumbhāṇḍa Venuka with his retinue of one hundred; and to the goddesses Śāntā and Sunetrā, each with their respective retinues of one thousand five hundred:
"May you all together protect the kingdom of Setavyā."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the country of Aparāntaka to the Devaputra Parvatacakṣus and his retinue of two hundred; the Gandharva Dharmaprīti and his retinue of one hundred; the Kiṃnara Śūciloma and his retinue of one hundred; the Yakṣa Mahākāya and his retinue of one thousand; the Asura Kṛtāstra and his retinue of one hundred; the Kumbhāṇḍa Sthitodaka and his retinue of three hundred; and to the goddesses Suvarṇaprabhā and Kṛṣṇaprabhā, each with their respective retinues of two thousand five hundred.
“You all must together protect the lands and territories of the western region.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the country of Pūrvaśaila to the Thousand-fold retinue of the devaputra Āraṇemi, the Hundred-fold retinue of the gandharva Nandi, the Hundred-fold retinue of the kinnara Viśuddhasaṃgha, the Thousand-fold retinue of the yakṣa Maṇipuṣpa, the Two-thousand-five-hundred-fold retinues of each of the nāga kings Kāṭa and Aparola, the Hundred-fold retinue of the garuḍa Mahābhaya, the Five-hundred-fold retinue of the asura Kṛtasmṛti, the Five-hundred-fold retinue of the kumbhāṇḍa Daṇḍadhārin, and the Five-hundred-fold retinues of each of the celestial maidens Tālusī and Trimukhī:
"All of you together shall protect the country of Pūrvaśaila."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the land of Oḍra to the divine son Śikhi-ghoṣa and his retinue of five hundred; to the gandharva Puṣpa-prabha and his retinue of three hundred; to the kinnara Subhaya and his retinue of one hundred; to the yakṣa Kālapati and his retinue of five hundred; to the nāga Lambuka and his retinue of three hundred; to the asura Cāmpeya and his retinue of one hundred; to the kumbhāṇḍa Mandāraka and his retinue of one hundred; and to the goddesses Hārītī and Rañjita and their respective retinues of five hundred each.
“You all should together protect the kingdom of Oḍḍiyāna.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Kiṣkindhā to the Thousand Retinues of the Devaputra Kṛṣṇa, the Hundred Retinues of the Gandharva Suvarṇa, the Eighty Retinues of the Kiṃnara Vānamukta, the Five Hundred Retinues of the Yakṣa Muktakeśa, the Hundred Retinues of the Nāga King Baladeva, the Hundred Retinues of the Asura Nakṣatrarājī, the Eighty Retinues of the Kumbhāṇḍa Vimalasvara, and the Five Hundred Retinues each of the Goddesses Jayasūcī and Vṛścikā:
"You all shall together protect the kingdom of Kiṣkindhā."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: “Excellent! Excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Suvarṇabhūmi to the five hundred attendants of the devaputra Dhyānottaraśrava, the hundred attendants of the gandharva Māṇava, the hundred attendants of the kinnara Sucandra, the five hundred attendants of the yakṣa Dhyānottaraśrava, the hundred attendants of the asura Ratnacūḍa, and the eighty attendants of the kumbhāṇḍa Gandhamādana.
“May you all together protect the kingdom of Suvarṇabhūmi.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Mathurā to the Devaputra Gāndharva with his retinue of one hundred, the Gandharva Pañcaśikha with his retinue of five hundred, the Kinnara Tejodhipa with his retinue of eighty, the Yakṣa Dṛḍhaśūla with his retinue of five hundred, the Asura Bhīṣma with his retinue of five hundred, the Kumbhāṇḍa Sumati with his retinue of one hundred, and the Apsaras Jambhalā with her retinue of five hundred, saying:
"All of you together protect the kingdom of Mathurā."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Soḷīka to the Thousand-fold Retinue of the Devaputra Dhanākṣi, the Hundred-fold Retinue of the Gandharva Sudhira, the Five Hundred-fold Retinue of the Kiṃnara Śamakuśa, the Five Hundred-fold Retinue of the Yakṣa Sthira, the Thousand-fold Retinue of the Yakṣa Yavāna, the Hundred-fold Retinue of the Kiṃnara Abhaya, the Five Hundred-fold Retinue of the Yakṣa Varadhuvasaja, the Eight Hundred-fold Retinue of the Asura Caṃpāhari, the Three Hundred-fold Retinue of the Kumbhāṇḍa Gokakṣa, the Five Hundred-fold Retinue of the Rākṣasa Caṃpāhari, and the Five Hundred-fold Retinue of the Rākṣasa Śikhara.
“You all should together protect the kingdom of Vṛji.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Pañcāla to the divine son Vāsava with his thousand retinue, the gandharva Candrābha with his hundred retinue, the yakṣa Veṇu with his thousand retinue, the asura Mahāmegha with his five hundred retinue, the kumbhāṇḍa Hanuja with his hundred retinue, the goddess Maṇiccharī with her five hundred retinue, and the goddess Tamālapatrī with her thousand retinue, saying:
"All of you together shall protect the kingdom of Pañcāla."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Pārśva to the divine son Dhanuṣi with his retinue of five thousand; the Gandharva Kubera with his retinue of three thousand; the Kiṃnara Revata with his retinue of one thousand; the Yakṣa Vīra-sthita with his retinue of five hundred; the Yakṣa Namuci-rāja with his retinue of five hundred; the Gandharva Āmradeva with his retinue of one thousand; the Kiṃnara Īśāna with his retinue of one thousand; the Kumbhāṇḍa Keśakambala with his retinue of four thousand; the Rākṣasa Nala with his retinue of five thousand; and the Rākṣasa Hārītī with his retinue of two thousand.
“You all must together protect the land of Persia.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Cakravāḍa to the devaputra Khārumanta and his retinue of one thousand, the exquisite gandharva and his retinue of five hundred, the Tiriya kinnara and his retinue of five hundred, the Trapu yakṣa and his retinue of twenty thousand, the Bhīma yakṣa and his retinue of ten thousand, the Hūliśa nāga and his retinue of one thousand, the Suvarṇakarṇa asura and his retinue of one thousand, the Kalpavṛkṣa kumbhāṇḍa and his retinue of one thousand, and the Suvarṇakiṃsuka rākṣasa and his retinue of five thousand, saying:
"All of you together shall protect the kingdom of Cakravāḍa."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Pāyāsa to the Thousand-fold retinue of the Devaputra Samudrabhaya, the Hundred-fold retinue of the Gandharva Nata-bhu, the Hundred-fold retinue of the Kinnara Aśvamukha, the Two-thousand-fold retinue of the Yakṣa Puṣpadanta, the Thousand-fold retinue of the Yakṣa Mahādanta, the Five-hundred-fold retinue of the Nāga Utpalakarṇa, the Hundred-fold retinue of the Asura Hastika, the Hundred-fold retinue of the Kumbhāṇḍa Vimokṣaka, the Five-hundred-fold retinue of the Rākṣasī Citramālinī, the two groups of two-thousand-five-hundred-fold retinues consisting of the Rākṣasa Tamas and the Door-guarding Rākṣasa, and the Thousand-fold retinue of the Rākṣasa Candrābha.
"You all must together protect the kingdom of Pāyāsa.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Śrīyāmā to the Black-Haired Devaputra with his retinue of one hundred, the Golden-Armed Gandharva with his retinue of eighty, the Wind-Sound Kiṃnara with his retinue of one hundred, the Aruṇa Yakṣa with his retinue of one thousand, the Eight-Haired Yakṣa with his retinue of one thousand, the Upplavaṇa Nāga King with his retinue of one hundred, the Kṣiprakārin Asura with his retinue of one hundred, the Gandhamālini Kumbhāṇḍa with his retinue of five hundred, and the Kṛṣṇavarṇā Devī with her retinue of five hundred, saying:
"All of you together shall protect the kingdom of Śrīyāmā."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Vārāṇasī to the son of heaven Red-Copper-Colored with his eight hundred followers; the Gandharva Lovely-Eyed with his one hundred followers; the Kinnara Black-Needle with his one hundred followers; the Yakṣa Mūrdhan with his five thousand followers; the Nāga Eḷaka with his one hundred followers; the Asura Cow-Pacifier with his one hundred followers; the Kumbhāṇḍa Abhinanda-Sari with his five hundred followers; and the goddesses Dīrghaśāli and Viśeṣavatī, each with their five hundred followers.
"You all should together protect the kingdom of Vārāṇasī.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Kaśmīra to the following: the Devaputra Bhīmakāla with his retinue of fifty; the Gandharva Pañcasvara with his retinue of one thousand; the Water-dwelling Kinnara with his retinue of five hundred; the Yakṣa Viśālapāṇi with his retinue of thirty thousand; the Yakṣas Jīvaka and Meghavisarga each with their retinues of two thousand five hundred; the Nāga Hūluka with his retinue of ten thousand; the Asura Kuṅkuma with his retinue of one thousand; the Kumbhāṇḍa Dhāruvarṇī with his retinue of five hundred; the Goddess Samyagvādini with her retinue of one thousand;
and the Rākṣasīs Vanavāsikā with their retinue of ten thousand: "May you all together protect the kingdom of Kaśmīra."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the country of Uraśā to Nalamandaga, the gandharva, with his retinue of one hundred; to the five Bhīṣaṇa yakṣas, with their retinues of two thousand each; and to Śrīṣa yakṣa, with his retinue of one thousand.
"You all must together protect the kingdom of Uraśā.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the country of Karapava to the Gandharva Śilana and his retinue of one hundred, the Yakṣa Puṣparatna and his retinue of one thousand, the Nāga Sukharatnanetra and his retinue of one thousand, the Kumbhāṇḍa Bhayajanaka and his retinue of five hundred, and the goddess Anuraktā and her retinue of one hundred, saying:
"All of you together shall protect the country of Karapava."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Aśmaka to the yakṣa Mūṣika with his retinue of two thousand, the rākṣasa Supātra with his retinue of one thousand, the nāga Bala with his retinue of five hundred, the kumbhāṇḍa Megha-sthita with his retinue of one hundred, and the rākṣasī Hārītī with her retinue of one thousand.
"May you all together protect the kingdom of Aśmaka.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the country of Darada to the Gandharva Vīvadāri and his retinue of one hundred; to the Road Yakṣa, the Yellow-Headed Yakṣa, and the Valiant Yakṣa, each with their respective retinues of one thousand; to the Dragon King Bhadra and his retinue of two thousand; to the Dragon King Peacock-Plumage and his retinue of one hundred; and to the goddess Janavidyā and the goddess Mālāśrī, each with their respective retinues of two hundred and fifty:
"May you all together protect the country of Darada."
When the Buddha and the great assembly had all praised him, saying, “Excellent, excellent!

at that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Vṛji to the yakṣa Manasvin and the yakṣa Śīlabhadra, each with five hundred followers; to the nāga king Megharava with three hundred followers; to the kumbhāṇḍa Vimukta with eighty followers; and to the goddess Sāvitrī with one hundred followers.
“You all must together protect the kingdom of Vṛji.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Gāndhāra to the Gandharva Dharapushpa and the Mahoraga Gandharva, each with a retinue of one thousand; the Yakṣa Kinki and the Yakṣa Vibhīṣaṇa, each with a retinue of two hundred and fifty; the Nāga King Prabhapāṇi and the Nāga King Vijaya, each with a retinue of five hundred; and the goddess Āloki and the goddess Puṣpanetra, each with a retinue of two hundred and fifty, saying:
"All of you together shall protect the land of Gāndhāra."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Cakora to the Dragon King Kambala and his five hundred followers; the one hundred extremely wicked kumbhāṇḍas and their followers; the one hundred nāṭu-piśācas and their followers; the five hundred star-eyed rākṣasīs and their followers; the two hundred yakṣa generals wearing celestial armor and their followers; and the three hundred yakṣas who have ceased their evil ways and their followers.
“May you all together protect the kingdom of Cakora.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised them, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Sati to the Naga King Pūrṇa and the Naga King Sudharmā, each with their own retinue of one hundred; to the Kumbhāṇḍa Dṛḍhanetra with his retinue of one hundred; to the eight Vinayaka goddesses with their retinues of one hundred each; to the goddess Mārgadevī and the goddess Śrīdevī, each with their retinues of two hundred and fifty; and to the goddess Śaṅkhadevī and the goddess Sthitadevī, each with their retinues of fifty:
"May you all together protect the land of Sati."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Śālukya to the Devaputra Keśava with his retinue of one hundred; the Gandharva Rāṣṭrapāla with his retinue of one hundred; the Yakṣa Buddhagupta and the Yakṣa Aśanivaiśravaṇa, each with their respective retinues of five hundred; the Nāga King Mayūragrīva with his retinue of one hundred; the Nāga Daughter Parvatakṣī with her retinue of five hundred; the Kumbhāṇḍa Kṛtapañca with his retinue of five hundred; and the goddess Guṇadhārī and the goddess Nāgarakṣitā, each with their respective retinues of two hundred and fifty.
“You all must together protect the land of Śākala.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the land of Uttara to the Devaputra Duryodhana with his retinue of one thousand, the Yakṣa General Saṃjñeya with his retinue of ten thousand, the Great Yakṣa Meṇḍhaka-pāda with his retinue of eight thousand, the Yakṣa Suvarṇapuṣpamālā with his retinue of five hundred, the Nāga King Uṣṇīṣa with his retinue of one thousand, the Apsaras Anantamukhi with her retinue of ten thousand, and the Apsaras Tāṇḍyaśāri with her retinue of five thousand, saying:
"Empowered by the supernatural might of King Vaiśravaṇa, together with you, protect and sustain the land of Uttara."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the land of Kucha to Mūka the Devaputra and his thousand followers, the Great Yakṣa Yellow-Head and his thousand followers, the Rākṣasī Wealth-Disdainer and her thousand followers, the Great Yakṣa Guardian and his thousand followers, the Gourd-Eater (Kumbhāṇḍa) Sparse-Tooth and his thousand followers, and the Rākṣasīs Śrīcchanda and Deer-Tooth, each with five hundred followers.
"You all must together protect the land of Kucha.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Vārāṇasī to the yakṣa Khaṇḍa and his thousand followers, the kumbhāṇḍa Apakali and his hundred followers, and the rākṣasa Lambodara and his thousand followers, saying:
"All of you together shall protect the kingdom of Vārāṇasī."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Khejukā to King Jīvaka, the Gandharva, along with his five hundred followers, and to the Naga Khepila, along with his one hundred followers.
“You all should together protect the kingdom of Khejuka.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the country of Ayodhyā to the great yakṣa general Śūradundubhi with his thousand followers, the nāga king Hastikarṇa with his three thousand followers, and the rākṣasīs Kīcaki and Haimavatī, each with their two thousand five hundred followers, saying:
"All of you together shall protect the land of Ayodhyā."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!

At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Śāntanu to the divine son Āraṇemin with his retinue of one hundred, the yakṣa Aśvaka with his retinue of five thousand, and the rākṣasī Anāsava with her retinue of ten thousand.
“May you all together protect the land of Śāntanu.
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”
At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the kingdom of Kiṃnara to the great yakṣa Raktākṣa and his ten thousand followers, and to Acala Kumbhāṇḍa and his thousand followers, saying:
"All of you together shall protect the kingdom of Kiṃnara."
Thereupon, the Buddha and the great assembly all praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!
At that time, the World-Honored One entrusted the land of China to five thousand *Viśvakarman* devaputras.
The yakṣa general Kula with five thousand followers; the yakṣa general Kapila with five thousand followers;
the yakṣa general Dharmapāla with five thousand followers; the yakṣa general Dṛḍhanetra with five thousand followers;
the yakṣa general Mahānetra with five thousand followers; and the yakṣa general Śūrasena with five thousand followers.
The yakṣa general Maṇibhadra with his retinue of five thousand; the yakṣa general Bhadrapāla with his retinue of five thousand;
the yakṣa general Tejodhara with his retinue of five thousand; the yakṣa general Atavaka with his retinue of five thousand; and the yakṣa general Pañcika with his retinue of five thousand.
The Dragon King Vasuki with five thousand followers; the Dragon King Sumana-phala with five thousand followers;
the Dragon King Puṣpavimardaka with five thousand followers; the Yakṣī Hārītī, Mother of Ghosts, with five thousand followers;
the Great Goddess Elāpatyā with five thousand followers; and the Twin-Eyed One.
The Great Goddess, with her five thousand retinues, said: "O virtuous ones!
You must all together protect and sustain the land of China."

May all forms of affliction, strife, enmity, contention, litigation, the clashing of opposing armies, famine, pestilence, untimely winds and rains, frost, cold, and toxic heat therein be brought to rest. May the unwholesome and evil beings who are wrathful and coarse be warded off, and may all things that are bitter, pungent, astringent, tasteless, and so forth be made to cease. For the sake of causing my Dharma-eye to endure for a long time, for the sake of ensuring that the lineage of the Triple Gem continues without interruption, for the sake of increasing the three kinds of vital essence, and for the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all devas and humans, you must diligently provide protection and support.
"By these causes and conditions, you shall always obtain peace and happiness in this life and in future lives.

Thus spoke the devaputra Viśvakarman and his retinue; the great yakṣa Kapila, the yakṣa Dharmapāla, the yakṣa Dṛḍhanetra, the yakṣa Mahānetra, the yakṣa Śūra, the yakṣa Maṇibhadra, the yakṣa Bhadrapāla, the yakṣa Tejodhara, the yakṣa Atabakura, and the yakṣa Pañcika, along with their respective retinues; the nāga king Vāsuki, the nāga king Sumana-phala, the nāga king Puṣpavimardaka, and their respective retinues; and the goddess Hārītī, the goddess Elāpatyā, the goddess Viśālākṣī, and their respective retinues, each saying these words:
“O Great Virtuous Blessed One!
We shall together protect the land of China, pacify all strife and contention, and even cause the three types of vital energy (*ojas*) to increase.

We shall diligently provide protection, support, and nourishment; furthermore, we shall doubly establish, protect, support, and nourish those disciples of the World-Honored One’s *śrāvakas* who act in accordance with the three karmas and do not accumulate [defilements].
At that time, the World-Honored One praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! Well-spoken, son of good family!"
"You should protect and uphold my Dharma in this way.
The great assembly that had gathered also rejoiced and praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"

“O virtuous ones! I entrust all the lands of Jambudvīpa to the devas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, yakṣas, nāga kings, asuras, kumbhāṇḍas, and the celestial maidens, commanding each of them to establish, protect, and nurture all sentient beings.”
Therefore, you great dragon kings who do not receive a share should exercise forbearance and harbor no resentment.

These include the Dragon King Sāgara, the Dragon King Anavatapta, the Dragon King Elāpattra, the Dragon King Varuṇa, the Dragon King Supratiṣṭhita, the Dragon King Takṣaka, and the Dragon King Gaṅgā... [and so forth].
The Naga King Gaṅgā, the Naga King Sindhu, the Naga King Vakṣu,
the Naga King Sītā, the Naga King Tāpī, the Naga King Mahī-mucalinda, the Naga King Suvarṇapārśva,
the Naga King Vācīsuta, the Naga King Pūrṇabhadra, the Naga King Citrābhraka, and the Naga King Kuna.
The Naga King Bhadrika, the Naga King Asta, the Naga King Chāmila, the Naga King Gandhamādana,
the Naga King Nārāyaṇamukha, the Naga King Vāsumati, and the Naga King Nataxa—
these and one million eight hundred thousand other great naga kings dwell in Jambudvīpa.
Regarding those who gain merit, you should be patient and harbor no resentment.
Each of you should remain in your respective palaces to protect, uphold, and nurture my True Dharma, and you should perform deeds that bring benefit to all sentient beings.
By these causes and conditions, you shall benefit yourselves and others in both this life and future lives. Why is this?

Those devas, nāgas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, yakṣas, asuras, kumbhāṇḍas, devīs, rākṣasīs, and so forth, according to the lands where they formerly dwelt—those devas, nāgas, up to the devīs—will, for the sake of protecting each of those respective lands, establish and nurture all sentient beings.
"Therefore, you great yakṣa kings who do not receive a share should exercise forbearance and harbor no resentment.
These include the yakṣas Śara-roma, Śarabha, Kaṭaśūli, Pārāvatika, Pārāvata, and Vāmana."
The yakṣa Līkāṭa, the yakṣa Yautika, the yakṣa Kīlika, the yakṣa Pūrṇamukha,
the yakṣa Kāśyapiti, the yakṣa Rāṣṭrapāla, the yakṣa Loka, the yakṣa Śarakarṇa, the yakṣa Panāluci, the yakṣa Vṛkakarṇa, and the yakṣa Siṃhabhaya.
yakṣas, āluṇi yakṣas, śūrasaṃbhava yakṣas, ātmasārin yakṣas, takṣasirin yakṣas, bhasmāntaka yakṣas,
sumanahasta yakṣas, ramaṇīya yakṣas, akṣani-kira yakṣas, and citra.
The yakṣas, the Buddha-protected yakṣas, and the eight *bimbara* yakṣa generals such as these—
who dwell in various monasteries, gardens, springs, ponds, mountain crags, marshes, and beneath trees throughout Jambudvīpa, yet have not received their allotted shares—
should exercise forbearance and harbor no resentment; they should, according to [their respective places]...
Dwelling in their respective abodes, from mountain forests to beneath trees, each shall abide in their original place, protecting and nurturing my True Dharma,
and practicing for the benefit, peace, and happiness of all sentient beings.
By these causes and conditions, you shall benefit yourselves and others in this life and in future lives. Why is this?

Those devas, nāgas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, yakṣas, asuras, kumbhāṇḍas, devīs, rākṣasīs, and so forth, according to the lands and former dwelling places where they reside—from those devas and nāgas down to the devīs—they shall protect each of those respective lands and nurture all sentient beings.
"Therefore, you Asura kings who have not received a share should exercise forbearance and harbor no resentment.
These include the Asura King Rāhula, the Asura King Vemacitra, the Asura King Balada, the Asura King Śambara, and the Asura King Mucilinda."
The Asura King, the Asura King Sujiṭhila, the Asura King Vajravairocana, the Asura King Śilāruci, the Asura King Airāvaṇa, the Asura King Gomasapī, and the Asura King Vidyutkha.
The asura king Naya-cari, the asura king Gaṭamira, the asura king Cūladanta,
the asura king Asmala, the asura king Kāmardhi, the asura king Varakanda, and the asura king Pitamani...
Rāvaṇa, the Asura King Pārana-kha, the Asura King Sarvāṅga-kṣa, the Asura King Kṛṣṇabhuja,
and other such sixty thousand nayutas of Asura Kings who dwell in Jambudvīpa and do not receive their share,
should exercise forbearance and harbor no resentment; each [should act thus].
"Abiding in the primary palace, you shall protect, uphold, and nurture my True Dharma, and perform deeds that bring benefit to all sentient beings.
By these causes and conditions, you shall achieve both self-benefit and the benefit of others in this life and in future lives."

Why is this? Because those devas, nāgas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, yakṣas, asuras, kumbhāṇḍas, devīs, rākṣasīs, and others, according to the lands where they formerly dwelt—from those devas and nāgas down to the devīs—have established themselves to protect each of those respective lands and to nurture all sentient beings.
"Therefore, you great goddesses should exercise forbearance and harbor no resentment.

These are: the goddess Śāntā, the goddess Prabhākārī, the goddess Pṛthivīvidharaṇī, the goddess Vardhanī, the goddess Vimuktā, the goddess Vārivardhanī, the goddess Alpakleśā, and the goddess Viśuddhanetrā."
The goddesses are: Strī, Prajñapti, Ratnagarbhā, Maṇinakhī, Kālapāśī, Kālī, Rājamaulī, Jaladevī, Netradevī, Padmadevī, Udumbaradevī, Śaśidevī, and so forth.
The goddesses Pradīpānanī, Sumati, Durjayā, and Jayānanī—
these and sixty-two hundred thousand other great goddesses— resided in various stūpas and monasteries,
cities, towns, villages, gardens, groves, springs, ponds, riverbanks, and mountain valleys throughout Jambudvīpa.
Regarding those who dwell by the great ocean and are not entitled to a share:
"In whatever places you may reside, each of you shall protect and nurture my True Dharma therein.
In those places, [you must guard against] all fears, strife, enmity, famine, pestilence, hostile enemies from other regions, and unseasonable winds and rains."
May all cold, frost, poison, and heat be brought to rest; may the unwholesome, evil beings, their anger and coarseness, be warded off;
and may all things that are bitter, pungent, astringent, or tasteless be made to cease.
May my Dharma-eye abide long in the world, ensuring that the lineage of the Triple Gem is inherited and never severed, so that the three kinds of vital essence may increase and flourish.
Nevertheless, for the sake of the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all devas and humans, I shall diligently protect and uphold [this teaching].
By this cause and condition, you shall always obtain the benefit, welfare, and happiness of sentient beings in both this life and future lives.
Then those sixty-two hundred thousand goddesses addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Venerable Bhagavān! We shall protect, uphold, and nurture the Buddha-dharma;

we shall bring rest to strife and increase all three kinds of vital essence. Furthermore, regarding the World-Honored One’s śrāvaka disciples who act in accordance with the three karmas and possess no accumulation, we shall diligently provide protection, support, and nurturing for them.”
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent, you virtuous women!"
"You all should protect and uphold it in this manner.
The entire great assembly that had gathered likewise rejoiced and praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed all the devas, gandharvas, and even the great goddesses, saying:

"I now bestow upon you the Great Dharani-heart for Ceasing All Disputes. By means of this dharani-heart, each of you shall, within your respective realms, cause those whose planetary positions or lunar mansions have gone astray to gather all sentient beings and lead them to respectful faith, so that all strife and contention may entirely come to rest."
Having spoken these words, he then recited the mantra:

"Tadyathā | madana madana gomadana apamata ahe-mata madanakha acamatipara samati arivasa mamatini-khamati prasamati sucāraṇamati abhibhamati aravibhamati siddhāntamati kṣamamati svāhā. At that time, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, rose from his seat, joined his palms toward the Buddha, prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet, and spoke these words:
"O Bhagavat, Great Virtuous One!..."
I shall now further employ this great dhāraṇī to subdue all malevolent nāgas and evil spirits, to protect and sustain the land, and to ward off all wicked sentient beings.
Having spoken these words, he then uttered this mantra:
"Tadyathā | Dhanvaramūru mūru |"
Nāgamūla nāgamūla asuramūla.
Yakṣa-mūla, kumbhāṇḍa-mūla, pūtana-mūla, kaṭapūtana-mūla.
Ārya-bhamu-luhu-hu-ha-mulu-he-he-he-he-mucu-te-yakṣa-mulu-rā-bhaha-rā-bha.
*Rāva ha sarva-uṣa rāva ha svāhā.* At that time,

all the devas, nāga kings, kumbhāṇḍas, pretas, piśācas, pūtanas, and kaṭapūtanas who drink blood and eat flesh were all struck with alarm, grief, and fear; they joined their palms toward the Buddha, prostrated themselves at his feet, and spoke these words:
“We only pray that the World-Honored One will protect us with great compassion; how else shall we continue to survive?
The Buddha said, “Do not grieve.

Whatever flowers, fruits, the five grains, medicinal herbs, and various pure flavors upon the great earth have fallen to the ground before being eaten—such flowers, fruits, and the vital essence of these various flavors, you shall eat and thereby sufficiently sustain your lives.”
Furthermore, if there are people who prepare pure food and leave some scattered on the ground, you should also consume its essence to sustain yourselves.

Moreover, when my śrāvaka disciples who practice meditative concentration offer blessings through their own roots of goodness, you shall likewise obtain an abundance of physical strength, vitality, and essence, and your retinues and factions shall be endowed with full power.

If there are donors who bestow upon my disciples monasteries, gardens, fields, or dwellings, and they recite incantations and prayers while naming you, you should grant your consent, rejoice in it, and protect and nurture them; by virtue of this matter, your palaces shall increase and flourish.

If there is a donor who, when giving food, drink, clothing, bedding, or medicinal requisites to my disciples, recites names and offers prayers of blessing at the time of receiving them, you should likewise rejoice. Because of those prayers of blessing and your rejoicing, you shall obtain an increase in lifespan, an increase in physical appearance, an increase in well-being, an increase in followers, and an increase in power. Day and night, you should diligently protect, uphold, and nurture such donors as well as the recipients.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke these verses:
“The Great Dharma King among two-legged beings, Observing the assembly, spoke these words:
‘Śakra, you have questioned me; I shall grant each his respective portion.’”
Devas, nāgas, and kumbhāṇḍas, yakṣas, asuras, and rākṣasas;
throughout all the lands of Jambudvīpa, cities, towns, and all the villages;
in wildernesses and various groves of trees, on mountain crags, by wells, springs, and ponds.
May the Dharma-eye endure for a long time, and may all evils be brought to rest.
May there be abundance and all that is delightful; for the sake of Jambudvīpa, I entrust it to the devas and spirits of the four quarters to diligently protect and maintain.
"You have renounced your kinsmen, and I shall further distribute [the teaching].
Do not be angry or envious; grant your consent and rejoice.
The food is the joy of the Dharma and the flavor of dhyāna."
Thus all these hosts of devas arose together and spoke these words:
"For the sake of the True Dharma, we shall protect Jambudvīpa;
[we shall protect] those śrāvakas who maintain the precepts and do not engage in hoarding."
"Though they have shaved their heads but do not uphold the precepts, if you wish to cause the Eye of the Dharma to increase,
we shall all, with sincere hearts, diligently provide protection and nurture.
The Teacher addressed them, saying:
After my parinirvāṇa, for a full five hundred years, the True Dharma will remain firmly established in liberation.
For five hundred years it will consist of meditation and recitation; for five hundred years, the building of stūpas and temples.
Then, in the final five hundred years, it will persist firmly in contention.
Later, there may be those who have shaved their heads, who break the precepts and lack shame;
by making offerings to such as these, one likewise obtains immeasurable merit.
Just as gold is priceless, and even silver is a treasure compared to [base] gold.
Brass, counterfeit copper, and iron, white tin, lead, and pewter—if these were not considered treasures in the world, then tin and pewter would be the most supreme.
So too is the Jewel of the Buddha; most honored and uniquely foremost.
Next are the jewel-like pratyekabuddhas, arhats, and those who have realized the remaining fruits;

those who have attained meditative concentration and pure precepts, as well as the Sangha in name only who have broken the precepts—yet those who possess deep faith and seek liberation: if one can make offerings to them, [the merit is vast].
Not dwelling long in the stage of patience, one will surely and swiftly realize Bodhi.
The sons of the gods of the six heavens of desire, the various spirits of the precious lands,
the gandharvas dwelling in the forests, and the ten great nāgas of the ocean—
The ten great kumbhāṇḍas and the ten yakṣas with supernatural powers each dwell in their own palaces, protecting and upholding my true Dharma.
The hungry ghosts dwell in the wilderness, and the piśācas in empty rooms.
Pūrṇa dwells in the fields, and Kāṭhā resides among the graves;
thus each rejoices according to their own inclination, and they all maintain their respective domains.
Yet, while maintaining their domains improperly, they further diligently cause distress to others.
By means of these and others like them, I further transmit [this teaching] to other devas,
to the hosts of nāgas and yakṣas, to gandharvas and kiṃnaras,
to devīs and asuras, and to rākṣasas and kumbhāṇḍas.
Pervading all lands, he establishes, protects, and nurtures them:
In Kapilavastu and Vārāṇasī, In Magadha and Kośala, In Pañcāla and Aṅga, And in Soma and Aśvaka.
The country of Mathurā and the Caitya country, Vatsa and Śākya, Rāḍha and Ujjayinī, Roruka and Saurāṣṭra,
the country of Maṇicindhā, Gandhāra and Pāṭaliputra.
Paṇḍubhūti, Vaṇisītuṇa, Campāpupphinī, Pūrṣapura, Oṃcalikasali, and Kanakamaturā.
The kingdom of Parśu, the Pañcanagaras, the country of Śrīyāmā, Parvataśūlika,
the kingdoms of Kaśmīra and Bālī, and Khara-urasa.
The kingdom of Kāśyaka, Dāravatiṣa, Śrītiṣa and the kingdom of Kāśmīra, Bālūhiñjuka, Yutian and Shanshan, Kucha and Kiṇṇara.
In lands such as China and others, they shall protect and establish [the Dharma].
In all these countries, there are one million eight hundred thousand nāgas who have no share, and likewise yakṣas who have no share.
And eight *bimbara* [of wealth], which the asuras could not share;
sixty thousand *nayutas* of celestial maidens, whom the sixty-two hundred thousand [asuras] could not share.
I now bid you all farewell; each of you shall dwell in your own palace, protecting and upholding my True Dharma.
I shall bestow upon you divine mantras to ward off evil beings, to bring rest to all afflictions and harms, and to quell all strife and litigation.
During droughts and floods, illnesses, famines, and various bandits,
may the three vital essences increase, and all evils be brought to rest;
protecting and upholding my True Dharma, may the seeds of the Triple Gem flourish.
The śrāvaka bhikṣus, whose three karmas are always in accord, though they shave their heads, do not merely hold the precepts; they protect and uphold them all.
For the sake of these śrāvakas, they fully renounce all fields and houses.
"Food and drink, as well as medicinal decoctions—
whatever you may require— all such donors, you must protect and nurture.
*Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*, Scroll 55.
The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra, Scroll Fifty-Six, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Northern Qi Dynasty. Chapter Eighteen:
The Reception of the Constellations; Part Twelve of the Candragarbha-vibhāga: The Eighteenth Chapter, "The Reception of the Constellations."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Mahābrahmā, Lord of the Sahā World, Śakra Devendra, and the Four Heavenly Kings, saying:
"How did the celestial seers of the past arrange the various lunar mansions, planets, and constellations to protect the lands and nurture sentient beings?"
The Great Brahmā, Lord of the Sahā World, Śakra Devendra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and others addressed the Buddha, saying:

“In the past, celestial seers distributed and established the various lunar mansions, planets, and constellations to protect the lands and nourish sentient beings, each having specific jurisdictions within the four directions.”
"The seven lunar mansions of the eastern quarter are:
first, the mansion of Ārdrā (the Horn), which presides over birds;
second, the mansion of Punarvasu (the Neck), which presides over those who have left the household life to seek the Noble Path."
Third, the lunar mansion Jyeṣṭhā presides over aquatic beings;
fourth, the lunar mansion Mūla presides over those who travel by carriage to seek profit;
fifth, the lunar mansion Pūrvāṣāḍhā presides over women.
Sixth, the constellation Jyeṣṭhā presides over sentient beings dwelling on islands;
seventh, the constellation Mūla presides over potters.
"The seven constellations of the southern quarter are: [as follows]"
First, the lunar mansion Well (Kṛttikā) presides over goldsmiths;
second, the lunar mansion Ghost (Ārdrā) presides over all kings and great ministers;
third, the lunar mansion Willow (Anurādhā);...
First, the lunar mansion Xue Shan presides over dragons;
second, the mansion Xing Shu presides over those of great wealth;
third, the mansion Zhang presides over thieves.
Sixth, the constellation Wei (Wing) presides over nobles;
seventh, the constellation Zhen (Axle) presides over the kingdom of Sūlata.
"The seven constellations of the western quarter are: [as follows]"
First, the constellation Aśvinī presides over those who ply boats;
second, the constellation Bharaṇī presides over merchants;
third, the constellation Kṛttikā presides over the country of Bharukaccha.
Fourth, the lunar mansion Mṛgaśiras presides over water buffaloes;
fifth, the lunar mansion Ārdrā presides over all sentient beings;
sixth, the lunar mansion Punarvasu presides over the kingdom of Videha.
Seventh, the seven lunar mansions preside over the Kṣatriyas.
"The seven lunar mansions of the north:
first, the mansion Dou (Ursa Major) presides over the country of Vārāṇasī;..."
Second, the constellation Rohiṇī presides over the Kṣatriyas and the country of Andrabhūti;
third, the constellation Mṛgaśiras presides over the countries of Aṅga and Magadha;
fourth, the constellation Ārdrā presides over the country of Pañcāla.
Fifth, the constellation Ārdrā presides over those who wear flower crowns;
sixth, the constellation Punarvasu presides over the Gandhara and Shuluna kingdoms, as well as various dragons, snakes, and other crawling creatures;
seventh, the constellation Pushya presides over the gandharvas who are skilled in music.
“O Great Virtuous Blessed One!
In the past, the celestial seers arranged the various lunar mansions in the four directions in this manner to protect the lands and nurture sentient beings.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:
"Listen attentively!

Among all those in the world—gods, humans, and sages—I possess the most supreme knowledge and vision; I shall also cause the lunar mansions, planets, and constellations to protect the land and nurture all sentient beings."
"You all shall proclaim this so that they may know it: 'As I have divided the lands and sentient beings, each shall protect, sustain, and nourish them according to their respective portions.
The Great Brahma Kings and others addressed the Buddha, saying, "So be it, Bhagavān, Great Virtuous One!"
"Very well, we shall receive your instruction.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:

"I now entrust these twelve countries—the country of Yuma, the country of Dhāru, the country of Siciṇa, the country of Namada, the country of Dharada, the country of Khaśa, the country of Lakha, the country of Śama, the country of Hourava, the country of Śatuka, the country of Aja-pa, and the country of Muchapa—to the constellation Aśvinī (the Horn) for its protection, guardianship, and nurturing. You must also protect those who establish kingdoms, cities, towns, and villages on the day of the constellation Aśvinī, as well as all sentient beings born on that day. You should proclaim this so that they may know it."
The Brahma King and the others said:
"So it is, Great Virtuous Blessed One!
We shall indeed receive your instruction."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these ten kingdoms—the kingdom of Aruṇa, the kingdom of Harina, the kingdom of Śukara, the kingdom of Parula, the kingdom of Vṛjiśā, the kingdom of Narmada, the kingdom of Koṭisa, the kingdom of Sunāpa, the kingdom of Śama, and the kingdom of Bhadrapa—to the constellation Rohiṇī, charging it to protect and nurture them. To this, they replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these thirteen kingdoms—the kingdom of Khaśauka, the kingdom of Śindhubaṭī, the kingdom of Āmalī, the kingdom of Yonimukha, the kingdom of Nandapa, the kingdom of Kāśa, the kingdom of Vatsakuñja, the kingdom of Yūpaka, the kingdom of Vakharā, the kingdom of Śavarā, the kingdom of Kāruṇḍa, the kingdom of Kauñcaka, and the kingdom of Vañcalīpa—to the lunar mansion Mūla, charging it with their protection and nurturing. To this, they replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these eleven kingdoms—Pāṭhuma, Puṣkara, Mukta, Śaṅgamaka, Kīlika, Amāpava, Dakṣiṇakīlika, Cāpala, Sudarśana, Devana, and Khujaka—to the lunar mansion Rohiṇī to protect, guard, and nurture them. They replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these ten kingdoms—the kingdom of Ghura, the kingdom of Kurava, the kingdom of Murava, the kingdom of Aṅgapa, the kingdom of Sotita, the kingdom of Kujika, the kingdom of Devendra, the kingdom of Vināpa, the kingdom of Pasuta, and the kingdom of Khiga—to the Heart Constellation (Hṛdaya-nakṣatra) to protect, guard, and nurture. [The constellations] replied, 'So be it; we shall receive your instruction.'"
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these fourteen countries—the country of Gaja-vat, the country of Karava, the country of Kakapatha, the country of Siddhaksha, the country of Utsatarapa, the country of Devarana, the country of Aravi, the country of Nava, the country of Vrishakarava, the country of Madhura, the country of Kalimgavati, the country of Mayudali, the country of Pishanga, and the country of Parashirava—to the two lunar mansions of Wei (Ursa Major) and Ji (Ursa Minor) for their protection, guardianship, and nurturing. [The deities] replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:

"I now entrust these seventeen countries—Vatsa, Ujjayinī, Urubilvā, Śūrpāraka, Mathurā, Vaiśālipura, Cārakarpa, Prācya, Rāmagrama, Kāśivardhana, Kurujāṅgala, Daśārṇa, Rohitaka, Avanta, Tiṇapaṇṇa, Carmaṇvatī, and Vigaja—to the constellation Aśleṣā to protect, guard, and nurture them. To this, they replied, "So be it," and received the instruction.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:
"I now [entrust] those countries of Pāṭaliputra, Maṇilambhā, Varuṇa, Nañcara, Karna, Northern Pañcāla, and Devadaha..."
The country of Kośala, the country of Śrāvastī, the country of Campā, the country of Sūdanā, the country of Kurujāṅgala,
the country of Sindhū, the country of Pūrvaśaila, the country of Hūmiḍha, the country of Rāmāvatī,
the country of Kuru, the country of Himavat, the country of Jayapatha, and the country of Vākula.
The country of Kośala, the country of Gaṅgādvāra, the empire of Tumbavana, the empire of Caṇḍālavaṭa,
the country of Vārakaca, the country of Sunīkṣa, and the empire of Gośavarta—
these twenty-five countries are entrusted to the constellation Ārdrā for protection and nurturing; [the deities] replied, "So be it," and received the instruction.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these ten countries—the kingdom of Khasali, the kingdom of Mahānadi, the kingdom of Oḍra, the kingdom of Sunīkṣa, the kingdom of Prābhava, the kingdom of Aurava, the kingdom of Koṅkaṇa, the kingdom of Nikha, the kingdom of Kaṇṭhaprābhava, and the kingdom of Vajita—to the lunar mansion Ārdrā, charging it with their protection and nurturing. To this, they replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:

"I now entrust these twelve countries—Aviccha, Subhaṇa, Jaṭa, Suvarṇabhūmi, Madhura, Vimāśrī, Kambaloccha, Sūli, Bhagoccha, Bindulāva, Varuṇa, and Pañcāṅgala—to the constellations to protect, guard, and nourish them. They replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these fourteen countries—Pārsa, Harita, Cakkin, Amara, Bharava, Sumani-kī, Parayana, Samuccha, Śiriṣa, Bārī, Kātyūṣa, Māccha, Tukhāra, and Mathurī—to the two lunar mansions, Zhang (Aśvinī) and Yi (Bharaṇī), for their protection, guardianship, and nurturing. To this, they replied, "So be it," and received the instruction.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these twelve countries—the country of Kārapura, the country of Uraśā, the country of Kaśmīra, the country of Vajrī, the country of Tāndramālī, the country of Bharukaccha, the country of Daṇḍa, the country of Dhanaka, the country of Sumkhiśā, the country of Kulūcā, the country of Khārapura, and the country of Aśvaka—to the lunar mansion Aśvinī for its protection, guardianship, and nurturing. To this, they replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these twelve countries—the country of Kauśāmbī, the country of Kiṃnara, the country of Kapilamala, the country of Samosira, the country of Śrāvaṇī, the country of Śivali, the country of Viśāṇī, the country of Madrakānti, the country of Paṇḍalī, the country of Miṇḍalī, the country of Surabhi, and the country of Humatani—to the lunar mansion Aśvinī to protect, nurture, and sustain them. To this, they replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:

"I now entrust these thirteen countries—the country of Tiṭibha, the country of Sumāvara, the country of Tārapiṇī, the country of Aśvaja, the country of Kuśaloka, the country of Siddhuna, the country of Saramuñci, the country of Kiṃnarī, the country of Śivanirī, the country of Ravaśiṅgi, the country of Khaṭarivi, the country of Khaśali, and the country of White Horse—to the lunar mansion Revatī, charging it with their protection and nurturing. They replied, "We shall do so," and received the instruction.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these thirteen kingdoms—Asana-kyi, Gundhāravī, Anisi, Cakūpa, Tūgada, Pucchi, Citavisi-ta, Uśati, Bandhumatī, Virāḷika, Madhāravī, Kaṇapada, and Dabhasali—to the lunar mansion Rohiṇī, charging it to protect, guard, and nurture them. They replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these eighteen countries—Pāraṇḍala, Citraka, Varuṣa, Śūluna, Kapilavastu, Śaya, Aśvamukha, Gāruḍa, Kaurava, Oḍra, Java-bhadra, Vairūḍha, Gārhā, Yutina, Gappara, Śvāmukha, Nepāla, and Kunasa—to the lunar mansion Kṛttikā, charging it with their protection and nurturing. To this, they replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

“I now entrust these twenty-five countries—the kingdom of Magadha, Videha, Sāla, Vibhūka, Munisaya, Rāḷa, Yonaka, Kosala, Vatsa, Aṭa, Vehaka, Aṇava, Gayā, Nepāla, Bārāva, Vajji, Thūna, Śrīmaṇḍa, Meghapura, Maheśvaraniraya, Kaśmīra, Paruṣada, Śākala, Udyāna, and Sindh—to Piṣṭa, charging him with their protection and nurturing. To this, [Piṣṭa] replied, “So be it; I shall receive your instructions.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

“I now entrust these twenty-five countries—the Niṣāda country, Kāśī, Śākuni, Aṭamāśa, Kiṃnara, Māmava, Dābhika, Aṣṭaka, Sthūlakoṣṭhaka, Pāvika, Bāhudā, Mahārāṣṭra, Gandhāra, Kapāva, Pañcāla, Daśārṇa, Śūrpāraka, Māṣavatī, Taurava, Suma, Bāhu, Madramallika, Marāṭha, Kuru, and Gauḍa—to the lunar mansion *Mṛgaśiras* for its protection, guardianship, and nurturing. [The assembly replied: “So be it; we shall receive these instructions.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:

"I now entrust these seventeen countries—the country of Aśva, the country of Śabdana, the country of Mathurā, the country of Aṅgadhava, the country of Mātumanta, the country of Kuñjara, the country of Mañca, the country of Bhakuma, the country of Kuśava, the country of China, the country of Śūrasena, the country of Anamukha, the country of Kharavara, the country of Rimasā, the country of Naulovabhadra, the country of Mañcirava, and the country of Hicuka—to the constellation Aśvinī to protect, nurture, and sustain them. They replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instruction."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:

"I now entrust these ten countries—the kingdom of Siṃhakuṇḍala, the kingdom of Guṇasīsa, the kingdom of Kālaccha, the kingdom of Sālaccha, the kingdom of Dāraṇīpata, the kingdom of Samudraphala, the kingdom of Aruṣṇarāva, the kingdom of Nabhasiprabhāva, the kingdom of Manadūri, and the kingdom of Maitrābha—to the lunar mansion Aśvinī to protect, guard, and nurture them. To this, they replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instruction."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:
"I now entrust those two places—the Kṣatriya celestial shrines—to the constellation Rohiṇī to protect and nurture them. To this, they replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instruction."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:

"I now entrust these ten countries—Aruna, Kausasrajali, Campatunsi, Kucha, Malambusa, Sakya, Vadarata, Sati, Gosira, and Varami—to the Nakṣatra Revatī, charging her to protect and nurture them. They replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:

"I now entrust these seventeen kingdoms—the kingdom of Nandivardhana, the kingdom of Pārśva, the kingdom of Pūrṇabhadra, the kingdom of Urasā, the kingdom of Lambusa, the kingdom of Sahā, the kingdom of Madhuvana, the kingdom of Sthānī, the kingdom of Khasa, the kingdom of Sarastī, the kingdom of Siṃhala, the kingdom of Hapata, the kingdom of Harikūṭi, the kingdom of Upavīra, the kingdom of Dāruṇī, the kingdom of Vaiśālī, and the kingdom of Ugali—to the Nakṣatra Śravaṇā, to be protected, guarded, and nurtured. They replied, "So be it; we shall receive your instruction."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:

"I now entrust these nine kingdoms—the kingdom of Kācavī, the kingdom of Pārija, the kingdom of Nāgapuṣpa, the kingdom of Kautapā, the kingdom of Nandivardhana, the kingdom of Vālukā, the kingdom of Gandhakūṭa, the kingdom of Sāmili, and the kingdom of Yaṣṭakūla—to the Nakṣatra Āśleṣā, to be protected, guarded, and nurtured. [They replied: "So be it; we shall receive your instructions."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Kings and others, saying:

"I now entrust these fourteen countries—the kingdom of Humanta, the kingdom of Śumanta, the kingdom of Tūmaka, the kingdom of Cūmaka, the kingdom of Kāñcava, the kingdom of Kucī, the kingdom of Vākṣali, the kingdom of Takṣaśilā, the kingdom of Vāmivari, the kingdom of Bhadrabhadra, the kingdom of Ummaca, the kingdom of Vaśatamūlimā, the kingdom of Varukaccha, and the kingdom of Varabhadra—to the two lunar mansions, Śravaṇā and Dhanisthā. You shall protect, nourish, and sustain them, as well as the lands, cities, towns, and villages established on the days of these two mansions, and the sentient beings born on those days. You must proclaim this so that they may know it."
The Brahma King and the others said: "So it is,
O Great Virtuous Bhagavat!"
"Very well, we shall receive your instruction.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma King and the others, saying:
"As for what is called 'luminaries,' there are seven kinds:"
First, the sun; second, the moon;
third, the planet Mars.
Fourth is Jupiter; fifth is Saturn; sixth is Mercury.
Seventh is the planet Venus.
As for what are called "lunar mansions" (nakṣatras), there are twelve kinds:
the first is named Miśra;...
The second is named Vṛṣabha;
the third is named Mithuna;
the fourth is named Kakkaṭaka.
The fifth is named Śāha;
the sixth is named Kāñja;
the seventh is named Tūra.
Eighth, Vīryaka; ninth, Dhanivī; tenth, Māgara.
Eleventh is named Kumbhāṇḍa; twelfth is named Mina.
I now command these planets and lunar mansions to protect the kingdoms, cities, towns, and villages, and to nourish and raise all sentient beings; you must proclaim this so that they may know it.
The Brahma King and the others said: "So it is,
O Great Virtuous Bhagavat!"
"So be it; we shall receive your instruction.
At that time, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, Śakra Devendra, the Four World-Protecting Kings, and their retinues addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O Virtuous Bhagavān!..."

If there are disciples of the World-Honored One who do not keep slaves, livestock, gardens, fields, houses, or worldly requisites, and who do not associate with laypeople—except for the property of the Sangha from the four directions—they exert themselves with diligence, act in accordance with the three karmas, always maintain a sense of shame and remorse, dwell alone in quiet forests, and gather all wholesome dharmas.

At that time, I shall cause the lunar mansions, planets, and constellations to move correctly through the world, warding off the affliction and strife of evil beings; I shall cause the cessation of military conflict between two nations, disease, famine, unseasonable winds and rains, and untimely cold and heat. I shall protect the Buddha’s True Dharma so that it remains long and flourishes, ensuring that the lineage of the Triple Gem continues without interruption. I shall cause the three kinds of vital essence to increase and abide securely, and I shall cause the World-Honored One’s śrāvaka disciples to maintain purity in their actions of body, speech, and mind, to arouse great valor, and to dwell in accordance with the Dharma.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ājñātakauṇḍinya, saying:

"In order that my Dharma may endure for a long time and to bring sentient beings to maturity, I entrust all the kingdoms within Jambudvīpa—whether they be those with a single name, those with many names, those with identical names, or those whose names are not recorded—to the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and even the kāṭapūtanas, commanding them to provide protection and support;

furthermore, I entrust the lunar mansions, planets, and constellations to these various kingdoms, commanding them likewise to provide protection and support, so that the lineage of the Triple Gem shall never be severed."

In all countries there are many names that are identical; in those various lands, there are yakṣas with the same names and rākṣasas with the same names. In some countries where there are no spirits by name yet spirits dwell, entrust them to those [beings] to act as guardians. Furthermore, let those other spirits in Jambudvīpa whose names have not been listed also provide protection.

“Kauṇḍinya! All ghosts and spirits shall resolve to protect, sustain, and nourish them—indeed, they shall protect, sustain, and nourish them at all times—even my śrāvaka disciples who act in accordance with the three karmas, who never accumulate possessions, and who dwell in accordance with the Dharma.”

Kauṇḍinya! You all should constantly refrain from amassing possessions while dwelling in araṇya; with your three karmas in accord, you should turn your backs on saṃsāra, head toward nirvāṇa, and bring sentient beings to maturity—you should train yourselves in this way.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke in verse:
"For the sake of maturing sentient beings, I questioned the various heavenly kings:
'How did the celestial seers of old assign the lunar mansions and govern the various realms?'"
Brahmā replied to me, saying:
"In the past, the celestial seers and others established the various lunar mansions and planets to protect sentient beings who act in accordance with the Dharma.
Now they entrust this realm to you; you ought to nurture and sustain them."
I also entrust them to the spirits and deities, commanding them to provide protection,
as well as to the lunar mansions and planets, each of whom shall govern their respective realms;
for the sake of guarding, sustaining, and nurturing [beings], may they cause the Eye of the True Dharma to blaze brightly.
Protecting those who do not own fields or houses, the assembly of pure śrāvakas,
warding off all evil beings, and quelling all turbid evils;
ensuring that the seeds of the Triple Gem are never severed, and causing the three vital essences to increase.
"You shall inform the constellations and planetary deities, commanding them to provide protection.
I shall inform the śrāvakas, commanding them to abide in the Eye of the True Dharma;
they should abandon arrogance and dwell diligently in the araṇya."
"Turning one's back on birth and death, One proceeds toward nirvāṇa;
Delighting in dwelling within the realm of dhyāna, One brings billions of sentient beings to maturity.

Chapter 19: Establishing Stūpas and Monasteries The Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra, Moon Store Section, Part Twelve: Chapter Nineteen, "Establishing Stūpas and Monasteries" At that time, the Great Brahmā King, Lord of the Sahā World, Śakra Devendra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and their retinues rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Buddha, paid homage with single-minded devotion, and spoke these words:

“The Buddha has declared that within these four continents, all the great stupas established and maintained by the Tathāgatas, the Buddhas of the past, and the abodes relied upon by the sages of the Munis shall never be empty throughout the present and future ages.”
The Buddha, for the sake of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and others, brought down a great rain of Dharma that completely filled them all:

the first was named "Arisen by the Multitude of Sages," the second "Accumulation of Virtue," the third "Vajra Flame," the fourth "Fragrant Chamber," the fifth "Śāmbalī," the sixth "City of the Worthy," the seventh "Sukṣetra," and the eighth...
Water Light; next, named Fragrant Incense; next, named Well-Established;
next, named Cāpala; next, named Golden Lamp; next, named Joyful Reliance; next, named Mukhaliṇḍa; next, named Vajra Ground;
next, named Cave of Compassion; next, named Nārāyaṇa Cave; next, named Kūmasa.
First, Lohagandha; second, named Prajñāśekhara; third, named Mahāguṇakūṭa; fourth, named Bhadra;
fifth, named Nīlavarṇaprarūḍhakūṭa; sixth, named Gaganaputra; seventh, named Gośīrṣacandanagṛha; eighth, named Durjaya.
This is the great stūpa established and maintained by the Buddhas of the past, which is constantly protected by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and others, and which we always offer worship to.

"Bhagavān, regarding all the śrāvaka disciples of the Blessed One, how many stūpas, temples, and dwelling places will there be in the present and future worlds that we and our like shall protect, maintain, and nurture?"

At that time, the World-Honored One smiled with a serene countenance, and from his face he emitted various kinds of light that illuminated all directions. Immediately, within these four continents, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Buddhas appeared everywhere.

Eighty thousand Buddhas appeared in Pūrvavideha; one hundred thousand Buddhas appeared in Uttarakuru; fifty thousand Buddhas appeared in Aparagoyānī; one hundred thousand Buddhas appeared in the various islands and nations; and two hundred and fifty thousand Buddhas appeared throughout this Jambudvīpa.

Sixty Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Vārāṇasī; twenty Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Kapilavastu; thirty Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Magadha; twenty Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Aṅga-Magadha; fifty Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Kośala; twenty Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Sūrata; thirty Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Mahārāṣṭra; ten Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Gandhāra; twenty-six Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Aparāntaka; twenty-five Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Pañcāla; twelve Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Suma; ten Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Ayodhyā; and ten Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Mathurā.
Eighteen Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Vīra; fifty-six Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Vatsa;
forty-two Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Śayā; twenty-three Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Ujjayinī;
twenty-five Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Śūronapānta; thirty-eight Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Śūrona; [and] Maṇi...
Twenty-five Buddhas appeared in the country of Lamba; fifty-five Buddhas appeared in the country of Pāriyātra;
forty-eight Buddhas appeared in the country of Varuṇavati; twenty-nine Buddhas appeared in the country of Devana;
twenty-five Buddhas appeared in the country of Campā; and thirty-six Buddhas appeared in the country of Sthūṇā.
Seventy Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Sīdika; fifty Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Pūrusapura;
twenty-six Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Udyāna; twenty-two Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Kāśī; twenty-nine Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Suvarṇabhūmi;
forty Buddhas appeared in the kingdom of Mathurā; and [Buddhas appeared] in the kingdom of Śūlika.
Twenty-eight Buddhas appeared in the country of Pañcāla; fifty-eight Buddhas appeared in the country of Persia;
twenty Buddhas appeared in the country of Cīna; and thirty-two Buddhas appeared in the country of Śrīśa.
In the country of Vakula, fifty-eight Buddhas appeared; in the country of Kaśmīra, fifty-five Buddhas appeared;
in the country of Uraśā, twenty-five Buddhas appeared; in the country of Kharapaura, twelve Buddhas appeared;
in the country of Aśvaka, twenty-two Buddhas appeared; in the country of Darada, fifteen Buddhas appeared; in the country of Pā... [text truncated]
Twenty Buddhas appeared in the country of Luṇa; fifteen Buddhas appeared in the country of Vīraśa;
twenty-eight Buddhas appeared in the country of Kāśa; twenty Buddhas appeared in the country of Cakuka; forty-five Buddhas appeared in the country of Śrīti;
ninety-eight Buddhas appeared in the country of Kāśgar; and one hundred and eighty Buddhas appeared in the country of Yutian.
Manifestations: Ninety-nine Buddhas manifest in the kingdom of Kucha; twenty-four Buddhas manifest in the kingdom of Bharuka;
eighteen Buddhas manifest in the kingdom of Hicoka; eighty Buddhas manifest in the kingdom of Eṇi; twenty-nine Buddhas manifest in the kingdom of Shanxian;
eighty Buddhas manifest in the kingdom of Kiṃnara; and two [Buddhas] manifest in the kingdom of Zhendan.
One hundred and fifty-five Buddhas appeared in the country of Rāra; twenty-four Buddhas appeared in the country of Wu;
fifty Buddhas appeared in the country of Xintuobachi; and twenty-five Buddhas appeared in the country of [the land where] Śuddhodana [reigned].
The Buddha said: "O virtuous ones!

Buddhas such as these appear everywhere throughout the lands, cities, towns, villages, mountains, and forests of this four-continent world-system. Because I now empower them with my supernormal powers, there shall likewise be stūpas and monasteries of such numbers in each and every place. My śrāvakas—both those of the present and future—who are endowed with the three karmas, who correspond to the three types of bodhi, and who are learners (śaikṣa) or those beyond learning (aśaikṣa), fully possessing the precepts, great learning, and good conduct, shall deliver sentient beings from the ocean of the three realms of existence. Furthermore, the donors who have built stūpas and monasteries for my śrāvakas and provided them with all their necessities, along with their retinues, are entrusted to you. Do not allow wicked kings or unlawful disturbances to trouble them."

"Furthermore, do not allow others to be terrified by enemies from other regions, thieves, water, fire, humans, or non-humans; nor cause them to suffer from hunger and thirst. Because of such deprivation, they will be unable to engage in the three wholesome karmas, will fall away from their prohibitive precepts, and will suffer the decline of their virtuous companions."

At that time, there were also various Brahma kings, Śakra kings, Nāga kings, Yakṣa kings, Asura kings, and Kumbhāṇḍa kings, all together with their retinues, who joined their palms toward the Buddha and spoke these words:
"O Great Virtuous Bhagavān!"

Regarding all the stūpas and monasteries of the Tathāgatas and the hermitages currently occupied by the World-Honored One’s śrāvaka disciples, as well as those in future ages belonging to kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, or śūdras—whether householders or renunciants—who construct stūpas and monasteries for the sake of the World-Honored One’s śrāvaka disciples: wherever there are śrāvaka disciples who correspond with the three types of karma, who correspond with the three kinds of bodhi, and who dwell in the observance of precepts, extensive learning, and virtuous conduct, whether they be those in training (śaikṣa) or those beyond training (aśaikṣa), we shall all together protect them and cause them to be free from all calamities and fears.

"Regarding all stūpas, temples, and forest hermitages established by the Blessed One’s śrāvaka disciples, and whoever provides them with all necessities such as food, drink, clothing, bedding, and medicinal decoctions—we, too, shall protect, maintain, and support such donors."

Furthermore, if there are disciples of the World-Honored One who are destitute of the various requisites needed for day and night, and who suffer in poverty, I shall act as their great benefactor; receiving their entrustment, I will protect, nourish, and raise them, removing all their fears.
The Buddha then praised them, saying:

"All of you throughout the four continents should act in this manner. Just as you have now received my instructions and practice according to what has been taught, I entrust you and all your retinues to Maitreya."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke these verses:

Chapter 20: The Extinction of the Dharma The Great Collection Sūtra, Part Twelve: The Moon Treasury Section, Chapter Twenty: The Extinction of the Dharma At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Candragarbha rose again from his seat, adjusted his robes so as to bare his right shoulder, and with palms joined toward the assembly of all the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas gathered from the ten directions, he looked upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Candrapradīpa with a smile on his face and eyes, and spoke these verses:

May all evils, famines, and pestilences be stilled; may untimely winds, heat, and rains likewise cease.

out of compassion for all sentient beings, Commands that the Buddha’s True Dharma be protected and upheld.
At that time, having heard these verses spoken by the Bodhisattva Candragarbha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Candrapradīpa spoke further in verse:

“Excellent, excellent!

The wicked bhikṣus of various monasteries Secretly speak of the holy life and its manifold unwholesome matters; For this reason, the kṣatriyas become enraged.

for vaiśyas and brahmins, it brings them joy and profit in the same way.

Kṣatriyas and brahmins who harbor resentment toward those who uphold the precepts—

or if one gives slaves, fields, and houses to others and causes them to take possession of these things; [one incurs grave transgression].
Unvirtuous bhikṣus shall regard such as their elders;

When the kṣatriya hears this, he gives rise to anger;

full of fraud and falsehood, will swiftly cause his own realm to perish;
his crops will not ripen, and he will suffer from both drought and floods.
The *śvāvidh* mouse and the fierce elephant are violent; military forces arise from both one’s own and foreign lands.
The planets enter non-ordinary constellations, the great earth trembles everywhere, and white rainbows and ominous stars fall.

You all may dwell at ease in this land, according to your own wishes.

"You shall thus become offerings to all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time;
you will swiftly realize the fruit of Bodhi and act as guides in pure lands.
